DOCUMENT RECORD DETAILS  EK.10.71.001 CABIN CREW MANUAL Rev.03  0.Management and Control  0.1.Foreword  Within the scope of the duties and responsibilities of the cabin crew members, EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual has been prepared in compliance with the terms and conditions of Turkish Airlines Air Operator Certificate (AOC), national and international legislation (Turkish DGCA, IATA, ICAO, EASA, etc.),   EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part-A , and the Company's policies, standards and regulations, and cannot contradict with this document and the requirements. EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual is revised within the framework of the revisions made in the national and international legislation to which the Company is subject, in parallel with  EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part-A. Within the scope of   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS | Instruction On The Procedures And Principles For Air Operations ORO.GEN.120 Means of Compliance   and   DK.33.001   EASA | Air   Operations   RegulationsORO.GEN.120,   the   principles   and   requirements   relating   to   the Alternative Means of Compliance (AltMOC) that can be used by the Company as an alternative to the Acceptable Means of Compliance (AMC) issued by EASA are described in   DK.22.155 UOD-2018/4 Alternative Compliance Methods (Altmoc). EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual has been drawn up with the purpose of defining the management, systems, processes, resources, procedures, as well as the duties and the responsibilities of the concerned employee; all of which have been established and defined in order to ensure safe and secure cabin operation. All reference documents used as sources are accessible through the   Digital Document  Management System (DDMS) of Turkish Airlines. This document is sent to the approval of R.O.T. Ministry of Transportation and Infrastructure / Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) following the review of Quality Assurance Directorate and approval of the Accountable CEO. The document shall come into effect on the "Effective Date" to be specified under announcement of issuance of the document, following the approval of Turkish DGCA. All Cabin Crew Members serving in the Company shall be responsible for the contents of EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, and the regulations specified therein must be followed through work flow. EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual is prepared and issued in Turkish and English. The cabin crews have full knowledge of the contents of EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual and apply the contents of the operation manual within the scope of their duties and responsibilities. The cabin crews are required to be aware that they are required to comply with the laws, regulations, standards, procedures of the countries where the flight operation is performed. Any employee, who does not act in compliance with such rules and regulations, or neglects doing so, shall be subjected to disciplinary actions, penal procedures or legal actions. EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual is the proprietary property of Turkish Airlines, and may not be quoted and/or reproduced without the prior consent of Turkish Airlines. Any of the pages of this document may not be copied, photocopied or otherwise used by any means, methods or techniques, without obtaining the prior consent of the beneficial owner thereof. === Sayfa 4 ===
The information on the emergency system and emergency application differences special to aircraft type variants is available in  EK.10.71.003 Cabin Crew Aircraft Types Manual and also a part of EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual together with the Quick  Reference Handlist (QRH).  0.2.Administration and Control of the Manual  Cabin Crew Directorate is responsible for performing and issuing any revisions and corrections in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual as well as updating the information therein as per   PR.10.18.036 Procedure for Management of External Documentation and External  Requirements and following up the implementation of such information; and cabin crew members is responsible for reading the up-to- date copy of the document and implementing during cabin operation processes within the scope of their task responsibilities. Nothing can be written on EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, nor can any word in the text of the manual be underlined, any addition and/or correction be made. It is essential that EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual is prepared in a format that is understandable for all employees taking part in the operation, easy to understand, legible, applicable, guiding, and in compliance with the Company's documentation structure, and that the Manual is easily accessible in the cabin crews’ activity areas, in accordance with   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operations Regulations ORO.MLR.100 and   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS | Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air Operations ANNEX-3 Organizational Requirements for Flight Operations (Section - ORO). Since the ordinary and temporary revisions are made on the entire manual, not on the basis of pages, there is no separate Applicable Pages List. The up-to-date copies of EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual are loaded as one English copy to the narrow- and wide-body aircraft in the Company's fleet. It is checked by the Cabin Crew Members every time they receive the aircraft for the first time, and if it is found to   be   missing,   it   is   completed   through   the   agency   of   Cabin   Crew   Directorate/Assistant   Directorate   (Operation   and Compliance)/Cabin Operations Management/Cabin Operations Tracking Supervisory. The principles regarding the distribution and up-to-dateness of EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual on aircraft are defined in   PR.71.090 Procedure for Management of Internal  Documents in Cabin Operations. The up-to-date revision of EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual shall be published electronically through the   Digital Document  Management System (DDMS) and made available to all Cabin Crew Members only in “read only” format through their Company user names and passwords. Besides, the Manual can also be viewed by the Cabin Crew Members through the “Documents Mobile/Web Applications”, and the read receipt can be recorded. That the Cabin Crew Members read the documents over the CRESS Documents means that “I have read and understood the document”. The bulletins that include the revisions to EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual and its approved version are published in the   Digital Document Management System (DDMS) and announced to the cabin crew through DDMS and/or mobile applications. The current revision of EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual is also made accessible through the tablet PCs distributed to Cabin Chiefs by Cabin Crew Directorate. The users are required to report the detected non-compliances/irregularities or the issues prescribed to be added in implementation and/or interpretation of the provisions of EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, or in case of contradiction of this Manual with a hierarchically higher document, to the e-mail address   kabinkaldoksf@thy.com. All departments and employees are required to submit their written proposals of revisions to update EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual in line with the national and international regulations as well as Company documents to Cabin Crew Directorate or the e-mail address  kabinkaldoksf@thy.com. EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual is prepared in accordance with   PR.10.18.039 Procedure for Management of Corporate Documents and   TL.18.006   Instruction   on   Preparation   of   Document.   Ordinary   and   temporary   revisions   are   made   in   accordance   with   the requirements in   DK.22.154 UOD-2018/3 Manual Review And Approval Processes, within the framework of PR.10.18.039 Procedure for  Management of Corporate Documents,   TL.18.006 Instruction on Preparation of Document, and   PR.71.090 Procedure for Management  of Internal Documents in Cabin Operations. Following the completion of the Company’s internal approval process, EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual is submitted to the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (Turkish DGCA) pursuant to the requirements of   DK.22.154 UOD-2018/3 Manual Review And Approval Processes.   Each   issued   ordinary   revision/temporary   revision   shall   cancel   and   supersede   the   relevant   previous   ordinary revision/temporary revision. Any details related to the revisions are available on the revision tables in Chapter 0. It is described in  TL.18.006 Instruction on Preparation of Document how to indicate the revision in the document so that each revision made to keep the document up-to-date can be understood. Any revision made to EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual through ordinary revision is included in 0.7. Details of Current Revision. Cabin Crew Directorate/Assistant Directorate (Operation and Compliance)/Quality and Document Management Supervisory is liable to archive a copy each of all revisions of EK.10.71.001 Cabin Product and Service Manual in accordance with all requirements specified in PR.01.30.007 Archive Procedure.  0.3.Purpose and Scope  EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual covers the processes related to the cabin services, cabin operation, and the cabin crews in all flight operations Turkish Airlines performs in the national and international airspaces. MoCA (Mobile Cabin Assistant):   The name of the application used by Cabin Chiefs to use the functions, which are defined within the scope of the DCMS project, on the tablet PC. Quick   Reference   Handlist   (QRH):   It   is   document   that   is   prepared   so   that   the   cabin   crews   can   manage   the   potential emergencies/extraordinary situations possible to occur during the flight operation correctly and rapidly, and includes the emergency procedures/applications and the announcements that may be needed. Accompanied Minor:   The minor passenger accompanied by a cabin crew member as their parent or legal representative is not on the flight.  Accompanying Cabin Crew Member:   A cabin crew member assigned to accompany a minor passenger who has no parent or legal representative on the flight to the final destination airport.  0.9.2.Abbreviations  A ABP:   Able-Bodied Passenger  ACARS:   Aircraft Communications Addressing and Reporting System  AMC:   Acceptable Means of Compliance  AML:   Aircraft Maintenance Log  ASP:   Attendant Switch Panel  ASR:   Air Safety Report  ASSC:   Aircraft Security Search  ASSCL:   Aircraft Security Search List  AQD:   Aviation Quality Database  B B/C:   Business Class  BCF:   Bromo-Chloro-Difluoro-Methane  BTP:   Bromo Trifluoropropene  C CA:   Cabin Attendant (Cabin Crew Member)  CAA:   Civil Aviation Administration  CBBG:   Cabin Seat Baggage  CC:   Cabin Chief  CCL:   Requirement for Contact Lenses  CFR:   Confidential e-Report E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 51 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250

In cases where there is no written delegation of the Senior Vice President, Cabin Crew or s/he cannot be reached, the power is delegated to the respective post holders pursuant to the requirements specified in   EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part-A Section 1.2 Names of Managers, Nominated Persons and Their Deputies and   LS.10.32.001 Acting List. Powers of Managers of Cabin Crew Directorate are delegated to any other manager deemed eligible by the Senior Vice President (SVP), Cabin Crew, or to the employee serving as the supervisor of her/his own management in accordance with the same regulations (due to temporary reasons such as illness and secondment). Duties, Authorizations and Responsibilities of Cabin Chief  Cabin Crew Directorate Cabin Chief job descriptions have been quoted from   TK Portal/Corporate Applications/Job Descriptions heading. They are detailed in the requirements specified in   EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part-A, Section 1.5.3 Cabin Chief.  Job Description  Within the scope of the national and international legislations and the Company rules and regulations; it is to carry out, monitor and report the cabin operation to ensure the cabin safety, security, service quality, and passenger satisfaction while performing the flight operation process on board the aircraft types which s/he is assigned to within the framework of their duties and responsibilities, and establish the necessary coordination.  Authority, Duties and Responsibilities  1. S/he is accountable to the Commander for ensuring that safety and security are maintained inside the cabin during flight operations, that the instructions and standards defined in the operation manuals regarding safety and security are achieved by the Cabin Crew Members, and for establishing the necessary coordination. 2. S/he is responsible for changing the standard of and/or terminating any cabin activity (offering of catering items/products, etc.) that is irrelevant to safety and security in terms of flight safety and security if and when necessary. 3. S/he ensures coordination of pre-flight crew briefing, conducts cabin briefing and post-flight debriefing. 4. S/he actively follows current documents, announcements regarding Company regulations and the Intranet and e-mail messages of the Company for all briefings and implements these. 5. S/he ensures and checks that pre-flight preparations are fulfilled completely and timely in accordance with the controlled documents; and reports any irregularities detected as per the relevant legislation. 6. S/he carries out and monitors the catering/product service as per the standards throughout the flight in accordance with the policies and objectives of the Company, ensures that the service is given within the framework of the flight duties and responsibilities to ensure the service quality, customer satisfaction/loyalty, and reports any detected irregularities. Duties, Authorizations and Responsibilities of Cabin Chief (Purser)  Job Description  Within the scope of the national and international legislations and the Company rules and regulations; it is to carry out, monitor and report the cabin operation to ensure the cabin safety, security, service quality, and passenger satisfaction while performing the flight operation process on board the wide body aircraft type(s) which s/he is assigned to within the framework of their duties and responsibilities, and establish the necessary coordination.  Authority, Duties and Responsibilities  1. On board the wide body aircraft type(s) which s/he is assigned to, s/he is accountable to the Commander for ensuring that safety and security are maintained inside the cabin during flight operations, that the instructions and standards defined in the operation manuals regarding safety and security are achieved by the Cabin Crew Members, and for establishing the necessary coordination. 2. S/he is responsible for changing the standard of and/or terminating any cabin activity (offering of catering items/products, etc.) that is irrelevant to safety and security in terms of flight safety and security if and when necessary. 3. S/he establishes the coordination of pre-flight crew briefing; conducts cabin briefing and post-flight debriefing, and receives the section chiefs’ (the Cabin Chiefs who are in charge of the section in the BC/Business Class and YC/Economy classes) confirmations that the section briefings have been done. 4. S/he actively follows current documents, announcements regarding Company regulations and the Intranet and e-mail messages of the Company for all briefings and implements these. 5. S/he ensures that the pre-flight cabin preparations are fulfilled completely and timely in accordance with the controlled documents, receives the section Cabin Chiefs’ confirmations that the necessary checks have been made and checks them, and reports any irregularities detected as per the relevant legislation. 6. S/he carries out and monitors the catering/product service as per the standards throughout the flight in accordance with the policies and objectives of the Company, ensures that the service is given within the framework of the flight duties and responsibilities to ensure the service quality, customer satisfaction/loyalty, receives the relevant section Cabin Chiefs’ feedback on the service offering, and reports any detected irregularities. 7. S/he fulfills the requirements prescribed for ordinary, extra-ordinary and emergency cases in accordance with the relevant legislation and the defined regulations by possessing the knowledge regarding technical and emergency equipment of the wide body aircraft type(s) for which s/he has been certified. 8. S/he submits hazards/threats, risks, near-misses, abnormal situations and emergencies, incidents/accidents and irregularities which may occur during the flight operation as well as verbal/written passenger feedback through the system in accordance with the legal regulations. 9. S/he is responsible for performing, checking the duties defined within the framework of the Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) legislation and the Company’s rules and regulations, and receiving the relevant section chiefs’ confirmations that the same has been checked, and for reporting the Occupational Health and Safety issues. 10. 1.8.1. Time of Assuming Duties Apart from Flight Duties  In planning duties for Cabin Crew Member outside of flight duties; the beginning and ending times of the relevant duty shall be communicated by the concerned Management and/or Directorate through the means of communication described in PR.71.084 Cabin  Communication and Activity Management Procedure. Planning of the office/training duties of the Cabin Crew Members are included in the flight duty period and applied by taking into account the flight/working and resting hours described under   EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part-A, Chapter 7. Flight Time Limitations. Each Cabin Crew Member who does not participate in any duty (flight, standby, training, etc.) in the operation without any excuse has to give feedback. The entire information on this subject is given in   PR.71.044 Procedure For Cabin Crew Members Attendance Monitoring .  1.8.2. Transfer of Cabin Crew Members to and back from Duties  Transfer of Cabin Crew Members to and back from Duties at the Main Base:   The Company ensures the transfers of flight crew employees to and back from duty in accordance with the requirements specified in   PR.01.70.011 Procedure for Ground Transportation of Aircrew , Section 6.   Implementation.  Outside the Main Base;   crew members use the vehicles provided and paid for by the Company while transferring to and back from their duties.  1.8.3. Conduct of Crew Members Out of the Main Base or during Stay-Over Duties 1.8.3.1. Accommodation of Crew Members Out of the Main Base  Out of the main base, the crews on stay-over duties accommodate at the Appropriate Accommodation Facility (hotels) wherein the Company has booked rooms as per the requirements specified in   PR.01.70.012 Procedure for Meal, Accommodation and Travel  Allowances of AirCrew on Flight Duties Section 6. Implementation. Any Cabin Crew Member who does not prefer to stay at the hotel, place or residence selected for crew accommodation or wishes to leave the accommodation for some time during stay-over duty must inform the Commander through the Cabin Chief or, in case of absence of Flight Crew Members, the Cabin Chief, and obtain permission by providing where and how s/he can readily be found. The hotel cannot be left without permission. The station official/manager informs the Commander (the Co-Pilot when necessary), or the Cabin Chief in the stay-over duties without Flight Crew Members, of the changes made in the flight program. However, the person leaving the crew keeps track of the changes in flight schedule. Person leaving the crew is responsible for the consequences of being unavailable for contact.  1.8.3.2. Points to be Taken into Consideration at Hotels  The crew members who stay in a hotel communicate the complaints about the hotel to Cabin Crew Directorate/Assistant Directorate (Operation and Compliance)/Cabin Support Management instead of the hotel employee by e-form or the “Hotel Feedback” form on AQD Portal. The crew members shall act coordinately from the beginning to the end of duty. Cabin Crew Members who have obtained permission from Commander or, when Flight Crew Members are not available on stay- over duties, from Cabin Chief, shall inform the Cabin Chief while leaving the hotel. Telephone number and full address of the place to be visited shall be provided. Crew members shall remain within the boundaries of the city. The principles described in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Chapter 10. Security are implemented in relation to security of the Personnel Identity Cards and personal belongings of the Cabin Crew Members throughout any stay-over duties. The information on the stay-over representation rules is available in the requirements specified in EK.10.71.007 Cabin Crew Uniform  Use and Representation Manual, Section 7. Stay-Over Representation Rules. The information on the international stay-over airports and hotels (such as security measures, contagious diseases and customs procedures) is available in the   Station Information System (SIS). The information on the domestic stay-over airports are given to the Cabin Crew Member by Cabin Crew Directorate by using the means and methods of communications (such as e-mail, SMS, announcement) defined in PR.71.084 Cabin Communication and  Activity Management Procedure. Information on the domestic stay-over airports is available in the   Station Information System (SIS). The irregularities detected by the cabin crew in relation to health, contagious disease and hygiene requirements are reported to  saglik@thy.com. The cabin crews never make any comment or evaluation on the hotel used for accommodation on the social media channels or hotel evaluation platforms. Smoking is not allowed in the facilities and hotel rooms, where smoking is prohibited.  1.8.4. Smoking on Board  Cabin crew members and passengers are prohibited from smoking (electronic cigarette included) on board in accordance with the national and international rules and the standards of the Company in line with the requirements specified in   DK.33.001 EASA |Air  Operations Regulations CAT.OP.MPA.240,   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS | Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Flight Operations ANNEX-4 Commercial Air Transportation (Chapter-CAT). In accordance with the international legislations, it is forbidden to charge electronic cigarettes on board aircraft. In accordance with the Company regulations, in any domestic and international round flights, cabin crew members are prohibited from smoking during waiting periods despite the existence of special areas allocated for smoking in the boarding bridge or terminal buildings of intermediate airports. No request shall be made to the flight crew and/or station employee in this regard. With regard to the article released by Directorate General of Pharmaceuticals and Pharmacy of the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Turkey on electronic cigarettes; passengers and crew members are prohibited from consuming on board the electronic cigarettes, considered under the scope of the limitations and prohibitions as per all requirements specified in   DK.21.064 Ministry of Health Law No. 4207 On The Prevention and Control of Harms of Tobacco Products. When the use and/or charging of electronic cigarette is detected the necessary warnings must be made, and the case must be monitored by the cabin crew throughout the flight.  1.8.5. Regulations on Passports, Customs, Currencies and Mails  All crew members must act in conformity with the regulations imposed by the relevant states in relation to any matters regarding passports, customs, exchange and mails. These regulations are communicated to the Cabin Crew Members through the Station  Information System (SIS) and announcements. The Cabin Crew Members are responsible for obtaining and practicing the required information in relation to such regulations prior to the flight.  1.8.5.1. Regulations on Passports and Visas  All Turkish citizens and foreign passengers shall produce their passports or a valid document substituting for passport to the law enforcement agencies of entry-exit gates on duty in order to be able to enter and exit the national boundaries of Turkey. Entry-exit processes have to be finalized by the law enforcement agencies in order to perform customs procedures and other processes. Passport checks during entry-exit procedures shall be carried out duly and in person. In accordance with   PR.71.024 Procedure for Tracking  Expiry Dates and Renewal of Passports and The USA Crew Member Visas of Cabin Crew Members , Cabin Crews shall carry their valid passports in all international line flights (including round trips) and shall not perform international line flights without passport. The Cabin Crew Member monitors and makes declaration for passport and visa validity/currency as per the principles of PR.71.024  Procedure for Tracking Expiry Dates and Renewal of Passports and The USA Crew Member Visas of Cabin Crew Members.  1.8.5.2. Regulations on Customs  Since the flight and Cabin Crew Members assigned to the flights to be performed from Istanbul Airport (IST) will carry out all the necessary exit transactions on the exit day and the entry transactions at the end of the duty, if they fly from abroad and continue to fly abroad the same day, they do not have to make entry-exit transactions, provided that they pass from the aircraft on which they have come to the aircraft on which they will go without entering the landside. Gold, narcotics (drugs or stimulants), forbidden medications, fire arms are principal smuggling issues. Smuggling, carrying goods related to smuggling or stolen goods from one location to another or intentionally letting these happen in any aircraft of Turkish Airlines, hiding those goods in a place owned by Turkish Airlines or helping their concealment are indictable offenses for the Company employee. The employee, clearly detected by judicial bodies to have been involved in a smuggling case, shall be discharged from the Company. Any arrangements in relation to customs regulations at the outstations entered shall be communicated to Cabin Crew Member by means of the   Station Information System (SIS) and announcements. The Cabin Crew Member obtains and implements the required information in relation to such regulations prior to the flight. The lines on which the General Declaration (GEN-DEC) and the Airline Declaration Form (ANNEX/10- E) are to be used as per the demands of the countries' customs authorities are informed to cabin crews through announcement or SIS Line Information form.  1.8.5.3. Regulations on Exchange  Currency exchange transactions in countries entered shall be performed in accordance with the applicable foreign exchange laws of such countries. Exchange regulations of outstations are communicated to the cabin crew through the   Station Information System (SIS), E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 67 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250

Operational Control and Monitoring  2.1. Administration of the Operation by the Company  The Company is required to plan, perform, and monitor the administration of the flight operation on the basis of flight safety and security under the scope of the national and international legislations and the operational regulations approved by Turkish DGCA in accordance with the requirements specified in   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operations Regulations ORO.GEN.110,   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS | Instruction on  the   Procedures   and   Principles   for Air   Operations ANNEX-3   Organizational   Requirements   for Air   Operations   (Chapter   -   ORO). Accordingly, detailed information regarding the methods for controlling and monitoring in respect of administration of the flight operation in parallel with the standards of the Company is available in the requirements specified in   EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part-A,  Chapter 2. Operational Control and Supervision.  2.1.1. Validity of Cabin Crew Aircraft Type-Variant Qualification(s)  For the Cabin Crew Members who have completed the training given as per the requirements specified in EK.10.72.006 Cabin Crew  Training Manual , Sections 3.4. Aircraft Type Specific and Operator Conversion/Differences Training, 3.9. Requalification Training, and 3.10. Recurrent Training and the evaluations of the relevant training program successfully,   FR.72.3000 Cabin Crew Aircraft Type/Variant  Qualification(s) that includes the aircraft types/variants which they will be assigned to and the current validity periods is issued by Flight Training Directorate/Cabin Training Management digitally in accordance with the requirements specified in   DK.33.001 EASA |Air  Operations Regulations GM1 ORO.CC.215(b)(2). After the relevant trainings, Flight Training Directorate/Cabin Training Management sends the certificate holder an e-mail so that they check the currency of their certificate. The certificate holder is required to check the currency of their certificate from Turkish Airlines Cress/Check In corporate mobile application. In the event that the relevant certificate holder detects any mistake/missing on their certificate, they are required to ensure that their certificate is reviewed and any necessary actions are taken by sending feedback to  KABINEGITIMSERTIFIKATAKIP@THY.COM. All Cabin Crew Members keep their   FR.72.3000 Cabin Crew Aircraft Type/Variant Qualification(s) accessible digitally or in hard copy throughout the flight as defined in the requirements in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 1.9. Documents and Papers Mandatory to be carried by Cabin Crew Members and follow the validity periods of their certificates. Before the flight operation, the Cabin Chief   of the aircraft checks the currency of their and all the assigned Cabin Crew Members’  FR.72.3000 Cabin Crew Aircraft Type/Variant Qualification(s)on Turkish Airlines Cress/Check-In corporate mobile application. If there is any error/omission in the certificates, the Cabin Crew Member holding such certificate is withdrawn from the flight and sent to take the necessary actions. One Cabin Crew Member may be assigned to maximum three (3) aircraft types as per the requirements specified in   DK.33.001 EASA |  Air Operations Regulations ORO.CC.250,   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS | Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air Operations ORO.CC.250. However, with the approval of Turkish DGCA, the cabin crew member may be assigned to operate on four (4) aircraft types if for at least two (2) of the types: Safety and emergency equipment and type-specific normal and emergency procedures are similar. Non-type-specific normal and emergency procedures are identical. In the event that the variants of an aircraft type are not similar in the following aspects, they are regarded as different types: Emergency exit operation, Location and type of portable safety and emergency equipment, Type-specific emergency procedures. Detailed explanations of the above items are available in the requirements in   EK.10.72.006 Cabin Crew Training Manual Section 3.4.2. Determination of Aircraft Type and Variants. Pursuant to these principles, the cabin crews may be certified for no more than three (3) aircraft types within the scope of the aircraft types/variants available in the Company's fleet. Evaluation of Competence and Performance of the Cabin Crew  In line with the standards in relation to flight safety, security and service quality, competence and performance of the cabin crews are evaluated to see that they have the competencies required for the duties they are assigned to, their strengths and improvement opportunities. The Cabin Chiefs complete all forms assigned to them through the Flight-based Evaluation System (FES). All program and system requirements are available in   EK.10.71.006 Flight-Based  Evaluation System Manual and   PR.10.71.001 Procedure For Implementation Of Cabin Crew Flight Based Evaluation System.  2.1.2.2. Cabin Crew Control and Evaluation Activities  In order to verify the Cabin Crew Members’ competencies while performing their duties to ensure safety and security in case of any ordinary situations/emergencies, control activities and practices are carried out as per   PR.72.317 Procedure for Principles of Check  Flight Implementation. SAFA/SANA/SACA  SAFA (Safety Assessment of Foreign Aircraft) is evaluation of the foreign-registered aircraft from the point of view of safety. These are the safety-oriented inspections conducted by the civil aviation authorities of foreign countries on Turkey-registered aircraft while they are parked. The purpose of SAFA is to check the cockpit, cabin and documents inside the aircraft and all exterior surfaces and cargo compartments outside the aircraft before and after the flight; and to determine and solve any matters which may affect flight safety adversely. A standard and international inspection performed on the aircraft and crew in accordance with all requirements specified in DK.33.003  EASA - RIM Appendix 1 | Inspection Instructions and Pre-Described Findings in order to check whether international aviation regulations regarding flight safety are implemented. It is a multidimensional inspection checking the critical points related to the technical and maintenance operation, flight operation, ground operation, and cargo operation. SANA (Safety Assessment of National Aircraft) is the inspection of the national aircrafts by Turkish DGCA from technical, safety and operational aspects. SACA (Safety Assessment of Company Aircraft) is the ramp inspection the operators conduct on their own aircraft in accordance with all requirements in   DK.33.003 EASA - RIM Appendix 1 | Inspection Instructions and Pre-Described Findings. The standard implementation methods in relation to the SAFA inspections are available in   PR.10.18.029 SACA Ramp Inspections Procedure. The inspections are conducted by the auditors and quality inspectors assigned by the Senior Vice President, Quality Assurance in accordance with the requirements specified in   DK.33.003 EASA - RIM Appendix 1 | Inspection Instructions and Pre-Described Findings. The employee performing the SACA inspection is authorized and entitled to monitor the operation and access any information by being present on board and around the aircraft throughout the entire operation. It is no problem that they are present in the cabin during the ASSCL implementation. The purpose, scope, regulations and operation of the SAFA/SANA/SACA inspections are identical. In all inspections, it is important to help the employee assigned to such inspections in carrying out their duties.  2.2.5.2. Legal Basis of SAFA  The SAFA inspections are conducted by evaluating the following topics as per the International Chicago Convention ICAO Annexes. Categorization and Enforcement of SAFA/SANA/SACA Findings  SAFA findings are subject to a standard categorization reviewed annually. Each finding must be included into a category.  Category 1 (CAT 1): Findings slightly affecting safety (slight) Category 2 (CAT 2): Findings effecting safety noticeably (significant) Category 3 (CAT 3): Findings significantly threatening safety (very significant)  In the event that the non-conformity is not eliminated in respect of the findings included in Category 1 and Category 2 before the flight, then the inspector shall inform the Commander of the matter, and shall ensure that such matter is recorded. Since Category 3 findings are considered as non-conformities threatening flight and passenger safety, the inspector shall inform the Commander that these non-conformities have to be eliminated before the flight. Accordingly, inspectors may request any technical irregularities to be eliminated, any missing materials to be completed (e.g., life vest), or any necessary documents (e.g., licenses of flight crew, necessary chapter of the manuals, security cards, etc.) to be provided. In case of failure in eliminating the findings, any operational sanctions such as grounding/decreasing the number of passengers may be imposed. 2.2.5.5. Monitoring of SAFA Activities  The authority conducting SAFA inspection and Turkish DGCA closely monitor corrective/preventive actions. For example, while cabin crew life vests not being easily accessible falls within CAT 2, such finding may be changed to CAT 3 in case of recurrence and more severe sanctions may be imposed.  2.2.5.6. Implementations During Audits and Quality Inspections Conducted in the Cabin  Inspectors may only inspect the fields they are authorized to inspect. Scope of inspection is determined depending on ground time of the aircraft, if enterprise or aircraft is on the list of enterprises with priority for inspection, presence of negative data regarding the enterprise on the information collection system, aircraft type, any findings detected during the inspections formerly performed by the team, and the physical status of the aircraft to be chosen. Inspectors introduce themselves by presenting their ID cards. Inspectors may try to enter the cabin without introducing themselves in order to see if cabin crew checks for ID cards. The ID card of the inspector shall be checked kindly, and the number of the inspectors shall be asked. Flight crew shall be informed by the cabin crew before inspectors enter the cabin. Inspectors shall be welcomed, and a good communication atmosphere shall be established. Auditors shall not be left alone during cabin audit in order to answer their questions and be familiar with the results of the audit. The entire inspection process is carried out under the coordination and responsibility of the Cabin Chief. Characteristics of the aircraft/cabin, emergency materials and their uses may be expressed without waiting for the inspectors to ask questions. Safety  Safety is to reduce any potential risk which may damage persons or goods to an acceptable level through hazard identification and risk management process carried out on constant basis and to maintain such risk at this level. Safety is a relative notion whereby inherent risks in a “safe system” are accepted. Risk is the combination of the probability of occurrence of unwanted events and the effect such events will have if they occur. The operational safety is defined with the cases in which the risks remain at the desired levels. Ensuring the operational safety is both an obligation and a necessity. The employees and all stakeholders have responsibilities to enhance the safety. The awareness levels, attitudes, decisions and behaviors of these persons with regard to enhancement of safety are very important.  3.5.2. Safety Management System (SMS)  It is defined in all requirements specified in   EK.10.21.001 Safety Management Manual.  3.5.3. Safety Reporting System (SRS)  The Safety Reporting System (SRS) currently implemented by Turkish Airlines consists of a series of comprehensive and centralized tools which integrate analysis of risk-associated activities throughout the Company, including safety, quality and security management, and occupational safety. Safety Reporting System includes mandatory reporting, confidential reporting, occurrence reports, Flight Data Monitoring (FDM) data, analysis and investigation as well as inspection and follow-up of corrective actions. The purpose is to determine the methods and principles regarding the recording and or reporting, via the Safety Reporting System (SRS), any nonconformities, irregularities, incidents and hazards appeared or possible to appear during the company operations and likely to affect the safety. The Safety Reporting System (SRS) is a central, electronic and integrated environment where safety notifications are made, the notifications made/received are reviewed by the relevant department and people, the relevant data are analyzed, and the AQD Application is used, for the purpose of managing the operational safety risks in all departments of the Company. The system allows the personnel of the Company to reach Corporate Safety Directorate directly in case of any accident or incident, hazard, nonconformity or breach of legal/sectoral regulations, which may affect the safety during the Company operations. The first step of the system flow process is to report any incidents or potential incidents as an e-report through Turkish Airlines SRS web application ( aqdportal.thy.com). Subsequently, an incident record is created on the database with said report. Collection of any details about safety concerns, hazards and safety incidents in all proactive safety processes is critically important in terms of maintaining and strengthening the integrity of safety barriers. 3.5.4. Information Transfer 3.5.4.1. e-Reporting by Cabin Crews through SRS  All cabin crew members shall submit “Mandatory/Confidential/Voluntary Reports”, which may cover operational safety matters, to Corporate Safety Directorate on electronic environment through SRS “Safety Reporting System” available on AQD Portal. The reports shall be completed in   Turkish   or   English . The system is accessed through the AQD Portal or mobile application. Any non-conformities in relation to quality, environment, occupational health and safety, and all confidential/voluntary reporting submitted to the Senior Vice President (SVP), Quality Assurance in relation to any matter whatsoever, shall be reported by Cabin Crew Member through “Non- Compliance Confidential e-Report (NCC)”. No sanction is imposed on the person submitting report through the SRS System as per all requirements specified in   PL.10.21.002 Safety Declaration that bears the signature of the General Manager.  3.5.4.2. SRS e-Report Types  a) Cabin Safety e-Report (CSR):   The e-reports submitted by Cabin Crew Members for any incidents which affect or may affect the safety of cabin operation process adversely. The minimum topic titles that the Cabin Crew Members are responsible and liable to report and are defined in the CSR that is available on the AQD Portal are determined by Corporate Safety Directorate. Mandatory reporting subjects are the responsibility of the Cabin Chief, and the CSR electronic form is filled in and saved within 48 hours by the Cabin Chief and the other cabin crews who got involved in or witnessed the incident. Mandatory reporting subjects are; Evacuation and Rapid Deplaning Inadvertent Slide Deployment/Dropping of Slide Pack Fire/Smoke Cabin Decompression Flight Crew and Cabin Crew Incapacitation Handling Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident in the Cabin Mild and Serious Passenger Injury in Cabin Nonconformity of Cabin Ready Reports  b) Hazard e-Report (HAZ):   Reporting of the situations such as irregularities, inadequacies, irregular practices, insufficient rules, etc. that are believed to threaten flight safety and may affect the safety of the cabin operation process negatively. The human is the most important aspect in the identification, reporting, and controlling of hazards. Many accidents occur due to inappropriate human behavior, human error, insufficient design, insufficient procedures, loss of situational awareness, intentional acts, insufficient ergonomics and the human factor. Any kind of incident which may result in blatantly interrupting safety or which has the potential to cause any damage and/or injury shall be reported through the hazard reporting process within the SRS.  c) Confidential e-Report (CFR):   The e-report type, also called confidential voluntary reports, used for the flight-safety-related situations that do not require mandatory reporting. The reporter's identity is secured by Corporate Safety Directorate.  d) Fatigue e-Report (FGR):   Reports that contain information about flights causing fatigue due to flight duty period, resting period and flight times/patterns. While filling out the FGR, the negative effects of the felt fatigue on the flight safety must definitely be reported. If there is any risk that has arisen from this fatigue, it must definitely be reported.  e) Non-Compliance e-Report (NCR):   The e-report type used for reporting the general deficiencies/non-compliance in the operation.  f) Non-Compliance Confidential e-Report (NCC):   The e-report type used for submitting confidential-voluntary reports of non- conformities/non-compliances of any sort to Quality Assurance Directorate.  g) Non-Compliance Environment e-Report (NCE):   The e-report type used for reporting any situation and incident which damages, or may damage, the environment partially or wholly during the course of Company activities.  h) Non-Compliance Health e-Report (NCH):   The e-report type used for any non-compliances regarding Occupational Health and Safety which occur or may occur either within the borders of the locations of the Company and/or at the location where any personnel serve during any activity or non-activity.  i) Security e-Report (SEC):   Reports of any incidents/hazards in relation to aviation security, submitted to Security Directorate. In cases where   FR.73.0031 On-Board Unruly Passenger Report (On Ground/In-Flight) is completed, the Threat Level 3 and Threat Level 4 issues must be reported as Security e-Report. Reporting and Just Culture Philosophy  The Safety Management System (SMS) is aimed at achieving the highest possible standards and levels of safety within the scopes of the Company’s operations. It is absolutely mandatory that all personnel contribute to safety programs to succeed in an initiative of this kind. Safety reporting at all levels assures a sustainable system. Therefore, every employee ensures that any information that may affect the safety and operations of Turkish Airlines is communicated. Reckless behavior and deliberate violations of Company’s procedures or a long history of non-compliance shall not be tolerated.  3.6. Monitoring Extraordinary/Unusual Situations and Crisis Management  The principles of crisis management across our Company are defined in all requirements specified in   EK.10.15.001 Security Program of Security Directorate and   EK.10.74.001 Crisis Management Manual of Integrated Operations Control Directorate. In the event that any extraordinary/emergency case occurs/may occur during the cabin operation, then preparation of the employees of Cabin Crew Directorate, and implementation of the crisis management plan, and any measures taken, and the management of any risks occurred in relation to the current situation shall be implemented in accordance with the principles specified in PR.70.013  Procedure for Emergency Unit Implementation Plan For Office of Chief (Flight Operations) Officer and PR.71.087 Procedure for  Monitoring of Extraordinary Situations and Crisis Management During Cabin Operation.  4. Extension with In-Flight Rest (augmentation) Table-9: Maximum Extended FDP. IFR is performed only at the cruise stage of the flight.  TL.71.025 Cabin Crew In-Flight Rest Instruction covers the processes of determining the IFR procedures within the scope of regulatory requirements, monitoring and recording them through internal practices of the Company. For flights requiring IFR, the resting period is specified in the roster application/monthly schedule. The IFR period is at least 90 minutes, during which resting is uninterrupted. If the IFR period is more than 90 minutes, the remaining time may be divided, provided that 90 minutes are uninterrupted. On the flights that require IFR, cabin crew members in at least the following number are ready for duty while the other crew members’ rest: Minimum 5 on board the aircraft types (B777) for which the Minimum Number of Cabin Crew Members is 10, Minimum 4 on board the aircraft types (A330/A350/B787) for which the Minimum Number of Cabin Crew Members is 8, For the narrow body aircraft types, the number specified in Table-2: Minimum Cabin Crew Composition. The familiarization and check flights seating layout and in-flight resting principles are available in LS.72.318 Familiarization and Control  Flights Seating and Resting Layout List. The allocating of crew rest seats on board the aircraft without separate resting area is carried out in compliance with all requirements specified in   PR.10.34.003 Procedure for Allocating Crew Rest Seat. Crew Planning Directorate calculates the IFR periods and reflects them to the cabin crew members’ Roster application/monthly flight schedules. Cabin crew members and Cabin Crew Directorate follow up that the IFR periods planned for cabin crew members and specified in the Roster application/monthly programs are implemented within the framework of the legislation. On the flights with IFR requirement not specified on the roster application/monthly flight schedule, but it is specified in the line information form that in-flight rest can be taken and the in-flight rest can be provided (if there is a crew rest or suitable rest seat), if the cabin crew members need rest, after the completion of the service offer, the IFR can be taken within the knowledge of the commander as per the operational suitability assessment of the cabin chief. Within this scope, IFR is given in the duration and order deemed appropriate by the cabin chief, independently of Table-3: Minimum In-Flight Resting Period and regardless of the In-Flight Rest Orders. The methods related to Principles of Abnormal Situation/Emergency implementation during IFR are carried out as per the requirements specified in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual Section 8.3.1.1.1.   Principles of Implementation for Abnormal Situation/Emergency during Cabin Crew Rest in Cruise. The Cabin Crew Members who are present and on call monitor the cabin, including also the lavatories and galleys, and the passengers, assist the passengers, and establish communication and coordination between the flight and cabin crews. The Cabin Crew Members who are present and on call act in accordance with the requirements specified in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual Section 8.2.10.   Monitoring the Cabin.  Present and On Call:   The readiness in which the Cabin Crew Members are awake and able to perform their duties in compliance with all the relevant normal and emergency procedures specified in the operational manuals. The duties and responsibilities of the resting Cabin Crew Members are carried out by the Cabin Crew Members who are not resting. The Cabin Chief delegates their duties and responsibilities to the most senior Cabin Crew Member while resting. Before and after the IFR, duties and responsibilities are reassigned and the information (special categories of passengers, defect, service methods, etc.) is shared between the Cabin Crew Members who are going to rest and those who are coming back from the rest. Since the in-flight resting varies by the flight conditions, it is given in compliance with Table-3: Minimum In-Flight Resting Period after deducting the actual service period. The IFR (in-flight rest) period is calculated over the period remaining after deducting the 60-minute period (the standard period determined for taxiing, take-off, and landing) and the service period determined for each flight. If the actual service periods are different from the planned periods, the IFR period is determined anew by the cabin crew. The period to be determined may not be less than the minimum in-flight rest period specified in Table-3: Minimum In-Flight Resting Period. The remaining period is divided into two for the flights performed with wide body aircraft, or into three so that the cabin crew members in the number specified in Table-2: Minimum Cabin Crew Composition will be present and on call for the flights performed with narrow body aircraft, thus ensuring that each Cabin Crew Member can take a rest in line with the requirements specified in DK.22.059 SHT-FTL Table-6. Senior Cabin Crew Training is assigned as Cabin Chief. In all flights of the Company, at least one Cabin Chief is assigned within the scope of the cabin crew composition.  4.6. Therefore, any employee other than the assigned Cabin Crew Member [medical personnel, security personnel, flying chef, flying service chef, vocational education student (cabin), translator, etc.] shall not be included in the number of cabin crew members as per the principles defined above and the requirements specified in   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operations Regulations,   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS |  Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air Operations ANNEX-3 Organizational Requirements for Air Operations (Chapter - ORO). Members, are not assigned for any matter directly related to flight security and safety, cannot prevent the flight and Cabin Crew Members from performing their duties; nor they can sit in the cabin crew seats allotted for the assigned Cabin Crew Members. Deadhead Crew on Duty  Deadhead crew on duty are required to act in accordance with   PR.70.002 Procedure on Mixed Planning and Embarkation of the Aircrew when they are on duty with tickets during departure from and arrival to international airports. In order that the passengers can distinguish the assigned cabin crew and the deadhead crew in case of emergency, and that the problems possible to arise during evacuation can be prevented, the following measures are taken: The cabin crews (deadhead cabin crews or the cabin crews traveling with pass tickets) other than the assigned cabin crew members do not serve in the activities (including passenger catering/service) other than the emergency/extraordinary conditions specified in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual Section 4.3 Reduction of Cabin Crew under Unpredictable Conditions (Incapacity or Failure to complete Cabin Crew Number) during Ground/Flight Operations outside Main Base and the Section 8.3.5.4 Selection, Duties and Briefing of Pre-Selected Passengers (PSP) in such a manner as to cause the passengers to confuse them with the assigned cabin crew. The deadhead crew members shall get out of their seats and evacuate their overhead bins during ASSC implementation. When they deadhead on duty, the Cabin Crew Members have to wear their badges reading “Non-assigned to this flight” on the upper right side of their uniforms throughout the flight to be distinguished from the assigned crew. The clothing and conduct codes required to be observed the by deadhead crews on duty are described in the requirements in  EK.10.71.007 Cabin Crew Uniform Use and Representation Manual Chapter 8. Deadhead/Deadhead on Duty Clothing and Representation Rules. The principles of the Accompanying Cabin Crew Member's participation in the flight operation are defined in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.1.5. Infant and Minor Passengers.  4.8. The Expat Cabin Crew Member recruited by Turkish Airlines is assigned to the relevant international line flight on   LS.71.037 Expat  Cabin Crews Prioritized Planning Lines List and in accordance with   PR.71.108   Procedure for Assignment of Expat Cabin Crew Member. Except for the international flights to which they will be assigned primarily, the Expat Cabin Crew Member can also be assigned to other international flights for the effective use of the capacity, provided that they meet the common language requirements and that the maximum/minimum period limits defined within the scope of all requirements specified in DK.22.059 SHT-FTL are fulfilled. According to the requirements specified in   DK.22.106 UOD-2017/2 | Notice On Procedures and Principles Of Foreign Cabin Crew  Assignment Section Two Assignment and Application Conditions, minimum 2 (two) Turkish citizen Cabin Crew Members must be assigned to narrow body aircraft and minimum 3 (three) Turkish citizen Cabin Crew Members to wide body aircraft. From among the Expat Cabin Crew Members: Those who have a minimum of four (4) years of cabin crew member experience and a certificate indicating Turkish language proficiency at minimum A2 CEFR level can be assigned as cabin chief. The Expat Cabin Crew Members are not planned for domestic flights. General  This chapter contains all requirements specified in   DK.33.008 EASA | Aircrew Regulations Annex V (Part-CC), Regulation (EU) No 1178/2011,   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operations Regulations,   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS | Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air  Operations, DK.22.027 SHT OPS N-O,   DK.22.215 SHT-CCTO | Approved Cabin Crew Initial Training Organizations Instruction and the principles defined in the documents of the Company and Cabin Crew Directorate in line with the national and international requirements in relation to the selection, promotion, aircraft type certification, competences, and continuation of such competences of Cabin Crew Members, required to be assigned as a Cabin Crew Member to any aircraft type during the cabin operation process of the Company.  5.2. Principles for Recruitment, Certification and Promotion of Cabin Crew Members  The need for Cabin Crew Members shall be determined with coordination of the Office of Chief Flight Operations Officer and the Office of Chief Human Resources Officer. The Cabin Crew Member recruitment process is managed by the Office of Chief Human Resources Officer in line with the requirements specified in   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operations Regulations ORO.CC.110,   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS |  Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air Operations   ANNEX-3 Organizational Requirements for Air Operations (Chapter -  ORO), Section ORO.CC.110 and all requirements specified in PR.30.002 Procedure for Recruitment Practices and PR.01.30.001 Human Resources Procedure. The principles of assignment of the Cabin Crew Members as per the requirements specified in   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operations  Regulations and   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS | Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air Operations ANNEX-3 Organizational Requirements for Air Operations (Chapter-ORO), ORO.CC.110 are as follows: (1) Minimum 18 years of age, (2) Being assessed to be physically and mentally eligible to carry out their duties and responsibilities safely within the scope of the applicable requirements of   DK.22.116 SHT-MED | Instruction On Aviation Medicine, (3) Having completed the trainings defined in   EK.10.72.006 Cabin Crew Training Manual, Section 3. Training Types and being competent sufficiently to fulfill the duties/responsibilities given in compliance with all procedures specified in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, The promotion and seniority ranking of Cabin Crew Members serving within the organization of the Company is carried out in accordance with all requirements specified in   PR.02.70.002 Cabin Crew Seniority Ranking and Promotion Procedure. Trainings required to ensure the certification of Cabin Crew Members shall be guaranteed under the training programs and training assessment principles prepared as per the national and international requirements and defined in   EK.10.72.006 Cabin Crew Training Manual.  5.3. Cabin Crew Trainings  All trainings that must be received by the Cabin Crew Members are detailed in   EK.10.72.006 Cabin Crew Training Manual Chapter 3. Training Types. 5.3.1. Training Programs  a. Initial Training:   The training program that equips the candidate Cabin Crew Members, in accordance with all requirements specified in   EK.10.72.006 Cabin Crew Training Manual , Section 3.2. Initial Training Program, with core knowledge, skills, and professional proficiency required to be able to perform their duties relating to the flight/passenger safety during the ordinary/standard, extraordinary, and emergency operations, assures the certification of the successful candidates through the measurement and evaluation activities carried out during and/after the training, and is approved by Turkish DGCA. It is implemented as per all requirements in   DK.33.001 EASA |Air Operations Regulations,   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS | Instruction on the  Procedures and Principles for Air Operations ORO.CC.120,   DK.41.001 IOSA Standards Manual (ISM)   CAB 2.1.2, DK.22.215 SHT-  CCTO | Instruction On Approved Cabin Crew Basic Training Organizations. The candidate Cabin Crew Members who have completed the Initial Training successfully are given FR.72.3113 Cabin Crew Attestation issued under the authority given by Turkish DGCA as per the principles described in the requirements of EK.10.72.006 Cabin Crew  Training Manual Section 3.2.3. Initial Training Certification. It is implemented as per all requirements in   DK.33.008 EASA | Aircrew  Regulations , DK.22.122 SHT-CC Cabin Crew Instruction ,   DK.22.215 SHT-CCTO | Instruction On Approved Cabin Crew Basic Training  Organizations. The Attestation is valid as of the effective date specified during its issuance. However, the Initial Training Certificate becomes invalid in the following cases: Suspension or cancellation of the Initial Training Certificate by Turkish DGCA, That the Cabin Crew Member does not perform any flight duty for more than 60 months. Since   Cabin Crew Aircraft Type/Variant Qualification(s) a Cabin Crew Member has to carry with them throughout the flight operation bears the reference number of FR.72.3113 Cabin Crew Attestation,   it is not mandatory to carry FR.72.3113 Cabin Crew Attestation  during the flight operation. The Cabin Crew Members are responsible for; Retaining their certificates in such a manner as to be protected from damage, Keeping it in a protective cover, Filing a renewal application with Flight Training Directorate/Cabin Training Management if their certificates get lost, get broken, become illegible or the signature on the certificate is smeared/deleted due to contact with chemicals (perfume, cologne, etc.), Submitting their certificates to the Company or Turkish DGCA upon demand (leaving the Company included).  Reasons of Suspension or Cancellation of Cabin Crew Attestation by Turkish DGCA as per All Requirements in   DK.22.122 SHT-CC Cabin Crew Instruction and   DK.22.215 SHT-CCTO | Instruction On Approved Cabin Crew Basic Training Organizations In case of losing compliance with the minimum standards a Cabin Crew Member is required to meet after issuance of the cabin crew attestation, or detecting safety-related nonconformity under Part-ORO and Part-CAT, the cabin crew attestation is suspended by Turkish Directorate General of Civil Aviation. Those concerned are given 30 (thirty) days in order to correct the nonconformity that has caused the suspension. In the event that the nonconformity is not corrected at the end of this period, the cabin crew initial training certificate is canceled by Turkish DGCA. The discretion to decide on sufficiency of the corrective actions taken to correct the nonconformity and validity of the cabin crew initial training certificate belongs to Turkish DGCA. In case of detecting forgery of documents submitted to Turkish DGCA or the training organization for issuance of the certificate or maintaining its validity, or finding out that the rights provided by the certificate have been exercised while under the influence of alcohol or psychoactive substance, or abusing the certificate, or using the certificate for fraud, the cabin crew initial training certificate is canceled by Turkish DGCA.  Suspension and Cancellation of Cabin Crew Attestation as per All Requirements in   DK.22.122 SHT-CC Cabin Crew Instruction and   DK.22.215 SHT-CCTO | Instruction On Approved Cabin Crew Basic Training Organizations According to the requirements specified in   DK.33.008 EASA | Aircrew Regulations CC.CCA.110, DK.22.122 SHT-CC Cabin Crew Instruction, and   DK.22.215 SHT-CCTO | Approved Cabin Crew Initial Training Organizations Instruction, the procedure for suspension and cancellation of the initial training certificate is as follows: Turkish DGCA informs the certificate holders and the Company of the suspension or cancellation decision in writing together with the right of objection in compliance with the legislation. After the person concerned has been informed of the decision, the certificate holder may not exercise the rights provided by the cabin crew attestation. Cabin crew members maintain their fitness for flight as per the health criteria defined in the Company’s standards for recruitment of Cabin Crew Members by taking protective measures against diseases, and report any decrease in their medical fitness according to the requirements specified in   DK.22.116 SHT-MED |Instruction On Aviation Medicine MED.A.020 to the Company's physicians and meet the requirements in PR.10.30.038 Procedure for Aviation Medicine Practices.  6.1.1. Statutory Requirements  Within the scope of all requirements specified in   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operations Regulations CAT.GEN.MPA.100,   DK.33.008 EASA |  Aircrew Regulations ANNEX IV Part MED,   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS | Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air Operations  ANNEX-4 Commercial Air Transportation (Chapter-CAT), DK.22.116 SHT-MED Aviation Health Instruction, and DK.22.119 SHT-APAM  |Instruction on Alcohol and Psychoactive Substance Examinations of Aviation Personnel subject to Control, when the Company’s Cabin Crew Members are under the influence of psychoactive substance or alcohol, or if they are not fit for flight and standby duties due to medication, fatigue, illness, injury or similar reasons, or if they find any deterioration in their fitness for flight in terms of health, which may prevent them from fulfilling their safety-related duties and responsibilities, and in case of a decrease in medical compliance according to the requirements specified in   DK.22.116 SHT-MED |Instruction On Aviation Medicine MED.A.020, they may not perform any duty on board aircraft, nor may they exercise the privileges of their cabin crew certificates; and if it is detected that they do so, they are removed from the operational duties. The list of the drugs the use of which by the crew members is disapproved by the health authorities is available in LS.35.024 List of  Drugs affecting Flight Safety. The list includes the active substances and the most frequently used commercial names of the drugs inappropriate to use regarding flight safety. Since there might be numerous drugs with different commercial names but containing the same active substance, it is necessary to pay attention to the active substance name. The drugs can be queried in the “Prohibited Drugs” list by accessing the “Prohibited Drugs and Food” field of the “Health Information” module in the HEALTHY mobile application. The crew member who has been informed that s/he will be subjected to alcohol and psychoactive substance test is not permitted to perform any duty in the operation unless s/he is subjected to the test. If it is determined that the cabin crew member has exercised the rights provided by the Cabin Crew Attestation while under the influence of alcohol or psychoactive substances, measures are taken within the scope of EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual Section 5.3.1. Training Programs and DK.22.122 SHT-CC Cabin Crew Instruction.  6.1.1.1. Deterioration of Medical Fitness  When a Cabin Crew Member is medically unfit to perform flight duty or in case of the requirements specified in DK.22.116 SHT-MED  |Instruction On Aviation Medicine MED.A.020 on deterioration of medical fitness; a) If they detect any deterioration of their health that can prevent them from fulfilling their flight duties (the certificate privileges), b) If they use a prescription or nonprescription medicine or legally prohibited substance that is likely to prevent the safe performance of the flight (the privileges of the relevant certificate), c) If they are exposed to any medical treatment, surgical treatment or similar treatment which may jeopardize the flight safety, They apply to the Cabin Operations Control Supervisory. Then, they are referred to the Company’s physicians for an evaluation of their fitness for flight. The Cabin Crew Member applies to the physicians in the Company’s health departments and FR.35.0088 Cabin Crew  Member Medical Eligibility Impairment Notification Form is filled out in line with the requirements specified in DK.22.116 SHT-MED  |Instruction On Aviation Medicine MED.A.020 on deterioration of medical fitness and PR.10.30.038 Procedure for Aviation Medicine Practices. Depending on the result of the medical examination carried out by the Company physicians, back-to-work/sick leave report/hospital referral action is taken. In the following cases, the Cabin Crew Members apply to the Human Resources Assistant Directorate (Health) health departments together with all their reports, prescriptions, and tests: In case they are exposed to any surgical operation or interference, When they start to use any medicine regularly, In case they suffer from a serious injury or disablement that prevents them from performing their duties as a Flight Crew Member, In case they suffer from a serious disease that prevents them from performing their duties as a Flight Crew Member; If they are pregnant, In case they are hospitalized in any hospital or health clinic, When they need a corrective lens for the first time, If the Company physician finds any deterioration in the Cabin Crew Members’ fitness for flight in terms of health, which may prevent them from fulfilling their safety-related duties and responsibilities, such cabin crew members are not permitted to perform any duty on E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 92 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250

board aircraft and use the privileges of the cabin crew approvals. In that case, the Cabin Crew Members are evaluated for fitness for flight as per PR.10.30.038 Procedure for Aviation Medicine Practices.  6.1.1.1.1. Fatigue  If a Cabin Crew Member does not feel physically and psychologically well enough to fulfill their duties due to fatigue, if they have any doubts about their health, they apply to the Cabin Operations Control Supervisory. The Cabin Operations Control Supervisory refers them to the Company physicians for an evaluation of their fitness for flight. Depending on the result of the medical examination carried out by the Company physicians, back-to-work/sick leave report/hospital referral action is taken. If they receive sick leave report due to fatigue, they complete the Fatigue (FGR) report over SRS (AQD system) as per EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual Section 3.5.4.2. SRS e-Report Types.  6.1.1.2. Sick Leave Reports  The subjects in relation to management of the sickness reports of Cabin Crew Members are described in PR.10.35.089 Procedure for  Implementation of the Processes of Submission of Sick Leave Reports and Performance of Return-to-Work Examinations. In the event that such a situation happens at an intermediate airport, Cabin Chief and Commander are informed, and it is ensured that the Cabin Crew Member's fitness-for-flight is assessed at the relevant medical institution under the coordination of the station officials.  6.1.1.3. Periodic Examination  Medical examinations of the candidate Cabin Crew Members prior to employment and periodical health screening of the cabin crew members are performed and monitored in accordance with all requirements specified in   DK.22.116 SHT-MED |Instruction On Aviation Medicine and PR.10.30.038 Procedure for Aviation Medicine Practices. Aviation medical examinations of Cabin Crew Members shall be performed every 5 years as of the date of their employment. The Cabin Crew Members participate in the planned periodic examination. The medical examination results of the candidate Cabin Crew Members are retained in their personal files kept at Cabin Crew Directorate, the periodic aviation medical examination results of the Cabin Crew Members are first evaluated by the workplace physicians of Turkish Airlines, and then retained in their personal files in Turkish Airlines Human Resources Assistant Directorate (Health).  6.1.1.4. Cabin Crew Health Examination Report  The Cabin Crew Members are required to carry the Cabin Crew Health Examination Report issued by the health institution with them throughout the duty. In case of name/surname changes, it is necessary to take the necessary actions as per the Medical Examination Report renewal transactions specified in the “ Name/Surname Change Notification and Document Renewal Process” announcement. In the event that the Cabin Crew Medical Examination Report issued from the medical institution contains any of the restrictions listed in  LS.35.027 Cockpit Cabin Personnel Turkish DGCA Periodic Inspection Restrictions List, Cabin Crew Members fulfill the requirements of   DK.33.008 EASA | Aircrew Regulations Annex IV Part MED AMC1 MED.C.035,   DK.22.116 SHT-MED | Instruction on Aviation Medicine MED.C.035 Cabin Crew Medical Report. If the Cabin Crew Members have any one or more than one of the restrictions specified in   LS.35.027 LS.35.027 Cockpit Cabin  Personnel Turkish DGCA Periodic Inspection Restrictions List in the health examination report issued by the hospital authorized by Turkish DGCA, they fulfill the requirements of those restrictions. After the evaluation, the medical report is retained in their personal health files in Turkish Airlines Human Resources Assistant Directorate (Health).  6.1.2. Crew Health Precautions. The methods related to nutrition for the Cabin Crew Members during the flight duty period are described in all requirements specified in  PR.01.70.012 Procedure for Meal, Accommodation and Travel Allowances of Flight Crew on Flight Duties.  6.1.2.1. The   use   of   psychoactive   substance   is   defined   in   the   requirements   in   DK.33.001   EASA   |Air   Operations   Regulations   AMC1  CAT.GEN.MPA.100(c)(1),   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS | Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air Operations ANNEX-4 Commercial E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 93 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250

Air Transportation (Chapter-CAT). In accordance with the national/international rules and the Company legislation, the flight and Cabin Crew Members are prohibited from using psychoactive substances and consuming foodstuffs that include poppy. Any Cabin Crew Member who is suspected to have used psychoactive substance prior to the flight or within the flight or standby duty shall be immediately reported to the immediate supervisor and/or Cabin Crew Directorate and transferred to the Health Department as per the principles specified in   PR.10.35.097 Procedure For Medical Examination For Alcohol And Psychoactive Substances. Regardless of the initial findings, the Cabin Crew Member’s duty is stopped by removing them from the operation, and they are subjected to more detailed verification tests. In the event of a positive result of the random verification test conducted before or after the flight by the supervising health employee without notifying the employee, the relevant Cabin Crew Member shall be suspended from the flight. Administrative measures shall be applied within the scope of   PR.10.35.097 Procedure For Medical Examination For Alcohol And Psychoactive Substances. Following the disciplinary actions, a notification is sent to Turkish DGCA for evaluation of suspension/cancellation of the cabin crew attestation in line with DK.22.122 SHT-CC Cabin Crew Instruction and   TL.72.311 Instruction on Suspension/Cancellation of Cabin Crew Attestation. It   may   also   be   detected   that   whether   the   Cabin   Crew   Member   has   used   psychoactive   substance   through   the   SHT-APAM examination performed in line with PR.10.30.038 Procedure for Aviation Medicine Practices. At each stage of the flight, the inspectors authorized by Turkish DGCA may conduct alcohol and psychoactive substance checks as per the requirements specified in   DK.22.179 BPR.03 Procedure Of Alcohol Screening Test,   DK.22.119 SHT-APAM |Instruction On  Control Of Alcohol and Psychoactive Substances Of Aviation Personnel Subjected To Control, and   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operations  Regulations, AMC1 CAT.GEN.MPA.100(c)(1) , ARO.RAMP.106. According to the requirements specified in   DK.22.179 BPR.03 Procedure Of Alcohol Screening Test: The flight and Cabin Crew Members help the inspection committee during the inspections and ensure safe continuation of the flight operation by meeting the requirements requested by the inspection committee rapidly. For any flight and Cabin Crew Member who rejects to participate in the test, the test result is deemed to be positive until proven otherwise.  6.1.2.2.
