6.1.2.16. Quarantine Applications  The quarantine measures to be applied in case any crew member or passenger shows indications of a significant infectious disease during flight are described in the requirements in   PR.10.35.025 Procedure for Protection and Control Practices Against Contagious Diseases and   EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part-A,   Chapter 6. Crew Health Precautions. If any one or more than one of the following findings and symptoms are observed in the passenger(s) and/or crew members before or during the flight; High fever (38⁰C and above) Sore throat, headache and body aches Nasal discharge, cough, phlegm, chill, shiver Hard breathing, rashes, unexplained bleeding Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach ache Crew members immediately inform the flight crew during the flight mission and the Human Resources Assistant Directorate (Health) through the most effective means of communication (11212,   SAGLIK@THY.COM) off the flight mission. When a passenger suspected to be sick is detected during the flight, the flight crew inform the Health Authority of the relevant airport of the situation urgently through the available channels of communication due to contagious disease suspicion. Any suspected infectious disease detected during the flight must be reported immediately by the commander to the relevant Air Traffic Unit, and timely notification to the public health authority at the destination must be ensured in an appropriate manner. If the disease is encountered during the flight, medical assistance is requested by making an announcement for physician; on the ground, medical ground support is requested through the ground employee/flight crew. Universal precaution kit is brought. The passenger and crew use the personal protective equipment included in it. If possible, the sick passenger is moved away from other passengers. The sick person is kept isolated from the other passengers without compromising on the flight security. Seat the sick passenger on the aft seats or replace the passengers sitting in the rows immediately in front of, behind, and next to the passenger, if possible. If this is not possible, it is made sure that the passengers sitting on the front 2, back 2, and next 2 seats wear masks. If s/he has symptoms of coughing/sneezing, the passenger suspected to have the disease is made to wear a mask; if the passenger cannot tolerate wearing a mask, s/he must be provided with adequate paper towels or paper napkins and asked to cover his/her mouth and nose; and also, s/he is provided with a sick bag and plenty of napkins against possibility of vomiting. Due to the risk of contamination, the areas used by the affected passenger are cleaned. In order to preserve the health of flight crew and other passengers, one of the lavatories is allocated for the use of passenger(s) suspected to be sick. The toilet must be flushed by closing the toilet seat lid. In times when it is not possible to use soap, use alcohol-based hand sanitizers/wipes. The least possible number of cabin crew members contact the disease suspect directly. These cabin crew member(s) shall not be assigned to any other service. The existing duties of the assigned cabin crew member are redistributed. The assigned cabin crew employee shall wear mask, disposable gloves (double gloves shall be worn), apron, and safety glasses in the “Universal Precaution Kit” when necessary. They do not walk around inside the aircraft wearing personal protective equipment, they stay with the sick passenger only. After the use, take off the mask and the gloves carefully, destroy them, and wash your hands with soap and water immediately. It is ensured that the Personal Protective Equipment is used properly and in the correct order. The order of wearing PPE is as follows: Apron – Mask – Goggles/face shield – Gloves.  ➢ The apron is worn as shown in Figure-2. While wearing it; The apron material is selected depending on the process to be applied. The type and size of the material must be appropriate. It is tied at the back. The Country of destination may request from the Company information on the passenger’s destination (so that the passenger can be contacted) and itinerary. Through the Public Health Passenger Locator Card, which contains the information of the suspected case (passenger), the relevant Country Health Authority can obtain the contact information of the persons and follow up the case. The cabin crew fills in the Public Health Passenger Locator Cards in the Universal Precaution Kit for suspicious cases detected during the flight, and delivers these cards to the Airport Official Health Authority at the end of the flight. The cabin crew waits for the medical team to meet the aircraft and acts as per the instructions of the medical team. After transferring the suspicious case (passenger) detected during the flight to the Airport Official Health Authority, one copy of the Gen-Dec (General Declaration) completed by the employee is placed into the Universal Precaution Kit and delivered to Turkish Airlines Health Department.  6.1.2.17. 6.1.2.18. Cabin Crew Members who have Restrictions in their Cabin Crew Health Examination Reports  The Cabin Crew Members who have one of the restrictions specified in the requirements in   DK.33.008 EASA | Aircrew Regulations ANNEX IV Part MED/AMC1 MED.C.035 Limitations have to fulfill their restriction requirements. In the event that the Cabin Crew Member who has any health restriction in their health examination report catches any illness that will threat the safety and security of the flight or fails to fulfill their duties and responsibilities properly during any flight operation, the incident is reported urgently by the Cabin Chief or the Cabin Crew Members who have witnessed the incident to Corporate Safety Directorate by using the SRS “Safety Reporting System” available on AQD Portal and Cabin Crew Directorate/Assistant Directorate (Operation and Compliance)/Cabin Operations Management/Safety Tracking Supervisory by using   FR.71.0070 CCD Correspondence Form.  6.1.2.18.1. Cabin Crew Members who have Restriction due to Vision Disorders  The Cabin Crew Members who have CVL (a requirement for visual correction) restriction and need to work with prescription glasses as per the requirements specified in   DK.33.008 EASA | Aircrew Regulations ANNEX IV Part MED/AMC1 MED.C.035 Limitations have to wear glasses or contact lenses during the duty as per the requirements specified in   DK.33.008 EASA | Aircrew Regulations ANNEX IV Part MED/AMC13 MED.C.025/article g and are required to carry spare glasses or contact lenses with them. The Cabin Crew Members who have CCL (by the aid of corrective lenses) restriction in their Health Examination Reports are required to carry spare contact lenses with them. The Cabin Crew Members are required to submit to the Cabin Chief, before the flight, their health examination reports, and inform her/him that they carry the glasses/lenses (together with the spare ones) that meet the restriction with them; or if the person who has the said restriction in their health examination report is the Cabin Chief of the flight, s/he is required to do the same thing to the Cabin Operations Control Supervisory.  Color Vision Deficiency  When their aircraft type certificates are to be changed, or when they have incidents reported, the Cabin Crew Members who have MCL (a restriction to operate only in multi-cabin crew operations) and SSL (must be re-evaluated in case of aircraft type certificate change and incidents reported) restrictions in their medical reports due to color vision deficiency are required to apply to the Company physician and not to perform flight duties until their examinations at the healthcare institution where they have been referred to are completed.  6.1.2.18.2. Cabin Crew Members who have Restriction due to Hearing Disorders  The Cabin Crew Members who have HAL (a requirement for hearing aid) restriction and need to work with hearing aid as per the requirements specified in   DK.33.008 EASA | Aircrew Regulations ANNEX IV Part MED/AMC1 MED.C.035 Limitations have to use hearing aid during the duty as per the requirements specified in   DK.22.116 SHT-MED | Instruction On Aviation Medicine, DK.33.008  EASA | Aircrew Regulations ANNEX IV Part MED/AMC14 MED.C.025, and carry spare aid or battery with them. The Cabin Crew Members are required to submit to the Cabin Chief, before the flight, their health examination reports, and inform her/him that they have their hearing aids attached, and that they carry the spare aids/batteries with them; or if the person who has the said restriction in their health examination report is the Cabin Chief of the flight, s/he is required to do the same thing to the Cabin Operations Control Supervisory.  6.1.2.18.3. Cabin Crew Members who work under the condition of Continuous Health Check  The Cabin Crew Members whose medical reports issued by the Health Institution include TML (a requirement to undergo an aerodynamic examination and/or assessment immediately before the one required by a restriction imposed for a predetermined aircraft type or a predetermined operation type), SIC (a requirement to undergo specific regular medical examinations), and SSL (special restriction as specified) restrictions, or who are required to undergo checks at regular intervals without any restriction, undergo the necessary examination on the date specified by the health institution and fulfill the requirements specified in PR.10.30.038 Procedure for Aviation Medicine Practices.  6.1.2.18.4. Cabin Crew Members who have Restrictions against Certain Operation and Aircraft Types  The Cabin Crew Members whose medical reports issued by the Health Institution include OAL (a restriction to specified aircraft type(s) and OOL (to a specified type of operation) restrictions are required to give information   to the Company physician to be referred to the health institution for re-evaluation   in case of aircraft type certificate change or operation change.  6.2. 6.2.1. Illness on Domestic or International Stay-over Duties  In case of incapacitation, the cabin crew members shall act in accordance with the requirements specified in   EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part-A, Section 6.2.4 Procedures to be Carried Out In Case of Sickness During a Layover Period. Sickness of any cabin crew member during the flight is reported to the Cabin Chief and the Commander as soon as possible. For the information on the situation in which s/he has been incapacitated, the Cabin Crew Member and/or the Cabin Chief starts an e- mail correspondence with   cabinincap@thy.com by adding also the e-mail address of the station department where the incapacitation took place, and gives information to the station. The operational e-mail address of the relevant station is found by adding “OPS” to the end of the three-letter area code (example:   jfkops@thy.com,   esbops@thy.com). The personnel member who had been incapacitated applies to a medical institution under the guidance of their superior and/or the officers of the relevant station. After completion of their examination and treatments, their flight is ensured by the operational departments, provided that they have “Fit to fly report” indicating that they can fly as assigned crew member or passenger. If there is any situation that requires the continuation of their treatment, s/he is given health and accommodation support throughout the stay-over by the station authorities until their “Fit to fly report” is approved. The procedures to be applied in case of illness or incapacitation of a cabin crew member on a domestic or international stay-over duty are   described   in   the   requirements   specified   in   EK.10.73.001   Operation   Manual   Part-A,   Chapter   6   Crew   Health   Precautions, PR.10.30.038 Procedure for Aviation Medicine Practices, and PR.10.32.004 Procedure for Health Practices.  7. Flight and Duty Limits  7.1. General  In respect of ensuring flight safety, the principles and procedures in relation to flight duty and resting periods required to be observed by flight crews to serve at any aircraft of the Company and by the Company during the planning process are carried out as per the requirements specified in   EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part-A, Chapter 7. Flight Time Limitations, and all requirements specified in  DK.33.001 EASA |Air Operations Regulations CAT.GEN.MPA.100,   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS | Instruction on the Procedures and Principles  for Air Operations ANNEX-4 Commercial Air Transportation (Chapter-CAT), DK.22.059 SHT-FTL of the Directorate General of Civil Aviation.  8.1. Cabin Ground Operation Implementations  8.1.1. Duty Commencement  In case of the flights originating from the main base and the flights performed out of the main base, the Cabin Crew Members wear the cabin crew uniform given to them by Turkish Airlines and enabling the passengers to know them as the Cabin Crew Members, and are ready to receive duty in full uniform at the scheduled signature time. In the flights departing from the main base, the cabin crews prove their attendance at the signature time through the kiosk machines/“Check-in” application/Crew Assignment Management. The principles of the fitness-to-fly check of cabin crews specified in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 2.   Operational Control and Monitoring are carried out as per   PR.71.022 Cabin Operation Control Supervisor Daily Operation Process Management Procedure. The cabin crew member obtains the forms/documents s/he will use during the duty. As defined in   PR.70.002 Procedure For The Mixed Planning And Embarkation of The Aircrew, for all domestic and international flights (ER flights included), if the aircraft is given at the signature time, the Cabin Chiefs board the aircraft at the signature time without waiting for the Flight Crew Members even if there is absent Cabin Crew Member, and the flight and cabin crews meet on board the aircraft. If the flight and cabin crew members meet on board the aircraft, the Cabin Chief ensures that the entire crew participates in the crew briefing to be given in the forward section of the aircraft. In respect of all flights where the aircraft is not ready at the main base, the crew briefing shall be performed in Turkish in the available areas such as briefing rooms, etc. in coordination with the Commander in compliance with the schedule and without causing any delay. If there is minimum one expat employee in the flight/cabin crew, it is necessary to give the briefing in English. As for airports other than the main base, cabin crew shall be ready at the time determined by the Commander/station official. Cabin crew members embark the aircraft just after the aircraft is assigned to a flight on FID (Flight Information Data)/Check-In system displays, in order to improve on time departure performance. In cases where the Cabin Chief of the flight is absent at the signature time, the most senior Cabin Crew Member shall contact with the Crew Assignment Management, and the crew shall act in compliance with the directives. Cabin Crew Briefing  Cabin crew briefing is performed in the appropriate areas such as briefing room, etc. or on board the aircraft before each flight in accordance with the requirements specified in DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operation Regulations GM1 ORO.CC.250, AMC1 ORO.GEN.110 (f)(h),   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS | Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air Operations ANNEX-3 Organizational Requirements for Flight Operations (Chapter-ORO), and   DK.41.001 IOSA Standards Manual (ISM) section CAB 4.1.1. In order to meet the safety, security and service standards in all flights, prior to each flight and subsequent to coding of the cabin crew members, the Cabin Chief gives the cabin crew briefing by reminding the pax/special categories of passengers, current malfunctions, and the requirements in the line information form. The Cabin Crew Member who has the highest seniority after the Cabin Chief on Duty is assigned as C/A1 in narrow-body aircraft or C/C1 in wide-body aircraft. The other Cabin Crew Members may be coded under the Cabin Chief's initiative. In respect of ER flights, it must be ensured that any Cabin Crew Members with a command of any foreign language serve in different classes while coding. The class F (inexperienced Cabin Crew Member) is defined in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual Section 4. Number and Composition of Cabin Crew. If there is any open/ongoing cabin-related defect in the Aircraft Maintenance Log (AML), the flight crew shares this during the cabin crew briefing. The cabin chief informs the cabin crew of the AML defects before/during the briefing as per the requirements specified in  EK.10.73.001 Operations Manual Part-A, Section 8.1. Flight Preparation Instructions. If there is any procedure specified in MEL in relation to the ongoing defect in AML, which must be carried out by the cabin crew, it is informed to the cabin crew by the flight crew. If there is minimum one expat member in the cabin crew, the briefing shall be given in English. In order to apply the safety and security standards on all flights, the following items are included in the main briefing subjects: a) Methods of the emergency equipment and technical materials check b) Operational Practices - Emergency Practices c) Security and ASSC implementation procedures d) Procedures for opening/closing the doors and the “Slide Armed/Disarmed” practices e) Ground handling employee, crew and passenger communication, coordination and CRM f) It is reminded that the cabin must be monitored throughout the flight and on ground as specified in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual Section 8.2.10. Monitoring the Cabin. g) Pax information (pax number, SCP, etc.) h) Numbering i) Defects j) Special information on the flight in the line information form k) Door password l) In the event that the flight continues with a different aircraft type/variant, the Cabin Chief reminds the emergency, technical material, technical differences, practice differences, and the cockpit door password with a briefing in line with the requirements specified in DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operation Regulations GM1 ORO.CC.250, DK.22.115 SHT-OPS | Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air Operations ANNEX-3 Organizational Requirements for Flight Operations (Chapter-ORO). m) Depending on the flight pattern, rules regarding stay-over/deadhead flight duties are reminded in accordance with the requirements specified in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Chapter 1. Organizational Duties and Responsibilities and EK.10.71.007 Cabin Crew Uniform Use and Representation Manual Chapter 5. Stay-Over Representation Rules. n) The cabin chief receives verbal confirmation from all cabin crew members that the documents (Manual, Bulletin, etc.) containing up- to-date standard operational information have been read. Completion of Aircraft (Cabin) Preparation Form by Standby Cabin Crew  While preparing the aircraft for a flight, if any assigned cabin crew is to return from another flight with delay, then the standby Cabin Crew Members may be assigned for this preparation in order to prevent any operational irregularities. In such case, any Cabin Crew Member to be assigned is required to have the applicable certificate of the relevant aircraft type. The standby cabin crews acquire   FR.71.0107 Aircraft (Cabin) Preparation Form from the Cabin Operations Control Supervisory before beginning to prepare the aircraft.  FR.71.0107 Aircraft (Cabin) Preparation Form shall be filled by the standby Cabin Crew Members preparing the aircraft by indicating name, surname and registration and affixing signature. The Cabin Chief preparing the aircraft shall also writes the date, flight number, pattern and aircraft type, and reports flight preparation information on Greenwich Mean Time (GMT)/CET time. Aircraft preparation duty of the standby crew ends when the relevant cabin crew reaches the aircraft. All activities performed until that period are recorded in   FR.71.0107 Aircraft (Cabin) Preparation Form; and the Cabin Chief who will perform the flight writes their details down in the relevant field of the form. The unchecked items are specified on the form and informed to the Cabin Chief of the flight. The first copy of the form is delivered to the Cabin Chief who will perform the flight, and the cabin chief retains the form for one month. The standby Cabin Crew Members deliver the second copy to the Cabin Operations Control Supervisory after the aircraft preparation so that it can be delivered to Cabin Crew Directorate. If the aircraft has been prepared by the standby cabin crew, and if the passenger boarding process has also been carried out by this crew, the Cabin Chief who shall perform the flight is given a briefing by the Cabin Chief who has prepared the aircraft, and the contents of this briefing comprises of the following items: The checks performed in the cabin over   FR.71.0107 Aircraft (Cabin) Preparation Form and the passenger information Information on the Special Categories of Passengers (SCPs) Information on special loads and cargoes (Dangerous Goods, etc.) Standby cabin crew who completes aircraft preparation duty informs Crew Assignment Management that the duty is completed.  8.1.3. Use of Portable Electronic Devices (PED). Cabin Crew Checklist/Quick Reference Handlist (QRH)  Quick   Reference   Handlist   is   a   document   that   is   prepared   so   that   the   cabin   crews   can   manage   the   potential   abnormal situations/emergencies   possible   to   occur   during   the   flight   operation   correctly   and   rapidly,   and   includes   the   emergency procedures/applications and the announcements that may be needed. Cabin Crew Checklist is the document that itemizes the checks and operational duties the Cabin Crew Members are required to carry out throughout the ordinary flight operation by the stage of flight. Each item refers to a certain check/operational duty, and the relevant responsibility is defined to the Cabin Crew Member(s) required to perform that duty. Any cabin crew member uses the Cabin Crew Checklist at each stage of the flight within the framework of the duties and responsibilities assigned to her/him in the document with the number under which s/he serves. In order to ensure their effective use throughout the operation, Cabin Crew Checklist and   Quick Reference Handlist (QRH) are prepared considering the human factor. Compliance of the relevant documents with EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual and EK.10.71.003 Cabin  Crew Aircraft Types Manual prepared as per the requirements specified in   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operation Regulations ORO.GEN.110 and   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS | Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air Operations ANNEX-3 Organizational Requirements for Flight Operations (Chapter-ORO) and the methods specified the aircraft manufacturer firm documents in line with the national and international legislations is ensured. The Cabin Crew Checklists are placed in as many checklist holders as the minimum cabin crew count on all aircraft types, while the Quick Reference Handlists (QRH ) are available in the emergency equipment cabinet under the cabin crew jump seat, and the spare documents in the document cabinet. The cabin crews check during the ground checks that the Cabin Crew Checklists and Quick  Reference Handlists (QRH) are in their own places, that the Cabin Crew Checklists have the version and revision numbers that match the aircraft type, while the   Quick Reference Handlists (QRH) have the document and revision numbers that match the aircraft type, and that these documents are not incomplete/erroneous/worn, as specified in   FR.71.0312 Inflight Document Control Form. The Cabin Crew Checklists are kept in the checklist holders at all cabin crew stations/next to stations throughout the flight operation and left in the checklist holders at the end of the flight. If the backup Cabin Crew Checklists are used, they are put back into the document cabinet at the end of the flight.  Emergency Exit Passenger Briefing Card  The information on the   Emergency Exit Passenger Briefing Cards used to give information to our passengers sitting in the emergency exit window seats on board narrow-body aircraft as well as the principles of checking these cards are available in   FR.71.0312 Inflight Document Control Form.  Safety Card  The information on and the checking methods of the   Safety Card prepared so as to give the passengers the necessary information under the normal situation and emergency conditions on the basis of the features determined for each aircraft type/variant, the emergency equipment, and the normal situation/emergency procedures in line with   PR.10.70.059 Procedure For The Preparation Of  Safety Cards/Safety Video/Automatic And Manual Announcement are available in   FR.71.0312 Inflight Document Control Form. During departure from the main base, the Cabin Crew Member specified in the Cabin Crew Checklist must check that as many spare  Safety Cards as specified in   FR.71.0312 Inflight Document Control Form are available, and in case of missing documents, s/he must obtain them and complete the missing cards in the seat pockets at the intermediate airports. The   Safety Cards in the seat pockets are checked during ASSCL by the Cabin Crew Members defined in the Cabin Crew Checklist ASSC chart.  Safety Card Visual Placard fixed to Passenger Seat/Wall Panel  The safety card visual may be fixed to the back of the headrest of the front passenger seat or to the wall panel depending on the aircraft type/variant. The information on the check of the safety placard is available in   FR.71.0312 Inflight Document Control Form.  8.1.3.2. Manner of Use:  It shall be secured on the separators in front of the passengers, during level flight after take-off. While fasten seat belt signs are "ON", the infant's parent or legal guardian shall be informed about taking the infant out of the bassinet and securing the infant with the infant belt. Infant Belt  It shall be used with the purpose of securing the infants under the age of 2 (INF) on the laps of the parents/accompanying persons. It is not passed over the infant. When fastened, it must remain between the infant and the parent/accompanying person.  Extension Belt  It is attached to the seatbelt with the purpose of extending the seatbelt. The extension belts are distributed to passengers, and information on the use of the belt is given if requested. Passenger Safety Briefing. The view of the passenger safety film on the displays is checked by the cabin crew by observing the displays under the Cabin Chief's coordination during the ground preparations. Check of the Trolley Brake Pedals  Prior to flight: Catering trolleys: If a catering trolley with defective brake mechanism is detected, the trolley is affixed with the “Defective” label by filling in the relevant sections, and the catering employee is informed of the same so that the trolley is replaced. If it cannot be replaced before the flight, the defective trolley secured in its place, and not used. The cabin report is completed through MoCA. Waste trolleys/Foldable trolleys: If a waste trolley/foldable trolley with defective brake mechanism is detected, the relevant defect is recorded. If it cannot be replaced before the flight, the defective trolley secured in its place, and not used. During flight: Catering trolleys: Before entering the cabin, the Cabin Crew Member(s) who will use the relevant trolley in the service check(s) that its brake mechanism works properly. The catering trolleys whose brake mechanisms are found defective are affixed with the “Defective” label by filling in the relevant sections, secured in their places, and not used. Waste trolleys/Foldable trolleys: Before entering the cabin, the Cabin Crew Member(s) who will use the relevant trolley check(s) that its brake mechanism works properly. The catering trolleys whose brake mechanisms are found defective are secured in their places, and not used. Make a record of the relevant trolley defect. If there are defective catering trolleys that could not be replaced before the flight/whose defects have been detected during the flight and/or the alternative service methods have been used, the Cabin Chief creates a cabin report over DCMS MoCA. If a finding related to catering trolley is detected as a result of SAFA Inspection, a cabin report is issued through MoCA. Catering employees meet the aircraft and take delivery of the defective catering trolley. In order to prevent unsafe situations in trolley/unit loading, loading is carried out by the supplier catering firm in accordance with the placards in the loading areas. If it is detected on the ground that the loading is not in accordance with the placards, the supplier catering firm is informed, and a loading change is requested. If the loading cannot be changed appropriately, the flight crew is informed. The cabin report is completed through the MoCA application.  8.1.3.3. Additionally, the e-CML defects that have triggered no warning but been assessed to affect the flight safety are informed to the flight crew and ensured to be recorded in AML. Aircraft Maintenance Log (AML)  Flight crew reports AML defects (Open/Continuing Item) to cabin crew during/after flight briefing. The flight crew shall inform the Cabin Chief of the defects in the AML relating to the cabin, and the measures to be taken under MEL in the event that the flight continues despite the defect. It is necessary to ensure that any defects required to be recorded in AML   identified during preparation of the cabin   are eliminated prior to take-off by reporting them to the flight crew; or if such defects cannot be eliminated by the technical department due to any reason whatsoever, then they must be ensured by the technician to be recorded in the AML as a “Hold Item”. The defects detected   during the flight   and require to be recorded in AML are communicated to the flight crew as per the requirements specified in   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operation Regulations CAT.GEN.MPA.100,   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS | Instruction on the Procedures and  Principles for Air Operations ANNEX-4 Commercial Air Transportation (Chapter-CAT); the flight crew reports them to MCC through ACARS at a stage of flight when the work load allows and enters them into the AML after landing.  At an outstation , if there are the contracted maintenance organization technical employee at the aircraft, the flight crew informs the technician of the defect recorded in AML. If there is no contracted maintenance organization technician at the aircraft, the flight crew must give the station operation employee information so that they send the contracted maintenance organization employee to the aircraft in case of defects recorded in AML.  8.1.3.4. Cleaning Check in the Cabin  The cleaning checks in the cabin are performed as per   FR.71.0291 Cabin Interior Cleaning Check Form.  8.1.3.5. ASSC Implementations  Pre-flight cabin check shall be performed in order to detect any items, which do not pertain to the aircraft and which are not obtained through ordinary channels. All searches are performed in accordance with   FR.73.0001 Aircraft Security Search Checklist (ASSCL) as per the requirements specified in   EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part-A , Section 10.   Security. The search in the cabin is initiated by C/C by making announcement through PA after all ground personnel leave the aircraft (except for the ASSC implemented simultaneously with cleaning team on board narrow body aircraft). The cabin check is made by the persons identified in the chart available in the Cabin Crew Checklist. In case of the flights performed with 3 Cabin Crew Members on board A319 aircraft, the section assigned to C/A2 is divided into two equal parts and assigned to C/A1 and C/A3 by the cabin chief. The cabin check must be completed in 8 minutes in double-aisle aircraft and 6 minutes in single-aisle aircraft. Security authority of the destination country may check the compliance with ASCC during ASSC Practice carried out by the cabin crew members. The Company auditors and quality inspectors who carry out Turkish DGCA, SAFA, SANA and SACA inspections for the purpose of security inspection, are authorized to stay in the cabin during the implementation, and they must not be taken out of the aircraft.   Detailed   information   on   inspections   is   available   in   the   requirements   in   EK.10.71.001   Cabin   Crew   Manual,   Section   2. Operational Control and Monitoring. In terms of flight security; it is required to apply all articles of the ASSC, and to show the required care and seriousness to the security checks conducted upon performing passenger farewells, and to complete all checks in detail. It is important that all cabin crews pay attention to the following issues in line with the requirements in   EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part-A , Section 10.   Security: It is important to complete ASSC form upon completion of the checks, without marking beforehand. Start and end times of ASSC are required to be applied on the basis of the determined period and specified in the form as Z (UTC) time. In cases where the ASSCL is carried out by the contracted security firm or the cabin crew, there must be no one but the cabin crew, the technician, the cleaning team (in case of ASSC implemented simultaneously with cleaning team on board narrow body aircraft) in the cabin. In cases where the technical department employee is required to embark and/or work on board the aircraft, the check of the relevant area and whether any technical equipment/material has been left after the technician has left the aircraft must be done by the cabin crew responsible for the relevant area when the cabin crew is on board the aircraft, or by the security firm when the cabin crew is not on board the aircraft. In order to accelerate operational processes, for catering procurement, only 1R/2R (B737-A319-A320-A320 NEO), 1R/4R (A321- A321 NEO), 1R/2R/4R (A330-A350-B787), 1R/2R/4R/5R (B777) doors may be open. The catering personnel must be reminded not to pass to the cabin if the catering process is still continuing, and the galley region must be searched by the responsible Cabin Crew Member after the catering products have been received. In the event that the ASSC implementation is performed by the contracted firm, the relevant check is carried out by the responsible employee and the Cabin Chief is informed to establish defect record. Simultaneous Aircraft Search Implementation with Cleaning Team on Narrow Body Aircraft  The cabin crew may carry out ASSC when the cabin crews and the cleaning teams are on board the aircraft simultaneously while receiving cleaning service on board narrow body aircraft. Standard ASSC procedures are implemented in accordance with the requirements specified in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.1.3.5. ASSC Implementations in cases where the cleaning is finished or the cleaning team is not on board and on flights operated with wide body. The simultaneous implementation procedures are specified below. The cleaning teams begin to clean the aircraft from the aft; and firstly, the galley and the lavatories are cleaned. After the cleaning team has advanced by no less than 4 rows in the cabin, CA1 informs through PA that the ASSC will be started; CC writes the start time of ASSC down in   FR.73.0001 Aircraft Security Search Check List   (ASSCL). CA1 and CA2 begin to check the parts assigned to them. CC and CA3 start the security search from the section they are responsible for towards the forward galley immediately after the cleaning crew in line with the ASSCL scheme in the Cabin Crew Checklist. They must not wait for CA1 and CA2 to complete the check of the sections for which they are responsible. After completing ASSC in their assigned parts, CA1 goes to the aft galley and CA2 to the fore galley of the aircraft in order not to leave these parts empty while CC and CA3 perform their own checks. After completion of cleaning of the fore galley and lavatory, the ASSC check of the relevant sections is completed, and the finish time is written in   FR.73.0001 Aircraft Security Search Check List   (ASSCL). Additional cleaning service is not requested unless it is compulsory; the cleaning team is not called back to the aircraft.  8.1.4. Allocation of Seats to Passengers  Seat allocation is performed by ground handling employee depending on the aircraft type, number of seats, and classes indicated on the   passengers’ tickets   in   accordance   with   the   requirements   specified   in   DK.33.001   EASA | Air   Operation   Regulations AMC2 CAT.OP.MPA.165,   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air Operations ANNEX-4 Commercial Air Transportation (Chapter-CAT), and   EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part-A, Section 8.2.2.3 Allocation of Seats. Passenger seating is set out in accordance with the requirements specified in   EK.10.67.001 Ground Operation Manual (GOM), Section 1.1.4.2. Seating Order and specific principles described in this section. On board narrow-body aircraft (excluding A321, including the A321 NEO), at least 1 passenger must be seated in the seat rows aligned with the emergency exit window. This process is carried out by the ground handling employee in accordance with the requirements specified in EK.10.67.001 Ground  Operation Manual (GOM), section 1.1.4.3. Use of Emergency Exit Row Seats. Thus, the passengers are seated so as to help instead of hinder the evacuation of the aircraft when it becomes necessary to evacuate the aircraft. The number of the life vests and oxygen masks in the seat rows must not be less than the number of the passengers to sit down on the said seat row. The number of the oxygen masks available in any PSU (Passenger Service Unit) is defined in EK.10.71.003 Cabin  Crew Aircraft Types Manual. Passengers with infants must be seated on the appropriate seats in a manner not exceeding the drop oxygen masks available in any PSU (Passenger Service Unit), and the families/companions with multiple infants must be informed that their infants’ places must not be changed in such a manner that causes them to exceed the number of masks during the flight by stating also the number of the masks in their rows. Except for the infants traveling in the arms of their companions, there must be no more than one passenger on any one of the seats.  Seating and Transportation of Special Categories of Passengers (SCPs)  The procedures related to seating and transportation of the Special Categories of Passengers (SCPs) are defined in   DK.33.001 EASA |  Air Operation Regulations CAT.OP.MPA.155,   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS | Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air Operations ANNEX-4 Commercial Air Transportation (Chapter-CAT),   EK.10.67.001 Ground Operation Manual (GOM), and PR.67.021 Procedure  for Applications related to Disabled Passengers or Passengers with Reduced Mobility. Besides, the following points are taken into consideration while determining these persons' seats: They must not prevent the cabin crews from performing their duties, They must not block the access to emergency equipment, or They must not prevent the evacuation. When Special Categories of Passengers (SCPs) are to be carried on board the aircraft, the Commander must be informed in advance. The number of the Special Categories of Passengers (SCPs) carried on board the aircraft must not exceed the number of the passengers who are capable of helping them in case of an emergency. The relevant process is carried out in accordance with the requirements specified in   EK.10.67.001 Ground Operation Manual (GOM), Section 1.4.4.2.2. Special Categories of Passengers (SCPs). The Companion Passenger is the passenger who can assist the said passenger in meeting his/her personal needs throughout the flight without needing the assistance of any Cabin Crew Member, or who can lift or drag the said passenger physically to the nearest exit during emergency/evacuation (without needing the assistance of any Cabin Crew Member). The passenger who will assist a SCP during an emergency may not be another SCP; that passenger must be selected from among the passengers who travel alone without any family member or relative s/he must be responsible for during the flight. The “companion passenger” sits in the seat next to the SCP who have to travel together with companion passenger. The special categories of passengers who have to travel together with companion passenger (the special categories of passengers for   whom   there   is   companion   passenger   briefing   within   the   scope   of   QRH)   and   the   contents   of   the   briefing   given   to   the passenger/their companion are described in the Quick Reference Handlist and EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.2.4. Passenger Safety Briefing as per the requirements specified in   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operation Regulations CAT.OP.MPA.155(b). If two (2) or more SCPs travel together, there must be a companion passenger in the seat next to each SCP who needs companion passenger to assist her/him. In accordance with the requirements specified in   EK.10.67.001 Ground Operation Manual (GOM), Section 1.4.4.2.2. Special Categories of Passengers (SCPs), the companion passenger is informed by the ground handling personnel on special condition of the SCP and the companion passenger's responsibilities before boarding the aircraft, and it is ensured that the SCP travels side by side with their companion. In order that they can help in abnormal situations and emergencies, the passenger that meets the abovementioned “accompanying passenger” criteria sits in the seat next to the SCP passenger. This passenger is given the relevant briefing defined in the Quick  Reference Handlist (QRH) and EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.2.4. Passenger Safety Briefing. The principles for evacuation of passengers with reduced mobility in case of emergency are defined under the heading Selection, Duties and Briefing of Pre-Selected Passengers (PSP) in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.3.5.4 Chain of Command. The passengers who cannot carry out the necessary procedures in case of an emergency or need special assistance throughout the flight must have appropriate/competent/able-bodied companions who meet the specified requirements and will accompany them throughout the travel (they must be declared before the end of the check-in procedures). If they declare that they are capable of meeting all their needs and will not request any special service in the aircraft, such passengers are required to sign FR.67.0425  Release and Waiver of Liability Form at the check-in counter. ( FR.67.0425 Release and Waiver of Liability Form is not used for the flights to/from the USA) One copy of the said form remains with the boarding employee, one copy remains with the Cabin Chief, and one copy remains with the passenger. For detailed information on country-based implementation differences, please refer to SIS Line Information Form. Turkish Airlines or its employees are not responsible for providing such services. The companion must be able to help the said passenger in normal conditions and emergencies physically, or to carry him/her. The process of accepting and delivering special categories of passengers from the aircraft is the responsibility of the Cabin Chief. The principles of the briefing to be given to special category passengers/their escorts are available in EK.10.71.003 Cabin Crew Aircraft  Types Manual, Section 6.1 Cabin Crew Checklist Usage Guidance. The responsible Cabin Crew Members specified in the Cabin Crew Checklist shall introduce themselves and primarily help special categories of passengers with seating and tend to their needs throughout the flight. Emergency Exit Seats  In line with all requirements in   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operation Regulations AMC1 CAT.OP.MPA.165 and DK.22.096 UOD-2016/8  Passenger Allocation   in The Emergency Exit Seats, the emergency exit seats include any seat that has direct access to an exit, and direct access is defined as the ability of a passenger to access an emergency exit from their seat without having to pass through an aisle or go around an obstruction. In accordance with all requirements available in   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operation Regulations AMC1 CAT.OP.MPA.165, DK.22.115 SHT-  OPS | Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air Operations ANNEX-4 Commercial Air Transportation (Chapter-CAT),  DK.22.096 UOD-2016/8 Passenger Allocation   İn The Emergency Exit Seats, according to   PR.71.090 Procedure for Management of  Internal Documents in Cabin Operations, the seats with direct access to emergency exits must be reserved for passengers who are physically competent to ensure fast evacuation of the aircraft in emergency, strong, and willing to help during evacuation. On board narrow-body aircraft (except the A321, including the A321 Neo), the passenger seat rows aligned with the emergency exit windows shall not be left empty during the critical phases (taxi/takeoff/landing) of the flight. At least one (1) passenger is seated in these seat rows (e.g., One passenger in the ABC seat row, and one passenger in the DEF seat row) next to each emergency exit window, thus ensuring that the Emergency Exit Briefing is given as per the procedures specified in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.2.4. 8.1.4.3. Change to Passenger Classes During Flights  Cabin Crew Member is not authorized to carry out make upgrade on board; and the issues in relation to upgrading processes are determined   in   accordance   with   the   requirements   specified   in   the   Company   memorandums/announcements   and   PR.01.30.014  Procedure for Free Upgrade of Travel Class in TK Flights in accordance with IATA regulations. All upgrading processes shall be completed during the final check-in. In the event that passengers are upgraded by station officials and different catering services are offered to such passengers; the Cabin Chief fills out a cabin report on the MoCA application. Details in relation to upgraded passengers are communicated to the Commander.  8.1.4.4. Rejection of Passengers for Transportation  Turkish Airlines is entitled to reject transportation, cancel reservation, and request disembarkation from aircraft of any person who may cause anxiety by disquieting passengers due to his/her behavior and appearance. Commander makes the final decision on passenger admission. The Commander ensures the safety of all Cabin Crew Members, passengers and cargo from the moment he boards the aircraft to the moment he deboards the aircraft. The Commander is authorized to give the orders he considers necessary to ensure safety of the aircraft and the people and goods carried in the aircraft. Everybody on board the aircraft has to follow the instructions to be given by the Commander. The commander is authorized to offload the people or cargo he believes to be potentially risky for safety of the aircraft, passengers, crew and the other employee from the aircraft. The relevant points are also described in the requirements specified in   PR.02.15.001 Procedure for Restriction   Of Transportation. The persons included in the following groups cannot travel with the Company aircraft: Passengers who suffer from asthma attacks right before closing of aircraft doors, The passengers, who are required to use electrical or pneumatic tools during the flight (excluding oxygen cylinder and portable respiratory equipment provided by the Company), Unaccompanied mentally disabled (DPNA) passengers, Unruly passengers, Passengers with a contagious disease (they shall not be admitted to the flight during the communicable period under any circumstances. However, they may be admitted to the flight with the medical doctor’s report bearing the expression “There is no risk of transmission of the disease to the other passengers”.), Babies born within the first 48 hours if declared by the passenger. In case of refusal of carrying the passenger, EK.10.71.002 Cabin Crew Announcement Manual, Section 2.16.   Passengers who Embark the Wrong Aircraft/Refuse to Fly After Embarking/Denied Boarding Announcement is made to the passengers on board; after ensuring that the passengers onboard the aircraft take all their personal effects inside the cabin on their laps and show them, a security search is made inside the aircraft so as to cover everywhere likely to be accessed by the passenger who has decided not to fly at the last minute. If the passenger has cabin and/or hold baggage, it is offloaded. a) At the end of the security check, the Cabin Chief fills out   FR.71.0225 Aircraft Security Search Report for Passengers who Embark the  Wrong Aircraft/Refuse to Fly After Embarking/Denied Boarding, which is obtained from the Cabin Operations Control Supervisory, in two (2) copies. One copy of the form shall be submitted to the passenger services officer at domestic stations, and to the station official at the outstations. The second copy of the form is delivered by the Cabin Chief to the Cabin Operations Management. b) In the event that the unclaimed items/objects found during the search and check of the cabin meet the suspicious objects description (i.e., they are suspicious objects), actions are taken as per the methods defined in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 10.2.11. Unclaimed and Left (Found) Property on Board/Suspicious Object.  8.1.5. Infant-INF  According to the requirements specified in   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operation Regulations, Annex I-Definitions and EK.10.67.001 Ground  Operations Manual (GOM), 1.4.2.   Infant and Minor Passengers, an infant (INF) is the passenger who has not turned two yet (between 0 and 2 years of age) on the start date of the travel. Infants can travel with their parents or accompanying persons. An adult and an infant (INF) under the age of 2 fastened with an infant belt can be permitted to sit on a single seat. The number of infants that may be admitted to flight shall be determined depending on the number of the oxygen masks and the infant belts and infant life vests to be loaded in addition to the standard number. Infant: 1. Infants must be secured by her/his parent by being fastened with an infant belt on the passenger seat, or on the baby seat which has been attached to the passenger seat, during taxiing, take-off, landing, turbulence, and while the “fasten seat belt” light is on. 2. Infant bassinets are provided by the cabin crew for use in cruises for passengers with infants traveling in the respective seats. 3. Passengers with an infant or accompanying person shall be given infant belt and information on its use, together with infant life vest, prior to the flight. 4. Passengers with infants shall not be seated in seats with direct access to emergency exits. 5. Passengers with an infant shall be seated in compliance with the number of oxygen masks, and the parents or the accompanying persons are informed about the use of oxygen masks. 6. Passengers with an infant may be seated primarily on the window side seats, or the quadruple or triple seat row in the middle in the wide-body aircraft, excluding the seats in front of the doors. 7. Head of the infant shall face the opposite direction of the aisle at all times. Thus, the infant will be protected from any possible spillage of coffee, tea, or bottles, boxes, etc., that may be dropped from the trolley. 8. One adult is allowed to accompany one infant. In case of a request to travel with more than one infant, the first infant passenger can travel on the lap of the parent/legal guardian, and the second infant passenger in a baby car seat/infant carrier, provided by the passenger, secured on a separate seat with the seat belt, or the baby must be accompanied by a second person. 9. The infant passengers must be accompanied. 10. Infants who will travel on the companion's arms shall be provided with an infant belt and an infant life vest. Passengers may bring their baby car seats or bag-type bassinets with them, provided that they comply with certain requirements.  Infant car seat   is used for infants under the age of two. The bassinet is required to be 40X40 cm to be attached to the cabin seat available on board the aircraft, and have its own belt. At all phases of the flight, infant car seats shall be fastened to the seats with the safety belts securely and prevented from leaning forward. In cases where they are not used, they must be stored safely. It is necessary to check that they are in upright position as long as the belt warning lights are on.  Bag-Type Travel Bassinets   shall be used when the seatbelt warning lights are off. Their sizes shall not exceed 70X30 cm.  Infant Carrier/Car Seat;  1. In accordance with the requirements specified in   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operation Regulations AMC1 CAT.IDE.A.205 and DK.22.115  SHT-OPS | Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air Operations ANNEX-4 Commercial Air Transportation (Chapter-CAT), if the infant carrier/car seat shall be used in all flight phases which require keeping the seat belts fastened, the child/infant must be secured with belts of the infant carrier/car seat, and the backrest of the seat must be upright. 4. If the backrest of the seat cannot be made upright due to structure of the infant carrier/car seat, it is necessary to secure the infant on his/her companion's lap with infant belt, and the child on his/her own seat with the seatbelt, and to place the infant carrier/car seat into the overhead bin, if it fits in, or otherwise, to send it to the cargo. The ground employee must issue baggage tag for the infant carrier/car seat sent to the cargo. 5. In cases where they are not used, they must be stored safely. They shall submit the third (3.) copy to Cabin Crew Directorate when they return from the duty.  Seat of Accompanying Cabin Crew Members  The accompanying cabin crew member shall be seated on the seat allocated for them. A seat shall be definitely allocated for any accompanied child passenger. The accompanying cabin crew member and the child passenger must be seated side by side. No seat by the emergency exit is given. Sick, Pregnant Passengers, Passengers with Reduced Mobility (PRM), MAAS (Meet and Assist) and Passengers on Stretchers  The ground handling agents are responsible for performance of processes in relation to admission of sick passengers, pregnant passengers, passengers with reduced mobility, mentally disabled passengers and similar passengers into the aircraft, and the station managers shall be responsible for adoption of the final decision in respect of ensuring the travel of such passengers. Persons with Reduced Mobility (PRMs), are the passengers with congenital physical and/or mental illnesses, or the passengers with acquired incapacity for any reason whatsoever, and needing more attention and medical assistance than other passengers during the flight operation. Detailed information about the procedures for admitting and carrying such passengers, and the passengers on stretchers is available in the requirements in   EK.10.67.001 Ground Operation Manual (GOM), Section 1.4.4.2. Categories of Disabled Passenger or Passenger with Reduced Mobility. The principles for evacuation of passengers with reduced mobility in case of emergency are available under the heading Selection, Duties and Briefing of Pre-Selected Passengers (PSP) in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.3.5.4 Chain of Command. Evacuation of passengers with reduced mobility in case of any emergency is performed after all passengers are evacuated. The station officials shall make the passenger with reduced mobility sign   FR.67.0425 Release and Waiver of Liability Form stating that s/he accepts and declares that s/he can meet all her/his needs alone without the need for a companion, and that s/he will not demand any special service beyond the standard services throughout the travel, including also the emergencies. FR.67.0425 Release and  Waiver of Liability Form shall not be used for the flights to/from the United States of America. In accordance with TL.10.67.004 General  Instruction on Admittance of Disabled and Sick Passengers, in cases where the passengers travel by connection flights, the passenger must be regarded as admitted to the flight by our Company, and no document must be demanded again in relation to admission of that passenger to the flight at the transit stations. The final decision on the continuation of the travels of the passengers who have come from the station of origin of the flight to the intermediate station shall be taken by the station manager. The station official coordinates any required services and equipment (wheelchairs, lift, etc.) in accordance with the regulations of the Company in relation to carrying any sick passengers and the passengers with reduced mobility through the flights of the Company. Sick passengers, or passengers with partially or completely reduced mobility and MAAS passengers are allowed to stay on board the aircraft during transit waiting periods upon agreement of related departments. The Cabin Crew Members inform and guide the sick passengers and passengers with reduced mobility with regard to reaching the lavatories, placing their items and servicing food/beverage/passenger comfort materials (opening the lid/bag, etc.) in the cabin during the flight. Any information transfer in relation to delays, announcements for in-flight service and connecting flights in respect of hearing- impaired passengers is performed by the cabin crew visually/in writing. The briefing and the scope of the briefing to be given to the passengers with reduced mobility and their companions before the flight are available in the   Quick Reference Handlist (QRH). After starting the boarding, priority must be given to disabled passengers or passengers with reduced mobility, if possible; and they must be disembarked after all passengers deboarded after landing of the aircraft, if possible. The cabin crews ensure the necessary coordination with ground employee during admission of any passengers with reduced mobility and any passengers with wheelchair into the aircraft; and any irregularities that occurred in respect of handing over of such passengers are reported to the Cabin Operation Management through e-form/DCMS/e-mail.  If it is necessary to carry any sick passenger with cabin wheelchair during the flight, the following actions shall be taken:  The wheelchair shall be brought next to the sick passenger. Brakes of wheelchair shall be locked. Foot rest of the wheelchair shall be opened towards the sides. A Cabin Crew Member shall grasp the legs of the sick passenger; and the other Cabin Crew Member shall cross the arms, and shall lift passenger from the armpits. Sick passenger shall be seated on the wheelchair, and the feet of the passenger shall be placed into the foot rest. Safety belt shall be fastened in a manner that the arms will be crossed. The brakes of the wheelchair shall be unlocked. Sick passenger shall be covered, and attention shall be paid to their privacy. LEGL:   Passengers who are considered to have partially reduced mobility due to their left broken legs, and who are able to walk by themselves by use of crutches.  LEGR:   Passengers who are considered to have partially reduced mobility due to their right broken leg, and who are able to walk by themselves by use of crutches. Deterioration of a Passenger's Health Status During Flight  The Cabin Chief is required to check through the MoCA application, during the ground preparations, whether there is any physician on board; and if any passenger/crew member on board becomes sick, injured, etc., assistance shall be requested from the passengers whose names are prefixed with the title Doctor (Smiling Doctors). In case where a passenger gets sick and the physician (Smiling Doctors), available on board, rejects to assist the medical needs of the relevant passenger, or it is found on the MoCA application that there is no physician passenger; cabin crew members shall promptly conduct an announcement for a physician and inform the Cabin Chief and flight crew members of the incident through interphone. Any medical intervention shall be performed by volunteer passengers on board, who have a "Medical Doctor" degree. If there is any passenger who declares that s/he is a Medical Doctor verbally and volunteers to perform a medical intervention on the passenger but fails to show any ID during the flight, action is taken as per the decision of the Commander. All principles of the implementation are defined in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 14.1. Emergency Medical Kit. Cabin crew may neither administer any medicine nor perform any medical intervention; they may only assist the doctor. In cases where no physician is available, cabin crew shall apply first aid to the sick passenger after receiving approval from their companion, if any. The patient shall be kept under surveillance by a Cabin Crew Member during the flight. If the first aid being applied on the sick passenger/crew member requires not to move her/him, the landing can be made performed while the patient is being kept at their then current position upon the Commander's decision after the assessment made by a doctor, if there is one aboard the aircraft, or solely upon the Commander's decision, if there is no doctor aboard the aircraft. In such a case, the cabin crew takes all measures required to ensure that the passenger can land safely. In cases where the patient is given basic life support (CPR), if the basic life support (CPR) will be continued during the landing, the Commander informs the cabin crew of the passenger door/exit to be left empty in accordance with the requirements specified in   EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part-A, Section 8.3.14.4 Procedures to be Followed in the Event of Incapacitation of a Cabin Crew Member In-Flight. On the flights performed with the number of cabin crews included in Table-1: Minimum Cabin Crew Composition Table in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 4.2. Number and Composition of Cabin Crew, as per article “Continue applying basic life support treatment to the ill/injured person until her/his vital signs are observed again or until medical assistance arrives. Do not interrupt basic life support under any circumstances even during landing.” in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 14.12. Basic Life Support, the door is blocked, PSP is selected, and manual passenger safety briefing is performed in accordance with the requirements in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 4.3. Reduction of Cabin Crew under Unpredictable Conditions (Incapacity or Failure to complete Cabin Crew Number) during Ground/Flight Operations outside Main Base . If there is any passenger on board the aircraft, whose health deteriorates, the flight crew is informed through the interphone of the passenger's seat number, age, gender, name-surname, the exit to which he is near, if landing will be necessary. If a passenger's health deteriorates at a degree that requires urgent medical intervention during the flight, the aircraft may be diverted to an airport deemed appropriate by the Commander. After the landing, EK.10.71.002 Cabin Crew Announcement Manual , Section 2.18. Announcement for Prioritized Disembarkation of the Sick Passenger is made to the passengers. Passengers Under Arrest  The requirements that must be observed on board regarding a passenger to be transported under arrest are as follows; 1. Passengers under arrest shall be accompanied by a security guard/guards at all times during the flight (convicted passengers with "Permission Certificate for Convicted Passengers" can be admitted on board without a security guard at domestic flights). 2. Matches or lighters carried by such passengers shall be confiscated prior to their boarding process. 3. They shall be embarked before all other passengers and disembarked last. 4. Passengers under arrest shall be seated in the seats with direct access emergency exits. 5. No alcoholic beverage shall be served to the passenger under arrest and their security guard. 6. The passenger under arrest shall not be permitted to speak with other passengers throughout the flight. 7. Handcuffed persons under arrest cannot be transported as passengers, except for decision of the Commander and special circumstances (he is accompanied by escort(s) whose number is determined by the relevant governmental agency). Serving Alcoholic Beverages to Passengers  Consumption of Alcoholic Beverages on Board by Passengers and Serving Alcoholic Beverages  Consumption   of   alcoholic   beverages   and   serving   them   on   board   shall   be   arranged   in   accordance   with   Company   regulations. Passengers shall not be permitted to drink their own alcoholic beverages on board. Such passenger is warned that their behavior is violating the regulations of the Company. However, the passenger disregarding such warning and continuing to drink cannot be physically restrained by the crew members. Completely drunk passengers may pose hazard for themselves and the other passengers on board. In case of an abnormal situation or emergency, the intoxicated passengers will have difficulty in responding, cooperating and fulfilling the instructions in case of evacuation of the aircraft. The Cabin Chief has the authority to decide whether to serve further alcoholic beverages to a passenger under the influence of alcohol or not, within the knowledge of the Commander. All cabin crew members are informed when no further alcoholic beverage is to be served to a passenger. The   passengers   who   are   no   more   served   alcoholic   drinks   within   the   scope   of   the   “Traffic   Lights   Practices   –   Behavioral Categorization”, The Deportee, INAD, persons subject to legal proceedings (suspects, the accused, arrestees, convicts) and the security officer(s) accompanying such passengers, and passengers under the age of 18 (even if their parents request to do so) shall not be served alcoholic beverages. The following Table-7: Traffic Lights Practices - Behavioral Categorization Table is used to identify potential hazards that may be caused by alcohol-consuming passengers and to classify the behavioral procedures in these situations. Transportation of Loads  Hand Baggage (Unregistered Baggage)  In line with all requirements in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.3. Cabin Abnormal Situation/Emergency Operation Implementations,   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS | Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air Operations ANNEX-4 Commercial Air Transportation   (Chapter-CAT),   and   DK.22.097   Carry-on   Hand   Baggage   Directive,   Cabin   Baggage   (Unregistered   Baggage/Hand Baggage) shall be placed in the overhead bins in a manner not to violate flight safety and security, or underneath the passenger seats in a manner not to move in the cabin and cause any injuries to the passengers. If the hand baggage admitted to the cabin is placed underneath the front seat by the passenger, it shall be made sure that its size is suitable to fit there and to stay stable. The cabin baggage must not be left on the passenger's lap, or on the floor in an unsafe manner, or on the passenger seat (except Cabin Seat Baggage [CBBG]), or in a manner protruding towards the aisle; and the cabin crew must provide guidance for correct placement of the passenger items/baggage.* 1. Hand baggage (23x40x55 cm) that can be placed inside the overhead bins shall not exceed 8 kg. The Station Officials ensure that all hand baggage to be carried in the cabin by the passengers meet the relevant dimension and weight conditions. The hand baggage right is for 2 pieces of hand baggage for B/C passengers and 1 piece for Y/C passengers and infants within the age range of 0-2. 2. In the Company's flights, it is requested from the passengers by the check-in employee to present all cabin baggage, and passengers are informed that untagged hand baggage shall not be accepted on board. The cabin baggage of the business class passengers must be tagged with black cabin baggage tags and those of the Y/C class passengers with red cabin baggage tags. 3. Practices regarding cabin baggage/personal belongings and their placement in the aircraft during passenger boarding and passenger settlement are carried out as per   TL.60.001 Cabin Baggage Acceptance Instruction. 4. In the event that any hand baggage not of appropriate dimension/weight is detected during boarding; cabin crew shall provide required information to the passenger; after which it shall be found out whether any onward flight will be attended or not, and the baggage shall be ensured to be loaded to the cargo compartment and tagged accordingly by giving the details of such passenger in relation to her/his onward flight to the ground handling employee. 5. The baggage and items in the cabin must be placed in a manner not obstructing a potential evacuation in front of the emergency exits and in the aisles during taxiing, landing, take-off and any stage of the flight deemed necessary by the Commander. Locations of the hand baggage in the cabin must not block the vision of the cabin crew and their access to emergency equipment, either. In the course of taxiing, passengers shall not continue to place hand baggage, the overhead bins must be closed, and there must be no passenger on foot. 6. All baggage on board, which may cause injury or damage or block the aisles and exits when their places are changed, must be placed in a manner not preventing the movement. All baggage placed under the seat shall be placed in a manner that will not obstruct the exit of a passenger. The placed baggage must not harm the passengers. If it is detected that the “baggage bar/restraint bar” under the passenger seat is defective or broken, baggage is not placed there, and the defect is recorded. 7. Depending on the flight phase, prior to take-off and landing, if the belt warning lights are on, or in any case instructed by the Commander, baggage shall be placed in such a way that it does not prevent the evacuation of passengers, causing injury by fall or otherwise and necessary controls shall be carried out accordingly. 8. Hand baggage of passengers seated on the emergency exit row or in front of the separator shall not be held on their laps or left on the floor or passenger seats in an insecure manner to block the aisle; and such passengers shall be instructed by the cabin crew to place their items/baggage in accordance with the rules. Carry-on baggage of the passengers shall be placed inside the overhead bins before take-off and landing by informing the passenger, and the carry-on baggage needed by the passenger during cruise shall be returned to the passenger. * 9. Cabin Seat Baggage (CBBG), Cabin Seat Baggage (CBBG) are the baggage carried on the seat with the passengers against a fee. Generally, such baggage is included in the following definitions. Cabin seat baggage: Musical instruments, Works of art, Electronic equipment, Diplomatic baggage, Valuable article or baggage. In line with such information, the following rules apply: a) A ticket is issued for the paid baggage to be carried in the cabin. b) One (1) piece of baggage shall be accepted per seat. c) Maximum weight of the baggage must not exceed 75 kg. d) It must not limit the access to or use of any emergency exit/door or aisle in the cabin. e) The CBBG (Cabin Seat Baggage) is given the window seat and the baggage owner passenger is given the seat next to it. f) The CBBG (Cabin Seat Baggage) is not given seat with direct access emergency exits. g) The CBBG (Cabin Seat Baggage) must fit into a single seat, be positioned in the seat so as not to block the cabin crew’s vision in the cabin, and securable with an additional extension belt if necessary; and it must be placed, immobilized and secured on the seat by using an extension belt to prevent its possible slipping under all normal flight and ground operation conditions. h) The procedures relating to checking that the cabin seat baggage has been packaged so as to prevent any potential injury to the Cabin Crew Members and the passengers and its admission into the cabin are available in   EK.10.67.001 Ground Operation Manual  (GOM), Section 1.1.6.12.1. Cabin Seat Baggage (CBBG). i) Its height must not prevent the passengers from seeing the warning signs and the emergency lights. j) If a cello is to be carried as cabin seat baggage, it must be positioned on the cabin floor in front of and leaning against the window seat and secured with an additional extension belt in a manner not blocking any potential evacuation and the cabin crew's vision. k) The cabin crew confirms that CBBG has been secured as specified above. Diplomatic baggage below 20 kg is carried free of charge inside the cabin; any baggage exceeding 20 kg is carried as cabin seat baggage (CBBG). The cabin seat baggage must be secured and tied in such a manner as not to block the evacuation and the cabin crew's vision. The Cabin Chief must share the valuable baggage information with the entire cabin crew at the earliest opportunity, it must not be requested at any stage of the flight that the baggage is removed from the seat purchased, the baggage must be observed throughout the flight, and the passengers must be supported as necessary during boarding/deboarding of passengers. 11. In cases where the used injector is not kept by the passenger; cabin crew shall place the injector inside a medical waste bin, available in the first aid kit, while protecting themselves by putting on gloves. 17. It is ensured that the hand baggage of the passengers is placed in the overhead bin by giving the necessary information before take- off and landing, and the passengers are informed by the cabin crew that they can access the relevant hand baggage if they desire so during cruise. Service Dogs (SVAN)  The practices relating to the service dogs are described in   PR.60.005 Procedure for Carriage of Live Animals. The ground handling employee checks the necessary documents of the service dogs and their owners to be admitted into the aircraft. The service dogs are made sit down at the feet of their owners throughout the entire flight so as not to affect the cabin hygiene negatively. When there is no infant passenger, the service dogs may be taken to seats where bassinets can be attached in aircraft with double corridors. It is not mandatory to muzzle the service dogs while admitting them into the cabin. These dogs may be admitted to flights without muzzle, but against the possibility of any problem, the passenger traveling with SVAN must carry a muzzle with them. In the event that the dog to be carried as SVAN barks, bares its teeth, etc., muzzling of the dog may be demanded. The relevant passenger is responsible for the damage such animal might cause during the flight. In the event that dogs cannot fit the place in the aircraft, the place of passenger and dog are changed within the scope of requirements in this chapter. There is no number limitation in the cabin for the dogs to be carried as SVAN during the flights to the United States of America; they are not included in Table-8: Quota on Pets to be carried in Cabin available in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.1.12. While PSAN can be transported in the cabin only in the United States of America line as service dog without a cage, in all other lines outside the USA, it can be carried in the cabin as PETC or in the cargo section as AVIH. Detailed principles of implementation relating to traveling with SVAN are available in   PR.60.005 Procedure For Carriage Of Live Animals. Rescue Dog: They are the dogs trained to locate the isolated people and search & rescue the individual(s) predicted to be alive during disasters and emergencies. Passengers with live animals (PETC) are seated in the window seats so that live animals transported in the cabin do not become an obstacle in emergency evacuation situations. The passenger services employee must give the passengers traveling with pets in the cabin seats in the rows that are behind the other seat rows so that such passengers can secure the cages. The live animal cage must not be placed in the places such as overhead bin, coatroom, etc., but instead kept with the passenger and placed under the seat in front of the passenger. Therefore, these passengers are not allowed in the rows with an emergency exit and door or even the window seats in the rows where infant bassinets can be attached; but the service dogs can be allowed to the seats where infant bassinets can be attached on board double-aisle aircraft if there is no infant passenger. The pets carried in the cabin must be placed on every fifth row. That the Cabin Chief receives the Commander's approval to close the door through the interphone means that the check of openness of all emergency exit routes as well as the following cabin preparation items will have been completed no later than “the first movement of the aircraft”. If the passenger seating and baggage placement is going on while receiving approval to close the door, the Cabin Chief informs the PIC of the situation. After closing the doors as per the requirements in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.2.3. Procedures for Opening – Closing the Door, the slides are “armed” before the first movement of the aircraft. It is checked that all passengers have sat down in their seats. In the cabin baggage placement process that starts with admission onboard of passengers, the overhead bins are closed, and it is checked that the passengers and the cabin hand baggage have been placed properly. If there is still passenger on foot and/or open overhead bin before or after the first movement of the aircraft, the cabin crew takes the measures related to the passengers’ being seated and placement of the baggage properly and/or the Cabin Chief makes EK.10.71.002 Cabin Crew Announcement Manual, Section 2.1. Push-Back Warning Announcement and informs the Commander of the situation by interphone when necessary.
