Passenger Count  With the exception of the stations specified by announcement or SIS Line Information Form, passengers are not counted at airports that have gate reader and where the passengers board the aircraft through the boarding bridge. On board the aircraft parked in the remote parking positions, and on the transit flights whose passengers wait inside the cabin, the passengers are counted absolutely. If the aircraft is in the remote parking position, the passengers are counted after completion of the passenger boarding process and "Boarding Completed" announcement. Passenger count, which is carried out under the responsibility of the cabin crew, is performed simultaneously after confirming that lavatories are vacant, by two (2) Cabin Crew Members in narrow body aircraft and by the number of cabin crew members specified by the Cabin Chief in wide body aircraft. The Commander, the Cabin Chief or the ground handling employee may require a passenger count in the cabin in case of any suspicion and/or necessity. The cabin crew shall take no more than three (3) counts. For security reasons, before closing the doors of the aircraft for take-off, the number of the passengers who have passed through the boarding gate must be equal to the number of the passengers on board the aircraft.  If there are more passengers than listed:   If there are more passengers than listed according to the result of the third (3.) count, the station official conducts a check on board the aircraft by matching the passengers’ boarding passes with their identity details on the basis of the requirements specified in   EK.10.67.001 Ground Operation Manual (GOM), Section 1.1.7.3. Passenger Discrepancy in Boarding. The cabin crew provide support in case of need. If extra passengers are detected, the necessary actions shall be taken by the passenger services. It shall be ensured that all security measures demanded by the Commander are taken. In the event of excess passengers and disembarking of the relevant passenger from the aircraft, the principles in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 10.2.10 Security Measures to be taken for Passengers who Embark the Wrong Aircraft/Refuse to Fly After Embarking/Denied Boarding shall be applied by the cabin crew.  If there are less passengers than listed:   If there are fewer passengers than listed according to the result of the third (3.) count, the station official conducts a check on board the aircraft by matching the passengers’ boarding passes with their identity details on the basis of the requirements specified in   EK.10.67.001 Ground Operation Manual (GOM), Section 1.1.7.3. Passenger Discrepancy in Boarding, and the cabin crew provide support if needed. The passenger's baggage, if any, in the cargo is offloaded from the aircraft. It shall be ensured that all security measures demanded by the Commander are taken. The Cabin Chief informs the final pax to the Cabin Crew Members. Deboarding of passengers shall be commenced after the approval of the Commander and the ground handling employee only. The flight crew shall not initiate deboarding of passengers until the ground handling employee ensures that the stairs or boarding bridge processes have been completed, and that the ground equipment does not pose any danger. The Cabin Crew Members stay inside the aircraft until all passengers deboard. However, if there is any passenger with reduced mobility or special category passenger, the minimum number of cabin crew members who are ready in the cabin during deboarding of passengers shall not be less than the numbers specified in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 4.3. Reduction of Cabin Crew under Unpredictable Conditions (Incapacity or Failure to complete Cabin Crew Number) during Ground/Flight Operations outside Main Base . Cabin crew shall confirm to the ground handling employee and the flight crew that all passengers have left the aircraft, and that there is no item left on board. At transit airports, if crew change is necessary while there are passengers on board the aircraft, the flight and cabin crews may disembark the aircraft, provided that the minimum number of cabin crew members specified in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 4.3. Reduction of Cabin Crew under Unpredictable Conditions (Incapacity or Failure to complete Cabin Crew Number) during Ground/Flight Operations outside Main Base stay on board the aircraft. Delays Attributable to Cabin Crew Members  In order to avoid any delay due to late performance of the passenger boarding announcement, the cabin crew is required to carry out the points in accordance with the requirements specified in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.1.1 Duty Commencement. In order not to cause delay due to cleaning, the required checks shall be performed before the cleaning team leaves the aircraft, or in a manner not to require calling back the cleaning team to the aircraft again as per   TL.10.60.004 General Instruction on Cleaning Services in Aircraft. The cleaning-related irregularities detected later on are reported by the Cabin Chief through the tablet PC. In order to avoid any delay, the passenger count started by the cabin crew upon the “Boarding Completed” announcement must not exceed the following maximum counting periods determined by the aircraft types: Six (6) minutes for B777 aircrafts. Five (5) minutes for BA330/A350/B787 aircrafts. Two (2) minutes for A321 NEO/321/320/320 NEO/319 and B737 aircraft Loading and unloading of catering products while welcoming or seeing off passengers may be performed under supervision of an authorized Cabin Chief/Cabin Crew Member after closing the galley curtain so as not to prevent boarding of passengers. Cabin crews must leave the catering service doors open with a safety band on them after obtaining the approval of the flight crew while leaving the aircraft. If the safety strap is not functional, the door is not opened when there is no boarding bridge, stairs, or catering vehicle in front of the doors. Cabin Chiefs are required to limit their debriefing periods to maximum three minutes inside the aircraft in order not to exceed the ground times, delay the connection flights and hinder the operations. A longer debriefing can be conducted at the discretion of the Cabin Chief at a location outside the aircraft that is deemed appropriate considering the time remaining before the connection flight. In order to prevent the cabin-crew-process-induced delays while the passengers are on board, boarding, or deboarding the aircraft, attention is paid to carry out the operational processes in coordination with the station officials especially at the intermediate points. Cabin Chiefs shall note down the time on which the crew members aboard the aircraft, and such time shall be confirmed with the operations coordinator. In all flights, while the aircraft door is being closed, it is necessary to reach an agreement with the operations coordinator by asking whether there is any delay caused by the cabin crew and learn the code of the delay if there is such delay. If any delay coded “66” or “68” is entered as caused by the cabin crew, or in case of any contradiction in the time of cabin crew boarding noted down by the operations coordinator; such delay or contradiction is required to be communicated to Cabin Crew Directorate by use of the electronic reporting system in no later than forty-eight (48) hours from departure.  8.1.15. Cabin Disinsection  The information on the lines for which the cabin will be disinsected and the application methods/places of disinsection is provided by Cabin Crew Directorate through SIS Line Information Form. Prior to disinsection in cabin, EK.10.71.002 Cabin Crew Announcement Manual, Section 2.19. Disinsection Announcement is made to warn the passengers to cover their eyes and faces. If they are demanded, the empty spray boxes are delivered to the ground employee at the landing station. The detailed information on disinfection/disinsection of aircraft is available in the requirements in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 14.31. Disinfection and Disinsection of Aircraft.  8.1.16. Weight/Balance Calculations  For each flight, the weight and balance calculations shall only be performed by the authorized employee manually by completing the Loadsheet or automatically through the Departure Control System (DCS). Detailed information is available in   EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part-A, Section 8.1.8.5 Mass and Balance Data Documentation and   EK.10.67.001 Ground Operations Manual (GOM), Section 5.4.3. Duties in the Weight and Balance Calculation Process. The Loadsheet shall match with the final situation regarding passenger seating on board in order to ensure flight safety. In order to ensure the flight safety, the passengers are required to sit down on their own seats during take-off and landing. If it is observed that numerous passengers have changed their places after the take-off (forward to aft, aft to forward), they must be informed that the passengers must sit down on their own seats again for landing. Fueling  Refueling and Defueling when Passengers Embarking, Onboard or Disembarking  Refueling/defueling when passengers embarking, onboard or disembarking is started only when the captain pilot permits, and the following additional measures are taken: 1. While refueling and defueling when passengers embarking, onboard or disembarking, one Flight Crew Member stays in the cockpit. 2. The minimum number of Cabin Crew Members defined in   EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part-A, Section 4.1.2.1. Number and Composition of Cabin Crew and EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 4.2. Number and Composition of Cabin Crew stay on board the aircraft. 3. In case of refueling or defueling when passengers onboard, the ground handling activities or the works inside the aircraft such as catering, cleaning are carried out in such a manner as neither to cause danger nor obstruct the evacuation to be made from aisles/exits in case of emergency. 4. All doors except for the main entrance door(s) used for passenger de/boarding are kept closed, provided that their slides are disarmed; if they are open, there are boarding stairs/bridges in front of all open doors. 5. In case of emergency, passengers shall be evacuated through at least two main passenger doors (determined by the Commander within the scope of the “briefing” to be performed together with the Cabin Chief and the ground employee who will carry out the refueling) (or the main passenger door and one emergency exit). 6. In order to ensure that the designated emergency evacuation exits and the area (such as boarding bridge/stairs) on the escape route are cleared of obstructions, the passengers board and deboard the aircraft through the door and boarding bridge/stairs (in single file and without clogging) under the supervision of the ground employee and in a controlled manner in accordance with the requirements defined in   EK.10.67.001 Ground Operation Manual (GOM), Section 3.2. Safety during Refueling/Defueling. 7. Between the ground employee supervising the refueling or defueling process and the flight crew on board the aircraft, two-way communication is established through the aircraft communication system and maintained throughout the refueling or defueling process. 8. The public address (PA) system is kept functioning. 9. There must be electricity on board the aircraft. 10. The crew, employee, and the passengers are informed that refueling or defueling is to be commenced. 11. In case of Boeing aircraft, defueling when passengers embarking, onboard or disembarking is forbidden. 12. Crew change is not allowed during refueling/defueling when passengers are on board the aircraft. The refueling/defueling process is started when the fuel hose is connected to the aircraft and completed when it is disconnected from the aircraft. 13. On board aircraft that has PED power, the switch is brought to “off” position. (A) Responsibility 1) Responsibilities of the Commander: Before commencement of refueling/defueling, the commander gives the Cabin Chief and the ground employee a briefing on the following subjects: - S/he determines which exits are to be used for rapid deplaning or emergency evacuation of the passengers, and informs the cabin crew of these exits. S/he reminds the cabin crew to clear such exits and aisles of obstructions, and the ground employee supervising the refueling/defueling process to keep the apron area under the aircraft clear. - S/he informs the cabin crew of the anticipated duration of the refueling/defueling process. Cabin Flight Operation implementations  8.2.1. Flight Crew/Cabin Crew Communication  In the flight operation process, it is necessary to ensure effective communication and coordination between the flight crew and the cabin crew in normal/abnormal situations by considering the critical stages of the flight and the sterile cockpit principles. In this context, it is necessary to use the common terminology and communication language in the in-flight communication, and the procedures of use of E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 141 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250

the in-flight communication devices must be observed. All cabin crews must be responsive to any kind of announcement and/or audio/visual warnings (chimes) that may be received from the cabin and the flight crew.  Critical Flight Phases:   Take-off run, take-off flight path, final approach, missed approach, landing, landing roll, and the other phases of the flight as determined by the Commander.  Sterile Cockpit  The sterile cockpit means that, as specified in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 10.2.5. Cockpit Security and EK.10.73.001  Operation Manual Part-A, Section 8.3.10.4 Sterile Flight Crew Compartment, the cabin crew neither calls the flight crew nor enters the cockpit at critical phases of the flight, even for cockpit briefing, in order to avoid any distraction of the flight crew, except for the force majeure circumstances in relation to flight safety, security, and the first aid. The Commander ensures that the sterile cockpit procedures are implemented throughout the following phases of the flight: 1. Throughout push-back, engine start-up, and taxiing, 2. During the critical phases of flight, 3. Below 10,000 ft above the aerodrome of departure after take-off and the aerodrome of destination before landing, except for cruise flight, and 4. During any other phase of flight determined by the Commander. Cockpit   stay   shall   be   limited   to   maximum   5   minutes,   except   for abnormal/emergency situations and briefing by the flight crew/Cabin Chiefs and cabin crew member shall avoid interrupting radio conversation. In order to avoid touching the flight controls inadvertently, the Cabin Crew Members shall not sit in the seats allocated to the Flight Crew Members (except for the abnormal situations or emergencies when they are demanded to do so by the Flight Crew Members). When s/he is in the cockpit, a Cabin Crew Member may sit on the observer seat if that seat is vacant and the Flight Crew Members deem it necessary that the Cabin Crew Member be seated there. Cabin Warning Systems and Communication  Flight crew informs cabin crew with the warning lights and PA in order to ensure flight security and safety at all phases of the flight. Detailed information about the subject is available in the requirements in   EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part-A, Section 8.3. Flight Procedures. Ordinance Signs; a) Fasten Seat Belt Sign b) No Smoking Sign c) Return to Seat Sign d) No Portable Electronic Device Sign and No Mobile Sign  a. Fasten Seat Belt Sign  The passengers are instructed to fasten their seat belts through the fasten seat belt signs and/or the announcement system. As long as the fasten seat belt signs are on at all phases of the flight and at all flight operation phases deemed necessary by the Commander, all passengers (infants included), including also the passengers seated on the vacant jump seats, must be seated and fastened. When deemed necessary for the flight safety (for example, Turbulence, abnormal situation) the Cabin Chief informs the Commander that all passengers (infants included) are seated and fastened by interphone in line with the requirements specified in   EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part-A, Section 8.3 Flight Procedures. The principles of implementation in relation to the cabin ready report and the situations in which the cabin crew members can stand up during taxiing are available in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.2.5. “Cabin Ready Report” before Takeoff/Landing.  On the ground:   Seat belt signs shall be set in "OFF" position during passenger boarding and/or when transit passengers are onboard. The earliest time for the cabin crew to turn the fasten seat belt signs “ON” before the aircraft starts to taxi from the push- back or parking position is when the last passenger has boarded the aircraft.  Before take-off:   The cabin crew gives the “Cabin Ready Report” to the Cabin Chief in line with the “Cabin Ready Report Check Items” in the Cabin Crew Checklist and EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.2.5 “Cabin Ready Report” before Take- Off/Landing. The flight crew warns the cabin crew by making the “CABIN CREW BE SEATED FOR TAKE-OFF” announcement. In cases where the taxiing for take-off will take shorter than expected, the Commander gives information to the Cabin Chief. When the flight crew is delivered the cabin ready report, the crew members and the passengers must be seated and fastened.  After take-off:   The passengers shall remain seated with safety belts fastened until seat belt signs are switched off. After the takeoff, depending on the block time and the weather conditions, the “Fasten Seat Belts” lights are turned first “OFF” then “ON” while passing the airport altitude plus 5,000 feet at the earliest, and the Cabin Crew Members are thus enabled to start the service. All passengers are warned through an announcement to keep their seat belts fastened while seated. In accordance with the sterile cockpit practice, the first contact between the flight crew and the Cabin Crew Members is established by the flight crew through the interphone. However, if this contact is not made within 20 minutes following turning “OFF” and “ON” the “Fasten Seat Belts” lights, E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 143 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250

the Cabin Chief gives the Flight Crew Members information about the cabin safety and the passenger situation by “interphone” at the earliest opportunity.  During descending:   When the seatbelt signs are turned on by the flight crew (no later than while passing the airport altitude plus 15,000 ft on board narrow-body aircraft, or the airport altitude plus 20,000 ft on board wide-body aircraft), the descent announcement is made to the passengers from the cabin, and all the cabin preparations are completed. The cabin crew gives the “Cabin Ready Report” to the Cabin Chief in line with the “Cabin Ready Report Check Items” in the Cabin Crew Checklist and EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.2.5 “Cabin Ready Report” before Take-Off/Landing. The Cabin Chief delivers the cabin ready report to the flight crew either verbally by interphone, or by keying cabin ready on the handset, or by pressing the “Cabin Ready” button if there is any on board the aircraft. The means of communication between the cockpit and the cabin are defined in all requirements in  EK.10.71.003 Cabin Crew Aircraft Types Manual. The cockpit shall not be entered physically to deliver the cabin ready report. Additionally, cabin crew members shall keep their seat belts fastened whenever instructed and warned to do so by the Commander.  b. Note: The No Smoking warning may be a sticker/placard on board aircraft.  c. No Portable Electronic Device Sign and No Mobile Sign  Some aircraft in our fleet is equipped with the “No Portable Electronic Device (No PED) Sign” and/or “No Mobile Sign” next to the “Fasten Seat Belt” sign. In our aircraft with “No Portable Electronic Device (No PED) Sign” and/or “No Mobile Sign” warning, the warning lights related to the use of electronic devices are intervened by the flight crew. When the seatbelt warning signs are turned “ON” in case of turbulence, there is no need to turn the “No Portable Electronic Device (No PED) Sign” and/or “No Mobile Sign” warning “ON”. In cases where the Commander restricts the use of PED with the intention of preserving the flight safety and security, the relevant warnings shall be made “ON”. The warning signs must be monitored by the cabin crews throughout the flight, and they must remind the flight crews when necessary.  8.2.3. Procedures for Opening/Closing the Door  If they are present on board the aircraft, primarily the cabin crew, the flight crew, and technical employee are authorized/responsible for opening/closing the aircraft door. In cases where the assigned cabin crew, flight crew and/or technical employee are not present on board   the   aircraft,   the   operations   coordinator,   the   cleaning   team   foreman,   passenger   handling   employee,   outstation   company employee, and airport security employee, trained and certified on opening-closing the aircraft doors, may also open and close the cabin doors internally and externally. In all aircraft types; All doors can be opened by the Cabin Crew Members [except for the inexperienced cabin crew members who have not completed their flight period of minimum three months] assigned to the aircraft regardless of the door responsibility, during the normal ground operation process (or the reasons such as catering loading, boarding of passenger with ambulift, etc.). In case of emergencies, on the other hand, all Cabin Crew Members (inexperienced cabin crew members included) can open and close all doors. E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 144 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250
=== Sayfa 147 ===
The inexperienced cabin crew members arm/disarm the slides of the doors which they are responsible for. The Cabin Crew Members must not arm/disarm the doors other than the doors they are responsible for. For the purpose of preventing the inadvertent slide deployments, all Cabin Crew Members perform   STOP-DROP-REVIEW   before all door opening/closing and slide arming/disarming applications. -   STOP   means stopping all the other works and concentrating on the door,  - DROP   means lowering the hands in order not to hold the door handle inadvertently,  - REVIEW   means reviewing the implementation methods. The flight crew's approval is obtained for the following situations that require opening/closing the door. Closing the door(s) after the completion of passenger boarding, Opening the door(s) after all slides have been DISARMED, Reopening the door in front of which the stairs or boarding bridge is attached for non-routine reasons (document delivery, loading of additional catering items, or passenger who refuses to fly, etc.), Receiving approval for once by the Cabin Chief that all doors can be opened if the flight crew is on board the aircraft during the ground preparations. (After the Cabin Chief has received the said approval, only the Cabin Chief's approval is received to open/close the doors during the ground preparations.) In cases where the cabin crew boards the aircraft before the flight crew, before opening of the door(s), the Cabin Chief does the following: S/he checks on FAP that all slides are DISARMED on board A319/320/321/320NEO/321NEO, A330/A350 aircraft, On board B787 aircraft, s/he checks on 1L ASP that the MANUAL indicator is lit, S/he receives verbal confirmation that the slides are “DISARMED” from the cabin crew on all aircraft types. For all aircraft types, the cabin crew checks visually one more time that the slide is “DISARMED” before opening the door. While there are passengers on board, or during the passenger boarding, if there is no boarding bridge, stairs or catering vehicle in front of the open doors, safety band shall be set and a Cabin Crew Member shall stand in front of the open door. If the safety strap is not functional, the door is not opened when there is no boarding bridge, stairs, or catering vehicle in front of the doors. After receiving approval of the Cabin Chief and the flight crew for opening the doors, agreement is reached with the ground handling employee (the ground handling employee knocks the door, gives the manual “OK” sign, etc.), and the door is opened after rechecking the slides are disarmed. After receiving approval of the Cabin Chief and the flight crew for opening the doors, the doors are closed by reaching agreement with the ground handling employee by checking that there are no obstacles around the door that could cause damage after the service received for the aircraft (catering, stairs, ambulift, etc.). The implementation methods in relation to keeping the doors of the parked aircraft open/closed are described as per the requirements available in   EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part-A, Section 10.1.8. Principles for Securing of Parked Aeroplane. While deboarding the aircraft, the cabin crew obtains information on the conditions of the service and passenger doors from the flight crew and acts as per the instruction given by the flight crew. The Cabin Crew Member shall check that the door safety band is completely placed in its slot on the door casing before closing the door. “CABIN CREW SLIDES ARMED AND CROSS CHECK”  The Cabin Crew Member receiving such command performs cross check after switching the slide of the door s/he is responsible for to "ARMED" position. Upon the first movement of the aircraft, even if a cabin crew member has not heard the command for any reason, they “ARM” the slide of the door(s) for which they are responsible and inform the Cabin Chief of the same by interphone. DOOR OPERATOR:  ➜   S/he neither rushes in nor acts reflexively,  ➜   S/he waits for the DOOR CHECKER to come to her/him. S/he does not tamper the door.  ➜   S/he performs STOP/DROP/REVIEW.  ➜   S/he disarms the door slide under the supervision of the DOOR CHECKER.  ➜   S/he says “ SLIDE DISARMED ” sufficiently loudly so that the DOOR CHECKER can hear her/him.  *At the doors of A330 (3LR), A350 (TC-LGI/LGJ/LGK/LGL) (3LR) and B777 (3LR);   after DISARMING doors which they are responsible for, the Cabin Crew Members perform cross check mutually and give OK with thumbs up. Passenger Safety Briefing  Performing the Passenger Safety Briefing  After all of the passengers have boarded, the relevant announcements in the Current Announcements presentation have been made, the doors are closed*, and the lights have been positioned appropriately, the passenger safety briefing is given through the video system. The cabin chief announces the start of the passenger safety briefing to CA1 for narrow-body aircraft, CC1 and CC2 for wide-body aircraft by interphone and receives confirmation that the cabin crew members responsible for checking the screen video and audio system in the cabin are ready at their posts as per the Cabin Crew Checklist. Then, the passenger safety briefing is carried out through the video system. If the implementation of the cabin readiness report is not carried out simultaneously with the passenger safety briefing, cabin crew members responsible for implementing the cabin readiness report items on board all aircraft types monitor that the screens are working and the sound system is active in the area they are responsible for until the safety briefing is completed. Emergency Exit Briefing  C/A2 gives briefing to the passengers seated in the emergency exit window row seats by distributing them the   Emergency Exit  Passenger Briefing Card before the first movement of the aircraft before the takeoff. On the flights to which an Expat Cabin Crew Member has been assigned as C/A2, this briefing is given by the R.O.T. citizen Cabin Crew Member assigned by the Cabin Chief. After completion of the briefing, the Cabin Crew Member who has performed the briefing collects the   Emergency Exit Passenger Briefing Cards from the passengers, puts them back into their place, and informs the Cabin Chief that the emergency exit briefing is over. While giving information, the passenger’s confirmation of accepting the responsibility is obtained by using the following sentences: “Welcome on board, your seat is in the emergency exit area and it is your responsibility to open this exit in case of an emergency. Please review the card for detailed information. Do you accept this responsibility?” The passenger’s questions, if asked any, are answered   (for   the   questions   about   opening   of   the   exits,   the   passengers   are   guided   to   the   placards   available   on   the   seat backrests/window and showing how the emergency exit is opened); and if there is no passenger who wants to change their seat, the briefing is completed, and the cabin chief is informed accordingly. If the passenger seated by the emergency exit window does not accept the responsibility of opening the emergency exit, or wants to be reseated, the cabin crews change the passenger’s seat within the bounds of possibility in accordance with the methods specified in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.1.4.2. Allocation of Seats to Passengers. Do you need any assistance on fastening the infant belt? * Have a pleasant flight.* * The question “Do you need any assistance on fastening the infant belt?” is not asked to passengers with infant using 3-point belts; the passenger is assisted without waiting for them to ask for. 3. Passengers with infants are seated in such a manner that their number will not exceed the number of the dropping oxygen masks available in their seat row; and any passenger with infant is given information on the use of the oxygen mask and told that in case of a change in the cabin pressurization, s/he is required to wear first their own mask and then put the other mask on the infant passenger. 4. It is informed that the brace position that must be taken together with the infant and the evacuation method are available in the  Safety Card.  Briefing for Passengers Using Crew Seats  The use of the crew seats and allowing the passengers to sit down on these stations is based on all requirements specified in  EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part-A, Section 8.3.13. Use of Vacant Crew Seats,   EK.10.67.001 Ground Operations Manual (GOM), Section 1.1.4.   Passenger Admission, and   PR.02.70.003 Procedure for Use of Vacant Crew Seats in Flight. During take-off, landing or the other stages of the flight, the stations of the Cabin Crew Members at the exits for which they are responsible during the flight may not be used by others. The responsible Cabin Crew Member shall give the person allowed to sit down on the empty cabin crew station the complete safety- related information concerning that station. If the said station is near the emergency exit, the person to sit down on that station is informed also about what to do and how to open the door in case of an emergency (by emphasizing that the door shall be opened only s/he is instructed to do so by the cabin crew). In the event that cabin crew stations are used by passengers, the briefing to be given to passengers includes giving information on the following: a) That the seat is foldable and how to use the belts, b) The location and use of the life vest, c) Oxygen system, d) Belts and smoking warning lights, e) Use of electronic devices, f) Nearest emergency exit and emergency lighting, g) The contents of the   Safety Card. The briefing to be given to the passenger using the vacant cabin crew station is given by the most senior Cabin Crew Member who performs takeoff-landing in the zone where the cabin crew station wherein the passenger will perform takeoff-landing is located. In the event that the relevant Cabin Crew Member is an Expat Cabin Crew Member, this briefing is given by the R.O.T. citizen Cabin Crew Member assigned by the Cabin Chief. After completing the briefing, the responsible Cabin Crew Member gives the completion information to the Cabin Chief.  8.2.5. Chief. (On board the narrow body aircraft with crew seats in the passenger cabin, CA1, after seeing that the cabin crew members are seated on the said seats with their waist and shoulder belts fastened, informs the Cabin Chief that the cabin is ready.) During take-off and landing, all electronic devices in the galley (except airchillers to avoid disrupting the cold food chain) must be turned off. Before the flight crew is delivered the cabin ready report, the Cabin Crew Members must have sat at their stations and fastened their seat belts and harnesses. After making sure (such as confirmation by interphone, last check of the cabin, or observation of the cabin) that the Cabin Crew Members have buckled up in their seats, and that the cabin is completely ready, s/he sits on their own station and fastens their seat belt and shoulder harness. The Cabin Chief gives the “Cabin Ready Report” to the flight crew either verbally by interphone, by keying cabin ready on the handset, or by using the “Cabin Ready” feature on board the aircraft equipped with this feature. On board the aircraft equipped with the Cabin Ready feature, if the “Cabin Ready” warning is deleted from the system due to a long taxiing/descending period, the Cabin Chief is required to reactivate the warning. The cockpit must not be entered to deliver the "Cabin Ready Report".  In accordance with the sterile cockpit practice, the flight crew must not be called by interphone during push back/engine start-up on board aircraft without the “Cabin Ready” feature, and the Cabin Ready Report must be given to the flight crew while taxiing. After the “CABIN CREW BE SEATED FOR TAKE-OFF” announcement made before takeoff and the “CABIN CREW BE SEATED FOR LANDING” announcement made before landing by the Flight Crew Member, if the Cabin Chief sees that the preparations made pursuant to the “Cabin Ready Report-Check Items” in the Cabin Crew Checklist have not been completed or concludes that the cabin is not ready due to another reason, s/he will give the Commander the “Cabin Not Ready” information immediately by interphone. Cabin crews sit at the cabin crew stations with their waist and shoulder belts fastened at all critical stages of the flight, during taxiing, and at any time and condition deemed necessary by the Commander. The cabin crews can only stand-up during taxiing if they perform a task related to the safety of the flight. It is necessary to remember that the aircraft might stop suddenly/there might be a collision during taxiing, which might cause injury/incapacity. Cabin crew members immediately inform the flight crew when they leave their seats to perform a flight safety related task. The cabin crews can stand up during taxiing in the following situations; To perform the flight-safety-related duties that are directly related to completion of the passenger safety briefing and cabin ready report during taxiing before takeoff, To perform the flight-safety-related duties that are required to be performed to prepare the aircraft for the destination point during taxiing after landing. Note: Deterioration in a passenger’s or a crew member’s state of health or the abnormal situations are included in the scope of the flight-safety-related duties. The duties of giving products-services to passengers are not performed during taxiing. If any passenger demands a product-service, s/he is informed that s/he will be assisted after takeoff/parking of the aircraft. The cabin crew may stand up during the taxiing process to perform a flight-safety-related duty that disturbs the cabin ready report (such as closing the open overhead bin doors, secure the unsecured bags, etc., warning a standing passenger not sitting down despite the warning announcement) by assessing the situation. If cabin crew leave their seats during taxiing to perform a flight safety related task, they shall return to their seats immediately after performing their tasks, fasten their waist and shoulder belts and shall not unbuckle their belts until the aircraft is parked and stopped. If a passenger stands up after the Warning Announcement has been made during taxiing: The Warning Announcement is repeated once. If the passenger does not sit down, the cabin crew close to the passenger gets up and informs the passenger to sit down and fasten the seat belt until the seat belt lights go off. If the passenger does not comply with the instructions, the flight crew shall be notified. If necessary, unruly passenger procedures are applied. Before the departure, if any cabin crew member observes any ice, frost stain, or any element similar to snow adhered to the wings of the aircraft, s/he informs the flight crew of the situation immediately. Announcement and Announcement Systems  Announcement system (PA and/or Automatic Announcement System) is an important means of communication, which is used in order to initiate evacuation and preparations in case of any emergency and during passenger briefing. During the pre-flight cabin checks, it is checked in line with the Cabin Crew Checklist that the PA system is active. All announcements that are not specified to be made manually by announcement/bulletin are made using automatic announcement system/EK.10.71.002 Cabin Crew Announcement Manual/ Quick Reference Handlist (QRH). In case of an Automatic Announcement System defect, the announcements are made with PA, and the defect is recorded in AML or e-CML depending on its type. The announcements performed by the flight crew/cabin crew by PA during the flight operation are listened carefully; when such announcements are not heard/understood, the irregularities are informed immediately to the Flight Crew/Cabin Chief; and the PA system defects are recorded in AML or e-CML depending on the type of defect. All announcements made by the cabin crew and recorded on the Automatic Announcement System are included in all requirements in EK.10.71.002   Cabin   Crew   Announcement   Manual   and   Quick   Reference   Handlist   (QRH)   or   issued   as announcement/bulletin/presentation. In the SIS Line Information Form of the flight, if the requirement to announce in a third language other than Turkish and English is indicated, all announcements made in Automatic Announcement System in Turkish and English are also made in the third language in Automatic Announcement System. If line information form of the destination country states that the third language announcement will be performed and a cabin crew member who has a command of the relevant language and allowed to make announcement by Directorate is present in the assigned cabin crew, the Third Language Announcements are made manually through the Current Announcements presentation by the relevant Cabin Crew Member and/or through the automatic announcement system by the Cabin Chief. The “Announcement for Accelerating Passenger Seating” shall be made by the cabin crew through the   Updated Announcements Presentation/Automatic Announcement System when required with the purpose of accelerating the passenger seating process and preventing crowding in the aisle during boarding. The Cabin Chief makes the “Boarding Completed” announcement to the cabin by PA when the ground handling employee informs that the passenger boarding has been completed. Before refueling/defueling, the passengers are instructed to unfasten their seat belts, not to smoke, to disconnect their electronic devices from the power units, and not to use lavatories by making Section 2.14. Refueling/Defueling with Passengers on Board (before the start of refueling/defueling) Announcement as per the requirements in EK.10.71.002 Cabin Crew Announcement Manual. If refueling/defueling is being continued when passengers embarking, onboard or disembarking, in order that all passengers are informed, Section 2.14.1. Refueling/Defueling with Passengers on Board Announcement (when refueling/defueling is continued) is repeated regularly at the intervals deemed appropriate by the Cabin Chief as per the requirements in EK.10.71.002 Cabin Crew Announcement Manual. When refueling/defueling is over, Section 2.14.2. Refueling/Defueling with Passengers on Board Announcement (when refueling/defueling is over) is made as per the requirements in EK.10.71.002 Cabin Crew Announcement Manual. In case of any delay exceeding the scheduled time, the Cabin Chief establishes coordination with the flight crew and performs delay announcements   in   the   event   that   they   are   assigned. In case of suspecting that a passenger is using his/her broadcasting portable electronic device out of the flight mode within the period during which they are not permitted to be used, the passenger is given the necessary explanation and requested to turn the device off. The information on the use of the portable electronic devices is made following the Boarding Completed Announcement. During take-off and landing smart phones, tablets and Portable Electronic Devices (PED) which are of smaller dimensions may be held in hand or placed in seat pockets. However, laptops, noteboooks, and PEDs of bigger dimensions and weights shall be placed in overhead bins or under the front seat within an appropriate case/bag. Particularly the Portable Electronic Devices (PED) carried in the baggage or cargo compartment must be switched off, as they are inaccessible to disable during the flight. If the passenger declares that the electronic device in the baggage loaded in the cargo compartment is on, the situation is notified to the flight crew. Since they may be needed in terms of use, it is not mandatory to turn off the medical devices [portable oxygen concentrators (POC), respiratory/ventilator devices, continuous positive airway pressure machines (CPCP)] used to support physical functions. Passengers who are going to use their POC and CPAP on board aircraft are required to carry sufficient number of batteries (extra batteries sufficient to meet one and a half times of a flight period) with them. There is no requirement to make available medical outlets for such devices in the   cabin.   Detailed   information   is   available   in   the   requirements   in   EK.10.67.001   Ground   Operations   Manual   (GOM),   Section 1.4.8.2.   Rules regarding Carriage and Use of Portable Breathing Devices by Passengers in Cabin. The cabin crew shall be prepared against excessive heating/leaking risks of PED batteries containing lithium during all phases of flight and respond to any potential fire properly. The practical principles with regard to fires possible to be caused by the Portable Electronic Devices (PED) are defined in the Section 8.3.3.2.1 Cabin Fires as per the requirements in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual. The electrical sockets in the galleys may not be used to charge the Portable Electronic Devices (PED) carried by the passengers. The portable oxygen concentrators (POC), breathing devices (respirator, ventilator), continuous positive airway pressure machines (CPAP) that belong to passengers may be used by connecting them to the onboard Medical Outlets by aircraft type depending on the passenger’s need at the flight stages other than taxiing, take-off/landing, critical phases of the flight, refueling/defueling, abnormal and emergency situations. If the passenger declares they do not have spare battery and that they cannot use the device if they remove it from the medical outlet, the flight crew is informed of the situation. The cabin crew must observe the passengers using PED throughout the flight, ensure that the PED suspected to pose a risk for the flight safety and security or to broadcast are switched off, and give information to the Commander. The passengers who continue to use such PED by ignoring the cabin crew's warnings must be warned by the Cabin Chief verbally and/or with an announcement, or in addition to that, with an announcement to be made by the Commander if necessary. In the event that the relevant persons do not switch off their PED, the unruly passenger procedures are applied. The Commander is authorized to restrict the use of PED at any stage of the flight for the reason of flight safety. If the Commander wants that the Portable Electronic Devices (PED) are switched off and secured, the Cabin Chief shall make the cancellation announcement in accordance with the requirements of EK.10.71.002 Cabin Crew Announcement Manual , Section 2.15. Announcement for Cancellation of the Use of Electronic Devices to passengers. If the flight crew demands that the IFE/Wi-Fi Systems are switched off, all systems (IFE/Connectivity/Wi-Fi/GCS/PED Power, etc.) on the IFE/Crew Panel are switched OFF. The cabin crew shall check that the PED are switched off, and inform the flight crew that the specified duties have been performed. The irregularities related to inappropriate use of electronic devices by passengers throughout the flight operation are reported by the Cabin Chief to the Commander, and the necessary measures are taken. In case of any event or suspicious situation detected to be effective on security implementations, the Commander submits information to the Company via Air Safety Report (ASR) based on the obligatory report which shall be submitted to Turkish DGCA. The Cabin Chief submits information on the subject to the Cabin Operations Management by   FR.71.0271 Cabin Operations Monitoring Supervisor's Office Electronic Correspondence Form.  8.2.7.1. Measures for Use of Flight/Cabin Crew Member PED (Portable Electronic Device)  There are two types of lithium batteries, lithium metal (non-rechargeable, i.e., disposable) and lithium ion (rechargeable). Laptop computers, tablets and other battery-operated devices are generally powered by one or more battery packs that contain multiple lithium-ion batteries or cells. The Flight/Cabin Crew Members can carry lithium battery powered devices and their spare lithium batteries during the flight as long as the Watt hours (Wh) of its battery do not exceed 100 for lithium-ion batteries, or the lithium content does not exceed 2 grams for lithium metal batteries. Current generation PEDs use lithium ion (i.e.,   lithium polymer) batteries and following data can be used for judgment about the Wh rating of a PED battery. Ipad Pro (12.9 inches): 38.5 Wh, Ipad Air 2: 27.3 Wh, MacBook Air (13 inches): 54 Wh, MacBook Pro (15 inches): 99.5 Wh.   Battery information can be found at technical specifications of PED. In terms of calculating the Wh of the battery, when one PED has several batteries powering it together, the addition of Wh of all the batteries powering the device must be considered. The Cabin Crew Members must be aware that lithium-ion cells are flammable and capable of overheating and self-ignition. Overheating can be caused by a short circuit, overcharge, rapid discharge, extreme temperature, mishandling or an internal defect. Overheating can cause a thermal runaway and can cause adjacent cells to overheat. This can cause a lithium battery fire to flare repeatedly as each cell overheats. The implementation procedures for the fire that includes lithium metal or lithium-ion battery cells are available in the Section 8.3.3 Fire.  8.2.8. In-Flight Entertainment Systems  "In-flight entertainment systems" used in all aircraft types are controlled from one source, and their location and denomination vary depending on the aircraft types. Thanks to such systems, video presentations are broadcast through screens located in several locations of the cabin, and audio presentations are broadcast through headphones and loudspeakers by the Passenger Service Units (PSU) available on the seats. Further information about such systems and their use, depending on aircraft types, is available on TK Portal/Cabin Crew Directorate page.  8.2.9. Product presentation and service tasks of cabin crew members may require momentary release of service trolleys in the cabin (with brakes applied). In such a case, cabin crew members are required to return to their trolley as soon as possible. Covers of garbage trolleys/fixed waste bins in the galleys must be kept closed at all times. In the event that any fluid leaks from garbage trolleys, ice units/drawers or galley panels during the flight, the relevant failure must be recorded in e-CML.  Lavatories;  Upon flashing of the seat belt signs earliest while passing the airport altitude plus 5,000 ft., the reminder announcement is made in accordance with 2.6. Post Takeoff Reminder Announcement through the Automatic Announcement System/EK.10.71.002 Cabin Crew Announcement Manual. The Cabin Crew Members open, check that there is anything abnormal and that the return to seat light is functioning, and lock again the lavatories for which they are responsible. Following turning off the fasten seat belt signs, the lavatories are unlocked. Attention must be paid whether lids of waste bins are closed (in order to function as automatic fire extinguishers), whether the floor is dry, and lavatories must be checked during the flight to ensure flight safety and security. These checks performed by cabin crew shall be as frequent as possible and shall not exceed 30 minutes consecutively. In the event that there is no water on board aircraft, or the existing water is consumed completely, on the ground/in flight, all lavatory heaters must be switched OFF. In the event that the lavatories are closed to use due to failure or for hygiene reason, it is necessary to affix a sticker on the door of the relevant lavatory indicating that it is closed to use. In that case, the relevant lavatory must be checked frequently throughout the flight.  Cabin;  The cabin is monitored during product/service offering. The cabin is also monitored by walking along the cabin aisle at regular intervals at the times other than product/service offering. Service trolleys are kept with the brake pedals pressed during use and are never left unattended. If any malfunctioning catering trolley is detected before the flight, it is replaced by informing the catering employee. In the event that any malfunctioning catering trolley is detected during the flight, this trolley must not be removed from its place but instead must be affixed with a failure label and reported to Cabin Crew Directorate/Assistant Directorate (Service and Performance)/Cabin Product Management after the flight. Foldable, service, and garbage trolleys are accompanied by a cabin crew member and not left unattended as long as they are in the passenger cabin. Product presentation and service tasks of cabin crew members may require momentary release of service trolleys in the cabin (with brakes applied). In such a case, cabin crew members are required to return to their trolley as soon as possible. Attention must be paid that there are no magazines, papers, bags or any other foreign objects on the floor throughout the flight, and if any, they must be collected. Before submitting the cabin ready report upon the descending announcement, it is necessary to take care to collect all the read newspapers, magazines, catering materials, etc. in the cabin, and to place the pillows and blankets not used by the passengers in a suitable covered compartment so as not to hinder the safety. Utmost attention must be paid to the passenger calls with the purpose of ensuring flight and passenger safety. On board aircraft where cabin crew call buttons cannot be used, special category passengers/their companions must be approached and asked about their needs during cabin checks conducted at fifteen (15) minute intervals during times other than product and service delivery. It is ensured that the cabin temperature is monitored by the cabin crew and kept at a level that ensures passenger comfort and satisfaction. The sudden temperature changes, extraordinary odors and sounds across the cabin or in some parts of the cabin are informed to the flight crew.  8.2.11. Controlled Rest in Cockpit  The rest made on the cockpit seat by transferring the flight controls to the other flight crew to ensure the flight safety. According to the requirements specified in   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operation Regulations GM1 CAT.OP.MPA.210,   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS |  Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air Operations ANNEX-4 Commercial Air Transportation (Chapter-CAT),   EK.10.73.001  Operation Manual Part-A, Section 8.3.10.3 Controlled Rest on the Flight Deck, in cases where the flight crew makes controlled rest, the finish time of the said resting is notified to the cabin chief. A Cabin Crew Member establishes communication by interphone or visits the cockpit every twenty (20) minutes. The Cabin Crew Member checks whether the Flight Crew Member is awake or not at the end of the said period. 8.3. Cabin Abnormal Situation/Emergency Operation Implementations  8.3.1. General  Flight safety and security is one of the primary principles of Turkish Airlines. The Section 8.3. Cabin Abnormal Situation/Emergency Operation Implementations has been drawn up to enable the cabin crews to act in compliance with the Company procedures relating to flight safety and security in case of any potential abnormalities/emergencies they may encounter in flights. The principles related to the pre-flight compliance check and usage information for the emergency equipment to be used in abnormal situations and emergencies are defined in   EK.10.71.003 Cabin Crew Aircraft Types Manual , Chapter 6. Emergency Equipment. Slow and sudden decompression, fire, evacuation, bomb, hijacking, illness on board, incapacitated pilot subjects are considered as part of emergencies. Bombs and hijacking situations are detailed in the requirements in   EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part-A, Section 10. Security and EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Chapter 10 Security. Decompression, fire, evacuation and oxygen demand during flight are specified in this chapter, whereas meeting basic first aid needs is specified in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Chapter 14. First Aid. Emergency practices caused by dangerous goods are described in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Chapter 9. Dangerous Goods and the emergency practices caused by biological/chemical weapons/substances in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Chapter 10. Security. According to all requirements available in   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operation Regulations GM1 ORO.CC.115,   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS |  Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air Operations ANNEX-4 Commercial Air Transportation (Chapter-CAT); “Safety equipment” is the stationary/portable equipment (e.g. seatbelt, infant carrier,   Safety Card, demo kit, etc.) available on board the aircraft to ensure a safe performance of the flight operation and the safety of the people on board the aircraft (passengers-crews). “Emergency equipment” is the stationary/portable equipment used to respond to abnormalities/emergencies requiring immediate response to protect and maintain the flight safety and the safety of lives of the people onboard the aircraft. “Normal procedures” are the procedures (e.g., pre-flight briefing, pre-flight controls, passenger briefing, securing the galley and cabin, observation of the cabin during flight) that define the normal flight procedures according to the Operations Manual. “Emergency procedures” are the procedures to be applied in case of abnormalities/emergencies according to the Operations Manual. To that end, “abnormal situation” refers to the situation that is atypical and extraordinary, a deviation from the normal operation, and any situation that may result in an emergency. As representative of Turkish Airlines, the Commander ensures that all preparations required to perform the flight duty are carried out in compliance with the national/international rules, and that all measures to ensure safety of the passengers, crew members, cargo and the aircraft are taken on the ground and during the flight as of the moment s/he takes control of the aircraft.  Cabin Chief:  Within the scope of the requirements specified   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operation Regulations ORO.CC.200(d),   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS |  Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air Operations ANNEX-3 Organizational Requirements for Air Operations (Chapter- ORO), the cabin chief is accountable to the Commander for ensuring that safety and security are ensured inside the cabin during the flight operation, the instructions and standards defined in the operation manuals regarding safety and security are met by the cabin crew members, and for establishing the necessary coordination. S/he is responsible for changing the standard of and terminating any cabin activity (such as offering of catering items/products) that is irrelevant to safety and security in cases where s/he deems necessary in terms of flight safety and security within the scope of the requirements specified in   DK.33.001 EASA Air OPS | Easy Access Rules for Flight Operations ORO.CC.200(d), DK.22.115 SHT-  OPS | Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air Operations ANNEX-3 Organizational Requirements for Air Operations (Chapter-ORO). S/he is responsible for ensuring that the cabin is monitored at each stage of the flight operations, as well as for establishing communication and coordination between flight crew members, cabin crew members and the other operational employee. According to all requirements specified in   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operations Regulations CAT.GEN.MPA.100,   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS |  Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air Operations ANNEX-4 Commercial Air Transportation (Chapter-CAT), s/he is responsible for communicating any technical failures, abnormal sounds, smell or appearance inside the cabin as well as situations deviating from the standard regarding operational regulations and the situations threatening the flight safety and security to the Commander within the periods defined in   EK.10.73.001 Operations Manual Part-A, Section 8.3.10.4.1 Communication to the Flight Crew and EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.3.1.1.   Abnormal Cases/Emergencies during Flight, S/he ensures that the required briefing and information are provided to the passengers in the cabin, in a complete and correct manner throughout the flight operations. The duties, authorizations and responsibilities of the Cabin Chief are described in Chapter 1. Organizational Duties and Responsibilities, section   TK PORTAL/DYS Job Descriptions. Cabin Crew Member  Cabin Crew Member shall be obliged to be familiar with and follow the standards and instructions describing their duties under normal, abnormal and emergency circumstances, and shall be accountable to the cabin chief and Commander of the relevant flight for fulfilling their own duties and responsibilities in accordance with the standards described in the applicable documents issued on the Document Management System and EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual and Cabin Crew Checklist prepared in line with the requirements specified in   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operation Regulations ORO.GEN.110,   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS | Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for  Air   Operations   ANNEX-3   Organizational   Requirements   for   Air   Operations   (Chapter-ORO).   The   duties,   authorizations   and responsibilities of the Cabin Crew Member are described in Chapter 1. Organizational Duties and Responsibilities, section TK  PORTAL/DYS Job Descriptions.  8.3.1.1. Abnormal Cases/Emergencies During Flight  As per   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operation Regulations   GM1 ORO.GEN.110(f), the cabin crew must keep an eye out for the abnormalities. It is important that the cabin crew gives clear information to the flight crew at the right time. Abnormal situations required to be reported to the flight crew; 1. Fire in the cabin or engine, 2. Burn odor or smoke, 3. Fuel or fluid leakage, 4. Exit door that cannot be armed or disarmed, 5. Zonal excessive cabin heat changes, 6. Symptoms of icing on the wings, 7. Cabin/galley equipment or material failure, or dangerous break of the same, 8. Suspicious object, 9. Unruly passenger, 10. Security threat, 11. Abnormal vibration or sound, 12. Medical emergency, 13. Fall of the overhead oxygen masks, 14. The other issues deemed relevant by any cabin crew or technical crew member. The cabin crew must be careful and attentive with regard to the use and abnormalities of the electrical appliances in the galley, inform the blown fuses to the Commander, and act in accordance with his directives. In case of any unannounced missed approach, the Cabin Chief must not enter the cockpit unless called in. The principles of the communication between the flight crew and the cabin crew in the normal/abnormal situations and emergencies are described in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.2.1. Flight Crew/Cabin Crew Communication. The Cabin Crew Member shall introduce him/herself through interphone, provide all details about abnormal cases to flight crew, communicate any measures taken, and implement any instructions to be received from flight crew. When Abnormal/Emergency situations occur during the flight, the product and service delivered to passengers is stopped immediately. Cabin crew members are required to warn the flight crew in abnormal/emergency situations in accordance with the sterile cockpit rules at the times specified in Table-12: Emergency/Abnormal Situation Warning/Information Time Table below.  Table-12: Emergency/Abnormal Situation Warning/Information Time Table In case of abnormal cases/emergencies (Except Hijacking), the cabin crew members shall warn flight crew at times specified below: E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 161 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250

Principles of Implementation for Abnormal Situation/Emergency during Cabin Crew Rest in Cruise  Cabin crew rest in cruise is defined in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 4.3.1. Principles of Cabin Crew Resting during Flight Operation. The cabin crew's course of action and the measures to be taken in case of abnormal situation and emergency are specified below:  Fire/Smoke:   In case of a smoke-fire possible to break out during the crew rest, from within cabin crew continuing to work in the cabin, the first person who saw the incident responds to it, and the second (2.) cabin crew member relays the information to the flight crew and the most senior Cabin Crew Member on foot in compliance with the procedures defined in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.3. Cabin Abnormal Situation/Emergency Operation   Implementations and   Quick Reference Handlist (QRH). The most senior Cabin Crew Member who is assigned with coordination, or another Cabin Crew Member to be assigned by him/her, assesses the situation, terminates resting of the resting crew members. She gives brief and clear information on the situation (place, type of fire, and status of response to fire). Resting Cabin Crew Members wear orange warning vests at crew rest and go to their stations. All Cabin Crew Members carry out the work steps defined in the   Quick Reference Handlist (QRH).  Suspicion of epidemics and detection of dangerous goods:   In case of suspicion of epidemics and detection of dangerous goods possible to occur during the crew rest, the first cabin crew member who has seen the incident responds to the incident, and the second (2.) cabin crew member relays information to the cockpit crew and the most senior Cabin Crew Member on foot in compliance with the procedures defined in   EK.10.71.003 Cabin Crew Aircraft Types Manual, Section 6.2.4. Universal Precaution Kit (Fluid Spill Kit). The most senior Cabin Crew Member who is standing, or another Cabin Crew Member to be assigned by him/her, assesses the situation, terminates resting of the resting crew members. She gives brief and clear information on the suspicious material. Resting Cabin Crew Members wear orange warning vests at crew rest and go to their stations. All Cabin Crew Members carry out the principles defined in the   Quick Reference Handlist (QRH) Section 1.13. Dangerous Goods.  Incapacitated crew situation (flight crew/cabin crew):   In case of incapacitated crew (flight crew/cabin crew) occurring during the crew rest, the most senior Cabin Crew Member on foot, or another Cabin Crew Member to be assigned by him/her, terminates the rest of the resting crew members in compliance with the procedures defined in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 4.3. Reduction   of   Cabin   Crew   under   Unpredictable   Conditions   (Incapacity   or   Failure   to   complete   Cabin   Crew   Number)   during Ground/Flight Operations outside Main Base. Resting Cabin Crew Members wear orange warning vests at crew rest and go to their stations.  Turbulence:   In case of light turbulence, the cabin crew member serving in the cabin carries out the work steps in turbulence as defined in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.3.7. Turbulence. She goes to check the cabin together with the most senior Cabin Crew Member. In case of severe and moderate turbulences, on the other hand, the crew member secures himself/herself first; and after the seatbelt signs go off, she contacts the cabin crew members in the cabin, lavatories, and crew rest through the interphone, and informs them of the situation. According to the post-turbulence status assessment (such as passenger injury, crew incapacity), the rest of the resting crew is terminated. Resting Cabin Crew Members wear orange warning vests at crew rest and go to their stations.  Medical Emergency/Sick Passenger:   In case of sick passenger and/or medical emergencies requiring attention, the cabin crew member serving in the cabin responds and carries out the necessary procedures. In case of need, the most senior Cabin Crew Member on foot or another Cabin Crew Member to be assigned by her/him evaluates the signs specified under the heading Vital Signs in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 14. First Aid, and terminates resting of the resting cabin crew, if necessary. Resting Cabin Crew Members wear orange warning vests at crew rest and go to their stations.  Unruly Passenger:   In case of an unruly passenger possible to be encountered during the crew rest, the Cabin Crew Members serving in the cabin try to get the situation under control. In each case where it is observed that the situation continues, that the cabin crew cannot get it under control and/or that it is decided to read the unruly passenger form, the most senior Cabin Crew Member on foot, or another Cabin Crew Member to be assigned by her, terminates resting of the resting cabin crew as per the procedures described under EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 10.5. Unruly Passenger. Resting Cabin Crew Members wear orange warning vests at crew rest and go to their stations. Bomb:   In the event that a bomb threat is received or a bomb is detected during a flight, the most senior Cabin Crew Member on foot, or another Cabin Crew Member to be assigned by her, acts in compliance with the principles defined in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 10.3 Bomb Threat Calls. Oxygen Systems  Oxygen is received from 3 sources on board the aircraft. a) Cabin oxygen system – chemical/gaseous b) Cockpit oxygen system - gas c) Portable oxygen system Each system features its individual control and indicator system, and functions independent from each other.  8.3.2.1. Cabin Oxygen System  According to the requirements specified in   DK.41.001 IOSA Standards Manual (ISM) CAB 3.4.13, the cabin oxygen system provides the passengers and the cabin crew with oxygen in case of decompression.For a comfortable flight, the maximum cabin pressure is 8,000 ft. If the cabin pressure increases to 13,500-15,000 ft for any reason whatsoever, the mask covers in the passenger overhead units, galleys, lavatories, cabin crew stations, and crew rests open automatically, or electrically by the flight crew, thus ensuring that the oxygen masks drop. If the mask covers remain closed, they are opened by the cabin crew as described in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.3.2.2.1. Manual Opening of Oxygen Mask Covers. While the oxygen is provided from the generator in the chemical system (the generator generates oxygen as a result of chemical reaction), it is provided from the oxygen cylinder in the gaseous system. The oxygen flow into the masks starts when the mask/the strip marked PULL, if available, is pulled. In the chemical system, the oxygen flow of a generator cannot be stopped once the generator is activated. The system on board B787 is breathing-sensitive and activated when the individual inhales, and it gives one unit of oxygen at each inhaling. In the chemical system, since the generator might heat up significantly during operation, a burning smell may occur; thus, it is necessary to avoid touching the generator. No burning smell is felt, since the cylinder in the gaseous system does not warm up. While donning the oxygen mask, the mask is positioned so as to cover both mouth and nose. The mask is strapped over the head with the rubber strap. It is fitted on the face fully by using the adjusting straps, if available. The detailed information on the cabin oxygen systems is available in all requirements in   EK.10.71.003 Cabin Crew Aircraft Types Manual.  Hypoxia:  When the cabin pressure exceeds 10,000 ft (3,048 m), the HYPOXIA symptoms appear. HYPOXIA is the inability to inhale oxygen due to insufficient pressure at high altitudes. The detailed information on the reasons, symptoms, and first-aid principles of hypoxia is available in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 14.23.1. Anoxia-Hypoxia. When enough oxygen cannot be inhaled, the periods for staying conscious on altitude basis are available in the following Table-14: Table of Periods for Staying Conscious. Cabin Decompression  There may be two types of decompression. The warnings to appear in case of decompression vary by aircraft type and are available in all requirements in   EK.10.71.003 Cabin Crew Aircraft Types Manual.  1) Sudden Decompression Causes:  A hole on the airframe, A sudden malfunction in the cabin pressurization system.  Symptoms: Symptoms in the cabin:  ▬ Loud sound like explosion, crashing, ▬ Sudden temperature drop in cabin, ▬ Fog caused by intensive humidity, ▬ Limited visibility due to dust particles, ▬ Free objects flying around, ▬ Blowout of the gaseous drink cups, closed packages, ▬ Sudden boiling of the liquids in the cups that contain hot drinks, ▬ Dropping of oxygen masks.  Symptoms observed in the people:  ▬ Severe pain in the ears and sinuses, ▬ Pain caused by the compressed gas in the body, ▬ Difficulty in speaking, ▬ Feeling cold/hypothermia, ▬ Having difficulty in breathing, ▬ Hypoxia. 1) Slow Decompression Causes:  A failure progressing slowly in the pressure system, A leakage which may occur in passenger doors and/or windows.  Symptoms: Symptoms in the cabin:  ▬ A high-pitched sound from the part with leakage (not always can be heard).  Symptoms observed in the people:  ▬ Feeling of pressure in the ears, ▬ Joint pain, ▬ Pain caused by the compressed gas in the body, ▬ Slowness of movements, ▬ Hypoxia. Symptoms of sudden and slow decompression do not take place in the given order; also, one or all of them may take place at once.  Measures to take in case of slow decompression;  The most senior Cabin Crew Member serving in the cabin contacts the flight crew immediately by interphone. If contact is impossible, the relevant cabin crew member enters the cockpit by opening the cockpit door by using the emergency password/opening it directly if it has   been   unlocked   automatically   (the   aircraft-type-based   differences   in   automatic   unlocking   of   the   cockpit   door   in   case   of decompression are specified in the requirements in   EK.10.71.003 Cabin Crew Aircraft Types Manual). Cabin crew members move the passengers away from the area with leakage and have them seated to another safe place. (If it is possible to locate the source of the leakage.) Product/service offer is stopped; safety of the cabin and galley shall be ensured. Cabin crew members shall fasten their belts at their stations. (If the leakage is at a cabin crew station, cabin crew shall sit to any other safe place.) If there is cabin crew in the crew rest during slow decompression, the procedures described in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section   8.3.1.1.1.   Principles   of   Implementation   for   Abnormal   Situation/Emergency   during   Cabin   Crew   Rest   in   Cruise   are implemented.  In case of decompression, the cabin crew shall;  Pull the closest mask available and place on their face demonstrating the process to the passengers, if possible, Sit in the nearest seat and buckle up, Secure herself/himself by holding a fixed item at their location or by squeezing into group of passengers in the nearest vacant place (by asking for help from the passengers if necessary) if there is not vacant seat, Implement the procedures described under the heading “B.) If No Command is given by the Flight Crew” if no command is given by the flight crew, and contact the crew rest by interphone if there is cabin crew in the crew rest, Implement the procedures described under the heading “A.) Commands likely to be given by Flight Crew” by acting as per the commands given if the flight crew gives commands, The announcement is activated automatically depending on the aircraft type, In cases where the automatic announcement is not activated, make the “Decompression Announcement” specified in the Quick Reference Handlist (QRH), (There is no need to remove the oxygen mask to make announcements/speak.) If possible, s/he shows the passenger with gestures (hand, arm, head movements) to press the mask to the mouth and nose, Position the trolley diagonally, and secure it by pressing on the brake, if decompression occurs during service, E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 166 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250

Secure herself/himself and inhale oxygen from the nearest mask if s/he is in the crew rest, and shall not leave the crew rest until receiving the “MASKS OFF” command from the flight crew. The detailed information on the warnings received in the cabin in case of decompression is available in the requirements in  EK.10.71.003 Cabin Crew Aircraft Types Manual. If the cabin lights do not automatically switch to the bright mode, they are switched to bright manually (if possible). In case of decompression, flight crew members shall perform emergency descent immediately. The duration of the emergency descent from the maximum altitude may vary by weather conditions, geographical conditions, and traffic intensity. The required assistance shall be provided to the passenger in line with the commands received from the flight crew members, when the aircraft switches to cruise.  In case of emergency descent, the flight crew gives information to the cabin through PA. A.) Commands likely to be given by Flight Crews 1) "EMERGENCY DESCENT", flight crew makes an announcement to the cabin through PA. (Twice)  This command is to inform the cabin crew of a sudden decompression and/or impending emergency landing. A sudden and steep descent is performed to reach the safe altitude. The cabin crew follow the procedures described under the heading “ In case of decompression, the cabin crew shall ” above.  2) “KEEP MASKS ON” (Twice)  This command is to instruct the cabin crew to continue using oxygen masks when the aircraft is cruising after a sudden decompression and the cabin altitude is above 14,000 ft. The cabin crew members; Inhale oxygen by using the closest portable oxygen cylinder (while shifting from the fixed oxygen mask to the mask of the portable oxygen cylinder, the cabin crew member must evaluate the situation well by considering her/his own oxygen need, and be careful against the risk of hypoxia). Hang the carrying straps to their shoulders in a way to ensure that the indicator is visible. Check the cabin, lavatories, and crew rests by taking MRT with her/him (except for B787 aircraft). Help the passengers and Cabin Crew Members inhale the oxygen they need from the general oxygen system by opening the mask covers remaining closed as described in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.3.2.2.1. Manual Opening of Oxygen Mask Covers. Give the passengers and Cabin Crew Members suffering from health problems oxygen from the oxygen cylinder, or the medical oxygen cylinder, if available, when the oxygen flow from the general system is over (the oxygen flow can be observed through the oxygen flow indicators [if available]). Give the first aid as per the procedures described in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Chapter 14. First Aid if there is injured passenger or Cabin Crew Member. The cabin crew on board must take into consideration that after the “KEEP MASKS ON” command, a descent may be made again. In the event of another descent, they must sit in the nearest seat and fasten their seat belt, as there may not be a new command from the cockpit.  3) “MASKS OFF” (Twice)  This command is to instruct the cabin crew to remove their oxygen masks when the cabin altitude drops to 14,000 ft. or below following a sudden decompression. This command comes when the safe altitude is reached. In that case; The cabin crews and passengers may take off their masks. Cabin crew checks cabin, crew rests and lavatories. Assist the passengers in need to receive oxygen from the general oxygen system; when the oxygen flow in the system is over, give the passengers with medical problems oxygen from the portable oxygen cylinder or from the medical oxygen cylinder if available. Give the first aid as per the procedures described in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Chapter 14. First Aid if there is injured passenger or Cabin Crew Member. The cabin crew checks the cabin for any damage. The most senior cabin crew member shall ensure constant information flow by communicating the status of the cabin and passengers to flight crew through the interphone.
