If the property/object is not deemed to be suspicious, on the other hand, the Commander calls IOCC/Flight Operations Control Departments with the best coordination possible, and gives the necessary information to Aircraft Security/Airport Security departments. Cabin crew members shall take the measures required to prevent any person from contacting the relevant property/object. If the suspicion continues after the assessments made by the relevant departments informed about the property/object, the safety and security measures are taken in line with the final decision of the Commander, or the bomb procedure is applied as per the requirements specified in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 10.3 Bomb Threat Calls. In cases where the flight crew is not aboard the aircraft and the detected property/object is deemed suspicious; the station official is informed about it by stating the position of the property/object in order to be forwarded to Aircraft Security/Airport Security departments. The cabin crew and the station officials take the necessary actions through coordination so that the suspicious object is not touched. If any dangerous situation is detected in respect of the suspicious object and/or such object is considered to have any potential hazard, as a result of the search performed by the Aircraft Security/Airport Security departments, then any required security measures are taken, and the bomb threat procedure is applied as per the requirements specified in Section 10.3 Bomb Threat Calls. The process of removing the suspicious object from the aircraft is carried out by the Aircraft Security/Airport Security officer as per  TL.15.004 Instruction on Actions to be Performed for Suspicious Objects Found Onboard Aircrafts at Parking Position and/or the Airport Security Plan/Program of the relevant station. The coordination processes regarding suspicious objects are performed by the Aircraft Security departments at the airports where there are Aircraft Security departments, or by the ground handling agent at the at the airports where there is no Aircraft Security department. In the event that the Aircraft Security/Airport Security departments deem the suspicious object non-dangerous, as specified in  TL.67.032 Unclaimed and Forgotten (Found Items) Item Properties Processes,   FR.67.0144 Found Properties Release Form is completed by the assigned employee (the authorized Cabin Crew Member, if the authorized Cabin Crew Member of the new flight has come, or otherwise, the authorized cleaning employee/supervisor, station personnel, etc.), and the found item is delivered to the Lost Properties department/authorized employee of the relevant station.  10.2.12. Security Measures  Any security measures are required to be taken completely in respect of all flights due to variety of terrorist targets and acts, and any additional measures are required to be taken if and when required.  10.3. Bomb Threat Calls 10.3.1. Bomb Threat Calls on The Ground  In case of any bomb threat call on the ground prior to take-off or after landing; then: The Company shall ensure that the procedures and connection checklists that are valid for each aircraft type are accessible to use to search or inspect concealed guns, explosives or the other dangerous devices during the flight in case there is the suspicion of sabotage or other illegal interventions. Such procedures shall include the following in accordance with the requirements specified in DK.41.001  IOSA Standards Manual (ISM) CAB 3.4.15: 1. The guide for the course of action to be followed when a bomb or suspicious object is found; 2. If specified by the aircraft manufacturer firm, the least risk location(s) for bomb or explosives in each aircraft type The Commander shall perform a briefing for the cabin crew members in respect of the following matters: The suspicious object must not be touched, The passengers must not be informed about the situation, The passengers and crew members must immediately leave the aircraft with their hand baggage. In such cases, the following regulations shall be applied: a) In case of any possible explosion, the aircraft shall be parked to any remote area of the airport in order to minimize the loss of life and property. b) In the event that any bomb threat call has been received when the boarding bridge is attached to the aircraft, then flight crew shall inform the controller, and shall prevent the aircraft from parking to the near boarding bridges. In the event that such kind of bomb threat call is received when the aircraft is moving on the ground, then the aircraft shall not return to the boarding bridge or terminal. First of all, the aircraft is moved to and stopped in the nearest safe area;   Quick Reference Handlist (QRH) “1.18. Bomb Threat on Ground Announcement” is made; the passengers and crew members leave the aircraft with their hand baggage. 10.3.1.1. In case of Detection of Bomb on the Ground  1. The bomb detected shall not be contacted. 2. The passengers and crew members shall be immediately disembarked in line with the instruction received from the cockpit.  10.3.2. Bomb Threat Calls During Flight  a) The Commander shall decide whether there is any chance for searching the bomb during the rest of the flight, or not, and whether the passengers will be informed about the situation, or not. b) If it is decided to inform the passengers, “1.17.   In Case of Detection of Any Bomb/Receiving Bomb Threat Call During the Flight” announcement is made as per the activity steps described in   Quick Reference Handlist (QRH). c) Passengers shall hold their hand baggage on their laps, and shall check their content in detail, and shall keep them on their laps, upon performance of the announcement.  d) Crew members shall check the content of their baggage. e) The bomb search process is performed by taking articles of the Bomb Search Form of the relevant aircraft, which is available in the cockpit document file in the number equal to the number of jump seats, as basis. f) All cabin crew members shall perform the searching process systematically based on the Bomb Search Form of the relevant aircraft. g) The primary places to be searched by the cabin crew members on board the aircraft are the lavatories and galleys which are open for public use. h) The lavatories shall be locked in order to keep them under control subsequent to the search performed. i) During the cabin searching process, the passengers shall be guided only to the areas that have already been searched. j) Passengers shall be prevented from standing unnecessarily, and it shall be ensured that they sit on their seats by keeping their belts fastened.  10.3.2.1. In case of Detection of Bomb During Flight  The “Bomb Threat Procedure” details of which are available in the paragraph 10.3.2.2. shall be applied. a) Even if any suspicious object has been found, cabin crew shall keep searching the aircraft until the searching process is completed. b) Flight crew shall descend the aircraft below 10,000 ft in order to minimize the effect of any possible explosion. c) In the event that it has been reported that the bomb will be detonated at a certain height, then cabin altitude shall be kept above this height.  After Landing:  a) The aircraft shall be parked to an area where no other aircraft is available. b) The stairs shall be requested, and fire department shall be called. c) Passengers and crew members shall immediately leave the aircraft without taking their hand baggage in line with the instruction of Commander. If the stairs required to ensure that passengers and crew members leave the aircraft as soon as possible cannot be provided within a reasonable period, the evacuation process shall be performed by use of slides upon decision of the Commander. d) Questions, especially asked by journalists in relation to the incident, shall not be answered, and no statement shall be made in relation to the matter. e) The detailed report shall be submitted to the authorities of the Company.  10.3.2.2. Bomb Threat Procedure  IF ANY SUSPICIOUS OBJECT IS DETECTED, DO NOT TOUCH IT, AND INFORM IMMEDIATELY THE PILOT-IN-COMMAND OR THE CABIN CHIEF. The cabin crew shall report all visible features and the place of the suspicious object to the Commander through interphone or in writing. IN CASE OF DETECTION OF ANY BOMB/RECEIPT OF BOMB THREAT CALL ON THE GROUND Do not touch the detected bomb, Disembark the passengers and the crew members in line with the instruction received from the cockpit. IN CASE OF DETECTION OF ANY BOMB/RECEIPT OF BOMB THREAT CALL DURING THE FLIGHT Do not cut or disconnect the tight rope/strip, Do not open suspicious parts, Do not cut or disconnect any wire or electrical connection, Keep searching the aircraft until completion of the searching process even if any suspicious object or pack has been detected. Procedures to be followed by Cabin Crew Members in case of Bomb on Flight are described in detail in the Quick Reference Handlist  (QRH) Section 1.17 and 1.18.  10.3.2.3. Least Risk Bomb Location (LRBL)  The least risk bomb location for each aircraft type is required to be specified in accordance with the requirements specified in  DK.31.026 ICAO Annex 8 | Airworthiness of Aircraft, 9.3.5. Accordingly; the least risk bomb location (LRBL) for all aircraft types has been identified by the respective manufacturers as AFT RIGHT DOOR. a) Cabin crew shall equalize the interior and exterior pressure prior to carrying the bomb, in order to minimize the effects of any possible explosion. b) LRBL area, to which the bomb will be carried, shall be cleared of passengers and properties. c) The person must move slowly and carefully while moving the bomb. d) The bomb must be carried in the same position as it is found. If there is a suspicious object in a bag, the bag must be carried in a horizontal and balanced manner; and the lid, if any, must definitely not be opened. e) Materials (preferably opposite colors) such as ties, belts, scarves, headphone cords shall be tied to each other in order to ensure that bomb squad detects the location of the bomb, which has been placed into the LRBL. Figure-22: Least Risky Area (for Bomb)  10.3.3. Chemical and Biological Weapons  It has been experienced that any chemical and biological weapons are also used in terrorist attacks occurred. Chemical weapons are chemical toxins with high toxic, and can be easily hidden and carried. Biological weapons are any bacteria or viruses causing any epidemic illness and death. They may be in the form of solid, liquid, and gas. Any object, envelope or pack, which is suspected to be any chemical/biological weapon; may include oil stains, color deformation or odor. may be in the form of white, nude or beige dust. may seem like talcum powder. The major step to determine the measures to be taken and the procedure to be applied is to distinguish the explosives from the nuclear/chemical/biologic weapons. In most cases, the non-fixed explosives detected on board the aircraft are required to be carried to E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 207 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250

LRBL, whereas any chemical/biological substances are required not to be relocated.  10.3.3.1. Measures to be taken by Cabin Crew  a) Flight crew shall be informed about the matter. b) Flight crew shall start to use their own oxygen system. c) It shall be ensured that passengers and cabin crew members receive oxygen from the cabin oxygen system through the response from cockpit. d) Flight crew shall decrease the temperature of cabin as much as possible. e) The substance must definitely not be tried to be cleaned. f) In case of any contact with the object, then hands and arms must immediately be washed with clean water. g) Protective materials shall be used (gloves, masks, etc.). h) The object shall immediately be covered with the most suitable material available. Thereafter, any barrier shall be established in order to stop the contact of the object with the air. After laying dry blanket on the substance, plastic bags and wet blankets shall be placed on it, respectively; thus, the diffusion and leakage of the object shall have been prevented. i) The surrounding area of the substance is isolated. Passengers shall be kept at least 3 m away from the substance. j) Excessive movement around the substance shall be avoided in order to prevent the release of the material. k) In the event that clothes are contaminated by the substance, then such clothes shall be sealed upon putting them into a polyethylene bag available in the Dangerous Goods Kit. l) It must be tried to detect the harm caused by the substance. m) Any persons, who have contacted with the substance, must be listed. n) Further information about the substance shall be reported to flight crew members through only interphone. o) The information on the terms of evacuation and quarantine for the passengers is given by the flight crew to the cabin crew during landing. It is ensured that the crew members and passengers of the flight are gathered in an isolated area after deboarding.  10.3.3.2. Detection of Suspicious Envelopes/Objects  a) Flight crew members must be informed as soon as possible. b) Flight crew must use their own oxygen system. c) It shall be ensured that passengers and cabin crew members receive oxygen from the cabin oxygen system through the response from cockpit. d) Protective materials (gloves, masks, etc.) shall be used. e) The surrounding area of the substance is isolated. Passengers are kept away from the object. f) The object shall not be moved. g) The suspicious envelope or object must not be shaken or emptied. h) The object shall immediately be covered with the most suitable material available. Thereafter, any barrier shall be established in order to stop the contact of the object with the air. After laying dry blanket on the substance, plastic bags and wet blankets shall be placed on it, respectively; thus, the diffusion and leakage of the object shall have been prevented. i) It shall be ensured that passengers will close their mouths and noses (through the headrests, if any). j) In case of any contact with the object, then hands and arms must immediately be washed with clean water. k) Contact and excessive movement around the object shall be avoided in order to prevent the release of the object. l) Any persons, who have contacted with the substance, must be listed. m) Further information about the substance shall be reported to flight crew members through only interphone. Hijacking  It shall be taken into consideration that crew members may suffer from hijacking despite all measures taken at the airports. The profile of a hijacker can be classified into broad categories: 1. Asylum seekers, 2. Criminals, 3. Political motivated, 4. Terrorists, 5. Mentally instable persons, 6. Others.  10.4.1. Phases of Hijacking  a) Intimidation Phase As for the hijacker’s behavioral pattern;  instigates fear, is violent and aggressive, is fiercely vengeful, is nervous.  Purpose of hijacker:  seize the control, prevent resistance, arouse respect.  Reactions of Passengers and Crew Members:  Fear, panic, astonishment, anger  Targets of passengers' and crew members' behaviors:  Be a good hostage, Not to attract attention, Pass to the "hostage phase" as soon as possible.  b) Hostage Phase As for the hijacker’s behavioral pattern;  S/he will consider the hostages objectively, S/he will consider the hostages as a tool to achieve her/his target, S/he will desire to communicate with the "Officials" and the "Crew".  Reactions of Passengers and Crew Members: E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 209 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250
=== Sayfa 212 ===
Despair, worry, Sense of belonging to society, Three syndromes may be observed (Stockholm, London, J. Wayne syndromes).  (A) Stockholm Syndrome  Subconscious sympathy developed following the positive communication established between hijacker and hostage for a while. It will cause not to trust in the "Officials". It will make the person feel an instant connection with the "enemy". Violence will remain at the minimum level.  (B) London Syndrome  Exact opposite of Stockholm Syndrome (desire of hostages to be killed by the hijacker). Any hostage, who does not collaborate with the hijackers, may become the target of them. Political or moral/ethical arguments may be generated. Instant returns to the "Phase of Intimidation" may occur.  (C) John Wayne Syndrome  Emotion of despair which is mostly felt by males. They, mostly, cannot fight back while desiring to be a hero. They feel depressed, despairing, and self-hatred.  c) Decision Phase The incident will conclude:  through the conciliation on gradual basis, through the act of rescue team or a hostage.  10.4.2. Code of Conduct of Cabin Crew  In case of hijacking, it is important that cabin crew members identify the number of hijackers as well as their appearances, locations and types of weapons, if any, and that they inform the flight crew about such details through interphone or by use of hijacking warning system (ECAS), depending on the aircraft type, and that ensure the continuity of the flow of accurate information.  10.4.2.1. General Code of Conduct  a) Cabin crew members shall inform the flight crew as soon as possible. b) TURN OFF the airshow as soon as possible. c) Pay attention that the displays, which indicate the status of doors on the cabin crew check panels, depending on the aircraft type, are not open. d) Do not move suddenly. e) Avoid talking about political issues. f) Do not act as if you take precedence of hijacker. g) Do not argue or obstinate. h) Do not act as if s/he is insane. i) Do not interrupt the hijacker. j) Do not provoke the hijacker. k) Do not try to grab her/his gun. l) Do not arbitrate for the hijacker. m) Do not serve alcoholic beverages to the passengers and hijacker. n) Do not serve through trolley. o) Protect yourselves from three syndromes.  (A) CONTROL YOURSELVES  Keep carrying out your duties. Have your meal when enabled. Be on the move. Work slowly. Protect yourselves. Be alert considering that there may be any rescue operation at any moment. Enable the crew members to rest due to the fact that the hijacking process may last long.  (B) CONTROL PASSENGERS  Do not allow the passengers to have a direct contact with the hijacker. Discourage the passengers from attacking to the hijacker. Remember that some other hijackers may have hidden among passengers. Distract attention of the passengers, satisfy their needs and cheer them up. Treat all passengers as if they are the passengers of same class. Consume food and drinks economically. Serve the product (hot course) first, which easily deteriorate. Ensure that the used service materials are kept.  (C) CONTROL THE HIJACKER  Try to communicate, but do not force her/him to do so. Allow the hijacker to talk to one of the crew members whom s/he will choose. Blame the officials for any delays. Try to reduce the hijacker's panic. Offer food and drink to hijacker. Remind him/her that any services such as food, beverage, water and air conditioning may be requested from outside. Enable the release of some hostages (elders, sick passengers, infants and women) by raising reasonable excuses. Thus, both bargaining power of the hijacker will decrease, and the flow of information provided to the officials will have been accelerated. Also, consumption of water and food on board the aircraft will be reduced.  10.4.2.2. Before the Operation  Maintain the general code of conduct until the operation begins. "Disarm" the slides of all doors without waiting for any command. Ensure that the seats, which are placed in front of all exits, are emptied, by raising reasonable excuses. In the event that it is required to provide information, then the names as well as the methods and techniques used, must not be mentioned. The flow of information in respect of occupational matters must not be provided to any persons, who are not included in such occupation, even if not being on duty.  10.5. Unruly Passenger  In accordance with all requirements specified in   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operations Regulations CAT.GEN.MPA.175, DK.22.115 SHT-  OPS | Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Air Operations ANNEX-4 Commercial Air Transportation (Chapter-CAT),  DK.41.001 IOSA Standards Manual (ISM) CAB 3.4.2, unruly passenger, unruly passenger is the passenger who Acts in a manner that may jeopardize the security/safety of the aircraft, flight employee and/or passengers, a) Acts in a manner that may damage the aircraft equipment or crew materials, and that jeopardizes the flight safety/security and equipment of the crew, b) Develops an attitude that will prevent the employee from carrying out their duties or may cause a reduction in their performances, c) Attacks flight and ground employees or any passenger on board the aircraft verbally or physically, d) Acts in a manner that may cause loss of life and property on board the aircraft, e) Does not observe the instructions given by the Commander or any person(s) authorized by the Commander on board the aircraft, f) Smokes, uses tobacco products and electronic cigarette, etc. in the lavatories or at any other aircraft sections where the security of the aircraft may be jeopardized, g) Damages any emergency equipment such as smoke detector, etc. by deactivating them, h) Uses any electronic devices on board the aircraft during the periods when they are not allowed to be used, i) Abuses any person sexually on board the aircraft, j) Damages the property of aircraft with behavior such as damaging the seats, and breaking the panels, E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 212 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250

k) Gives inaccurate information, which may jeopardize the security of the aircraft, or uses any sentences and expressions, which may mislead the officials, l) Insists on disobeying any kind of national and international regulations required to be observed legally, and any instructions given by the concerned employee in accordance with such regulations. If the unruly passengers are under the influence of alcohol or drugs, then it is observed that such passengers have a weak mental health. a) Such passengers may act potentially in a violent manner that may jeopardize the security of life and property of passengers and crew members. b) They may damage the aircraft, or the equipment available on board the aircraft. c) They may hinder the crew members from carrying out their duties, and may interfere in the crew members, and may cause the crew members to reduce their performances. d) They may act aggressively, nervously, disrespectfully and immorally on board the aircraft. Levels of Threat  In accordance with all requirements specified in   DK.41.001 IOSA Standards Manual (ISM), CAB 3.4.2, the definitions of threat levels serve as a reference to classification of the relevant incident in relation to the flight security on board the aircraft, and any measures to be taken by ground personnel/flight crew members. The first phase of the measures to be taken is the fact that cabin crew members determine the level of any threat, which may occur on board the aircraft. In the event that any cabin crew member detects any passenger, who acts in a threatening/suspicious manner, then s/he must immediately provide short and clear information to the flight crew without any comment/assumption. It would be more appropriate that the flow of information to the flight crew in relation to any incident occurred in the cabin is performed by any Cabin Crew Member, who is not included in the incident, and who detects as an observer. In the event that communication established with the passenger fails, then the Cabin Crew Member must transfer the communication duty to another Cabin Crew Member. Thus, it shall have been ensured that the level of the threat will not increase, and any situation, which may be simply solved, will not be magnified. The threat levels are defined in 4 categories within such practice. In accordance with all requirements specified in DK.31.023 ICAO  Annex 6 | Operation Of Aircraft - Aeroplanes (Part I / Part II), unruly passengers shall be assessed under such threat levels.  Level 1- Unruly behavior (suspicious or verbal threat) Level 2- Physical abuse/attack Level 3- Life threatening attacks Level 4- Entering the cockpit/Attempting to enter the cockpit  Passenger behavior defined under such categories may remain at the threat level that it starts, or may have always the potential for climbing the next level. Any 'unruly passenger' behavior, which is intentionally initiated under the "unruly passengers" category, may have been planned as the first stage of any hijacking.  10.5.2.1. Threat Level 1 – Unruly Behavior (Suspicious or Verbal Threat)  The following behaviors shall be defined under the Threat Level 1: a) Verbal disturbance of other passengers/personnel by the passenger. b) Smoking. c) Use of electronic devices. d) Disregarding the rules applicable to potential contagious diseases. e) Extreme and annoying behaviors under the influence of alcohol and drug consumption. f) Threatening behavior and suspicious behaviors in the body language. g) Disobeying the rules and keeping on such behavior despite the warnings of crew members. There is no violence and physical abuse under such threat level.  10.5.2.2. Threat Level 2 - Physical Abuse/Attack  The following behaviors shall be defined under the Threat Level 2: a) Physical disturbance of other passengers/personnel by the passenger. b) Damaging the aircraft/equipment. c) Damaging the properties of any other persons. There is violence threat, which may occur within a short period of time, under such threat level, and any molesting and physical abuse incidents shall also be assessed under such threat level. Since Threat Level 2 includes physical force, there is potential to easily climb to Threat Level 3.  10.5.2.3. Threat Level 3 - Life Threatening Attacks  The following behaviors shall be defined under the Threat Level 3: a) Any threat assessment under such type shall generally be performed through existence of any weapon. In the event that the weapon is hidden, then cabin crew must try all secure methods in order to define such weapon. Such weapons may be guns, explosives, knives, chemical or biological weapons, gas, flammable liquids, cables or cordons, aircraft materials, etc. Cabin crew members must assess the situation bearing in mind that there may be any weapon, starting from the fact that behavior of the attacker causes any life- threatening situation; hijacking may have been initiated. Flight crew shall request landing clearance for the closest station as much as possible. b) Crew/passenger injury. c) Bomb threat.  10.5.2.4. Threat Level 4 - Entering the Cockpit/Attempting to Enter the Cockpit  The following behaviors shall be defined under the Threat Level 4: a) Any action to be taken in order to enter the cockpit is the most important threat to occur during the flight. b) Attempting to enter the cockpit shall also be included in such threat level. The fact that any unruly passenger insists on entering the cockpit shall also be assessed under the Threat Level 4. Cabin crews take all measures in order to prevent the person from entering the cockpit.  10.5.3. Threat Level Checklist Items for Cabin Crew  Cabin crew shall behave in compliance with the threat level. There are some common behaviors under all threat levels. In the event that threat levels increase, then crew members are required to change their behaviors accordingly. Table-24: Threat Level Checklist Items for Cabin Crew  Threat Level 1  Try to control the situation by using "Handling Difficult Situations" techniques. Inform the flight crew in order to disembark the relevant passenger if the situation cannot be controlled.  Threat Level 2   Try to control the situation by using "Handling Difficult Situations" technique. Use "Separation Technique" in order to avoid any damage to the passengers and crew members. Inform the flight crew in order to disembark the relevant passenger if the situation cannot be controlled. Threat Level 3  Use   "Separation   Technique"   and   "Self-Defense   Responses"   techniques   in   order   to   protect   crew members and passengers, if and when so required. Restrain the passenger by using physical restraint techniques and tools. Inform the flight crew in order to disembark the relevant passenger if the situation cannot be controlled. Evacuate the aircraft together with passengers, if and when required. If the flight crew has left the aircraft; Try to communicate with the ground employee and authorities available outside the aircraft. Use any techniques regarding survival of the hostages, if and when required. Initiate the evacuation in case of suspicion/detection of any explosives. Act in accordance with the instructions of the authorized employee on the ground. Check if there is need for medical attention.  Threat Level 4  Inform the flight crew immediately. Initiate the evacuation if required. Try to minimize the damage caused by the threat by utilizing all sources, if evacuation is not possible.  DURING TAXIING Threat Level 1  Try to control the situation by using "Handling Difficult Situations" technique. Inform the flight crew in order to disembark the relevant passenger if the situation cannot be controlled.  Threat Level 2  Try to control the situation by using "Handling Difficult Situations" technique. Use "Separation Technique" and "Self-Defense Responses" techniques in order to avoid any damage to passengers and crew members. Inform the flight crew members about the matter in order to call for support, if the situation cannot be controlled. Restrain the passenger by using the techniques and tools specified in Chapter 10.6 Physical Restraint. Check if there is need for medical attention.  Threat Level 3   Inform the cockpit about the type of threat, the number, location and physical appearance of the attackers, and the type and number of their weapons, if any. Use "Separation Technique" and "Self-Defense Responses" techniques in order to avoid any damage to passengers and crew members. Restrain the passenger by using physical restraint techniques and tools. Ensure the control and order in the cabin. Use any techniques regarding survival of the hostages, if any. In case of existence of any explosives on board the aircraft, or any suspicion for existence of any explosives, then: E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 216 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250

Inform the flight crew immediately. Do not touch, move, cover the suspicious objects/explosives. Apply evacuation procedure. Check if medical assistance is required.  Threat Level 4  Inform the flight crew immediately. Try to minimize the damage caused by the threat by utilizing all sources. Call for help by utilizing all sources available (mobile phone, aircraft telephone, etc.). Evacuate the aircraft if possible.  DURING FLIGHT Threat Level 1  Control the situation by communicating with the passenger, and try to suppress fear factor. Inform the flight crew and other Cabin Crew Members immediately about threatening passenger. Use interphone to communicate with flight crew members. Do not open the cockpit door under any circumstances. Keep on observing the other passengers (incidents that seem to be Level 1 may be intended to distract attention in respect of hijacking plan). Give "unruly passenger form" to the passenger when deemed necessary. Determine ABP and inform them in order to block the area called "Clear Zone". Assign the passenger chosen as ABP to only block "clear zone" area, and control the incident occurred in the cabin as a cabin crew member. Ensure the cabin security again by verbal commands, if and when required, upon controlling the incident. Report the incident in detail through the company report. In such case, cabin crew shall inform the cockpit immediately through interphone. Cockpit door shall never be opened. Cabin crew shall assess the situation, and shall take any measures in order to prevent threat level from climbing. No one is allowed to enter the cockpit unless the threatening case is overcome.  Threat Level 2   Control the situation by communicating with the passenger, and try to suppress fear factor. Inform the flight crew and other Cabin Crew Members about the fact that threat level has climbed. Use interphone to communicate with flight crew members. Use Separation Technique. Do not open the cockpit door under any circumstances. Keep on observing the other passengers (the incident occurred may be intended to distract attention in respect of hijacking plan). Determine ABP and inform them in order to block the area called "Clear Zone". Assign the passenger chosen as ABP to only block "clear zone" area, and control the incident occurred in the cabin as a cabin crew member. Ensure the cabin security again by verbal commands, if and when required, upon controlling the incident. Ask for help from other cabin crew members and passengers. The Commander shall inform the station officials about the matter through the promptest means of communication. S/he may decide to land on the closest airport. In case of observation of any symptoms indicating that threat level 2 may climb to threat level 3 or 4, then: Provide "Clear Zone" through the assistance of the passengers who have been informed about the matter. Make sure that the passengers are sitting on their seats. Put the trolley in front of the cockpit door in order to prevent to enter the cockpit.  Threat Level 3  Inform the flight crew about the type of threat, the number, location and physical appearance of the attackers, and the type and number of their weapons, if any, through interphone. Inform the other Cabin Crew Members immediately about threatening behaviors. Stop serving. Determine any able-bodied passenger (ABP) to block the area called "Clear Zone", and assign him/her to only block "clear zone" area. Control the incident as a cabin crew member. If there is “hostage”, use diversion and distraction methods to gain time. Do not avoid using force in order to control threatening person(s). Restrain the passenger by using physical restraint techniques and tools. Apply "Bomb Threat Procedure", if and when required, against the possibility for existence of any explosives. Ensure the cabin security again by verbal commands, if and when required, upon controlling the incident. The Commander shall declare emergency, and initiate the preparations for landing.  Threat Level 4  Inform the flight crew about the type of threat, the number, location and physical appearance of the attackers, and the type and number of their weapons, if any, through interphone. Inform the other Cabin Crew Members immediately about threatening behaviors. Call for help through PA, if possible. Use all methods to protect cockpit. Do not avoid using force in order to control threatening person(s). Restrain any threatening person/persons by using physical restraint techniques and tools. The Commander shall declare emergency, and initiate the preparations for landing.  10.6. Physical Restraint  Any unruly passengers who may jeopardize the flight security and who damage flight crew, other passengers and even himself/herself, and who resort to physical violence intentionally or unintentionally, must be restrained by using physical restraint method, if and when required. In case of existence of any unruly passengers, cabin crew members must try to establish verbal communication with such passengers, and must control the incident by using effective communication techniques. However, it has been definitely specified under the national and international regulations that any behaviors, which will jeopardize the security of the flight and the persons on board the aircraft, shall not be tolerated in any way. It must be kept in mind that any passenger may behave unruly in order to distract attention of the crew members, and that such unruly behavior may occur prior to potential hijacking incident. Passengers shall be observed by the cabin crew members actively in all phases of flight beginning from the boarding prior to the flight. All crew members must be informed about any abnormal or suspicious behaviors. E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 218 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250
=== Sayfa 221 ===
In case of any unruly passengers, the cockpit door must never be opened in order to provide information about such unruly passengers. In respect of physical restraint practices, no assistance must be requested from the Flight Crew Members assigned, except the flight crew members who travel on passenger seats due to deadhead flight duty. It shall be ensured that any unruly passengers will be handcuffed and restrained by team work to be performed by using "Restraint Kit" available on board the aircraft in cases of threat level 3 or 4. Handcuffing method must be applied to the persons, who pass through the phase of causing physical damage, and who have the opportunity, capability and intention to perform this act. In respect of any kinds of unruly behaviors excluded from such conditions, the procedures other than the physical restraint shall be applied. However; any passengers, who resort to physical violence by sitting their seat as fastened, may not be restrained by using handcuff.  10.6.1. Principles to be applied to any Passenger Restrained Physically by use of Handcuff  a) Cabin crew members shall assess the situation, and shall decide that the person restrained physically by use of handcuff, will be kept at the place where s/he is handcuffed, or will be seated on any empty seat. b) It shall be checked that the handcuff of the passenger, who is restrained by using physical restraint method, is not too loose or tight, and the relevant passenger must be made comfortable as far as possible. c) Safety belt of the passenger shall be kept fastened. d) Back and hands of the passenger shall be supported by pillows. e) The passenger is not allowed to go to lavatory under any circumstances. f) No food shall be served to the passenger (considering the risk of choking or any possible medical intervention). g) Only water shall be given to passenger upon request. It is safer to serve water with straws, if possible, for cabin crew members (it must be kept in mind that drinking too much water increases the need to use the lavatories). h) It shall not be acted in a manner to prevent the passenger handcuffed from breathing (taping their mouth or using other objects to close their mouth). i) Any Able-Bodied Passenger (ABP) shall be selected for the passenger handcuffed prior to landing, and a briefing shall be performed. Scissors available in the Restraint Kit shall be given to ABP. j) In the event that Commander decides to land on the closest airport, the decision on the airport to be landed shall be announced to the passengers. ABP BRIEFING a) It shall be ensured that all handcuffs, except the one covering their hands, will be cut, and that they will get “Semi Brace” position, prior to landing. b) In respect of any emergency landing, ABP shall cut the handcuff with a scissor after the evacuation of all passengers, and the evacuation shall be performed. ISSUING FLIGHT INCIDENT REPORT Considering the legal aspect of the incident, it is of utmost importance to keep   FR.73.0031 On-Board Unruly Passenger Report (On  Ground/In Flight) and   FR.73.0066 On Ground in Flight Incident Report, and to complete the required documents in full. a) Crew members shall be obliged to specify each and every phase of the incident and all details for the threat level requiring physical restraint practice (time, all words used, persons involved in the incident, the location where the incident occurred on board the aircraft, etc.) in the report. b) Report must include the testimonies of 3 witnesses apart from the crew members, if possible. c) It is of great importance to specify in the report that the "Last Warning" (Is there anything else I can do for you?), which is considered as initial of the handcuffing process, has been made, and that such warning has been made by the cabin crew members in the written statements of witnesses. d) It must be made sure that any personal contact details such as address, telephone number, etc. are not specified in the report. e) The report must be issued in English. AFTER LANDING a) All other passengers shall sit on their seats. Emergency System and Equipment and Technical Equipment Checks before Flight Operation  10.7. International Regulations  The Commander shall be authorized to take any measures and actions for ensuring the safety and order on board, and, to that end, to give orders and instructions to the passengers, employees, and the other persons on board, and to offload the persons, who disrupt the safety and order, if and when required, in accordance with Tokyo Convention, national and international Civil Aviation Regulations, and any other international agreements, contracts and conventions. In the event that the Commander rightfully considers that any passenger on board the aircraft: has committed or is about to commit any crime violating the penal codes; has completed or is about to complete any action, which has jeopardized or may jeopardize the security of the aircraft, or the persons or properties available on board the aircraft, and which disturbs the order and discipline on board the aircraft, whether it constitutes any crime, or not, then the commander may take any required measures, including the physical restraint, with the purpose of: a. Ensuring the security of the aircraft, or the persons or properties available on board the aircraft; b. Maintaining the order and discipline on board the aircraft; c. Ensuring disembarkation of such person, and delivery of him/her to the competent authorities. The Commander may request assistance from other crew members, or may authorize them as well as may request assistance from the passengers/may authorize the passengers provided that s/he will not oblige them to do so, in respect of taking any physical restraint measures, in accordance with Article 6 of Tokyo Convention. Any flight/cabin crew member may take any reasonable preventive measures without such permission if s/he has justifiable reasons to consider that the aircraft, or the passengers or properties on board the aircraft must be secured. The Commander must inform the competent authorities of the government, as soon as possible prior to landing, about the fact that the aircraft will land together with a passenger, who has been subjected to the physical restraint measure pursuant to the regulations of the Tokyo Convention, and must inform them about the reasons of such measure. Neither Commander or cabin crew members nor passengers may be held responsible under any proceeding in relation to any practices, suffered by the person for whom such measures are taken, due to any measures taken in compliance with the Tokyo Convention. Contracting states shall pay attention required for flight safety and any other benefits while taking any measures for any proceedings and arrest due to any crime committed on board the aircraft, or exercising their authorities, and shall act in a manner to prevent the aircraft, passengers, flight crew members, and load of the aircraft from delaying unnecessarily.  10.7.1. References of National and International Civil Aviation Regulations  All requirements specified in   DK.33.019 Commission Regulation (EU) No 18-2010; all requirements specified in DK.31.041 ICAO Annex  17 | Aviation Security - Safeguarding International Civil Aviation Against Acts Of Unlawful Interference, all requirements specified in  DK.31.023 ICAO Annex 6 | Operation Of Aircraft - Aeroplanes (Part I / Part II), all requirements specified in   DK.31.013 Aviation Security  Manual (Doc.   8973 – Restricted), all requirements specified in   DK.32.001 ECAC.CEAC Doc 30, Part I | ECAC Policy Statement İn The Field Of Civil Aviation Facilitation, the requirements specified in   DK.41.001 IOSA Standards Manual (ISM) Table 5.1–Operations Manual (OM) Content Specifications, all requirements specified in   DK.21.301 Tokyo Convention on Offenses and Certain Other Acts Committed on Board Aircraft; all requirements specified in   DK.22.111 National Civil Aviation Security Program (NCASP); all requirements specified in   EK.10.15.001 Security Program; all requirements specified in   DK.22.020 SHT 17.1 Instruction on Access to All Airports Card, all requirements specified in   DK.22.019 Instruction on Civil Aviation Security Training and Certification (SHT-17.2). 11. Reports and Reporting  11.1. Information Transfer 11.1.1. Responsibility of the Crews for Reporting 11.1.1.1. Responsibility of Cabin Crews for Reporting to Flight Crew  The cabin crew gives the Commander information on the situations defined below throughout the flight operation: Any technical defect, system error and inadequacy of materials, including also the emergency equipment and systems of the aircraft, which may affect the airworthiness and flight safety of the aircraft negatively; Any situation and incident which jeopardizes/may jeopardize the flight safety and security, or which may pose a threat requiring taking preventive measures.  11.1.1.2. Responsibility of Cabin Crews for Reporting to Cabin Crew Directorate  The Cabin Chief reports, through electronic form,   FR.71.0070 CCD Correspondence Form or DCMS, any SAFA/SANA/SACA/Enroute inspections and security inspections as well as any irregularities or abnormal incidents which have occurred on board or during performance of the flight operation to Cabin Crew Directorate. Additionally, all Cabin Crew Members report all incidents required to be reported through electronic form or   FR.71.0070 CCD Correspondence Form. The cabin crew reports any safety- and security-related incidents/accidents and/or near misses had by the Company through the Safety Reporting System (SRS) as defined within the scope of the requirements specified in the Chapter 3 “Management Systems” and  EK.10.21.001 Safety Management Manual. The principles relating to repair, if possible/necessary, or recording of the defects detected in the cabin before the flight are described in EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual, Section 8.1.3.3.1. Cabin Maintenance Log (CML). The management of all reports and feedbacks sent from the cabin crew to Cabin Crew Directorate is defined in PR.71.063 Procedure  for Management of Reports/Reporting in Relation to Cabin Operation Processes. Reports are submitted through the forms available in TK Portal/Cabin Crew Directorate/E-Form center. The report subjects must match the issues dealt with by the relevant managements. DCMS (Digital Cabin Management System) is the name of the entire system used by the Cabin Chiefs to transfer the completed forms and application data concerning the flight duty to digital environment by means of a tablet PC. Through DCMS, the Cabin Chiefs can send the necessary reports through the forms defined in this system. The principles and methods related to use of the tablet PCs given to the Cabin Chiefs by Cabin Crew Directorate during the flight operation process are available in TL.71.008 Instruction on Cabin Crew  Directorate Tablet Computer Operational Use.  11.1.2. Addresses and Times for submitting the Reports  All cabin crew members must submit all incidents requiring information transfer to the Cabin Crew Directorate as soon as possible (within a period of maximum 48 hours following the flight transferring to the main base), through TK Portal/Cabin Crew Directorate/E- Form Center page, by using the electronic form for any matters included in the specified headers, and by using FR.71.0070 CCD  Correspondence Form for any matters not covered by the headers. In the event that information transfer is required to be submitted urgently, then the e-mail address may be used; however, the report must also be submitted through the identified system/reporting field. The reports containing operational safety and security matters shall be submitted through the Safety Reporting System (SRS) in accordance with the principles defined in Chapter 3 Management Systems. Principles regarding the notification of all kinds of incidents, accidents and occurrence reporting that affect flight safety are defined in   EK.10.21.001 Safety Management Manual. Any incidents, occurring out of the main base and requiring any kinds of information transfer, shall be reported to the Commander, primarily, and to the Cabin Crew Directorate by telephone/e-mail as soon as possible. Reports shall be submitted in max. 48 hours after returning to the main base. In cases where   FR.73.0031 On-Board Unruly Passenger Report (On The Ground/In-Flight ) form cannot be filled out digitally, the printed form is filled out, and one copy each of the forms such as   FR.73.0031 On-Board Unruly Passenger Report (On The Ground/In-Flight), etc.   filled out during the flight is delivered to the Commander. The Cabin Chief submits all forms (catering waybill, co-mail, UM, Deportee, etc.), a copy of which is retained by the cabin chief for three (3) months, upon request. The headings of the subjects to be reported to Turkish DGCA by the Company departments are defined in   LS.10.18.008 Authority  Reporting and Approval List as per   PR.10.18.023 Procedure for Authority Reporting and Approval. 11.1.3. Responsibility of the Cabin Chief for Assessing  Cabin Chiefs assesses the success rate of cabin crews' professional competences, service performances, managerial competences, attitude and behavior competences, compliance with the corporate identity and ethical values, and informs Cabin Crew Directorate about their assessments accordingly. The criteria for evaluation of performances of cabin crews and the principles for implementation are defined in   EK.10.71.006 Flight Based Evaluation System Manual, PR.71.001 Cabin Crew Member Performance Evaluation Procedure whereas the methods and principles to be followed in relation to the Cabin Crew Evaluation System on Flight Basis are defined in   PR.10.71.001 Procedure for Implementation of Cabin Crew Flight Based Evaluation System.  11.1.4. Passenger Feedback  The cabin crews report the feedbacks on incidents, which they have experienced personally or just witnessed, and which might lead to passenger complaints, even if the passengers state that they do not complain, by selecting the "Passenger Relations Reporting" heading in the Cabin Report through DCMS by providing a valid passenger contact information if possible. In case of any system- related problem, on the other hand, they report it by using the relevant e-form on TK Portal/Cabin Crew Directorate/E-Form Center page or   to   the   e-mail   address   of   Cabin   Crew   Directorate/Assistant   Directorate   (Service   and   Performance)/Cabin   Performance   and Competence Development Management/Passenger Relations Supervisory (Cabin) through the Company's e-mail. Procedures to be implemented in case passenger goods are damaged and/or passengers are physically injured in the cabin due to the negligence and responsibility of the Company have been defined in   PR.10.41.004 Procedure For Assessing Passenger Irregularities Within The Scope  Of Insurance Coverage. The coordination of the feedbacks provided through the Customer Relations Management, Stations, Insurance Management and Company evaluation surveys, the procedures for receiving, evaluating, and answering the passenger feedbacks delivered to the Passenger Relations Supervisory (Cabin) are defined in   PR.71.049 Procedure For Passenger Relations Management. The cabin crews may send their suggestions, which they think to have positive effects on the passenger satisfaction, to the Passenger Relations Supervisory (Cabin) e-mail address through the Personal Suggestion System and/or the Company’s e-mail.  11.1.5. Evaluation  Any kind of incident report submitted to Cabin Crew Directorate by the cabin crews shall be finalized upon being evaluated by the concerned manager and supervisors in accordance with   PR.71.063 Procedure for Management of Reports/Notices in Relation to Cabin  Operation Processes.  11.2. Birth/Death on Board  Detailed information on birth/death incidents on board is given in the requirements specified in   EK.10.67.001 Ground Operations  Manual (GOM) , Section 1.10. Birth/Death on Board and Section 1.10.3 Bomb Threat Calls and   EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part-A, Section 8.3.19.3 Death on Board and Section 8.3.19.4 Birth on Board.  11.2.1. Birth On Board  a) The Commander shall report the onboard birth event to station officials at the nearest arrival station by means of IOCC (ACARS, HF, etc.). b) Station officials must inform the law enforcement officers, airport authorities and health units. c) Upon landing, Commander shall inform the station officials about the details below: Date and time of birth (hour, minute), Location of birth (coordinates), Gender, Names of the mother and father, Nationality and birth places of the mother/father, Home address of the mother/father, Witnesses of the birth, if any. d)   FR.73.0068 Birth Onboard– Death Onboard Report available in the cockpit and provided as an example is drawn up in two (2) copies and signed by two witnesses, the Commander, and the Cabin Chief upon completion of such incident. Such report shall be submitted to the station official/manager in order to be forwarded to the Sales Manager. e) Notification of birth on board incidents by the Commander shall be made in accordance with   EK.10.73.001 Operation Manual Part- A ,Section 8.3.19.4 Birth on Board. 11.2.2. Death Onboard  Only a medical doctor may confirm an in-flight death, or approve stopping of the life support. If there is a physician on board, who can give a written confirmation of death, the flight may be continued to the destination aerodrome upon decision of the Commander. In such a case: 1. Inform the Commander. 2. Pay the utmost attention and respect to the deceased passenger. 3. Secure the deceased passenger with seat belts on the adjacent seats that are nearest to the intervention place. 4. Cover the deceased passenger with a blanket completely, and preserve their privacy. 5. Send the other passengers away from that place, if possible. a) The Commander shall report the onboard death event to station officials at the nearest arrival station by means of IOCC (ACARS, HF, etc.). b) The officials of the Company shall report the death on board to the following authorities: Local security officers and airport authorities, Authorities of Turkish Foreign Affairs (if any), Medical teams. Station officials shall submit the incident to the concerned authorities through a report. Station management ensures the completion of any required legal procedures in relation to the death. c) After landing, the Commander shall complete   FR.73.0068 Birth Onboard–Death Onboard Report by specifying the following details, and submit this report to the station officials. Full name, gender, nationality, date of birth, address, departure and arrival station of the deceased passenger Any details for the death such as the cause of death (if known), time of death, the altitude at which the death has occurred (cabin- aircraft), type of medical intervention if administered, any cases observed by the cabin crew inside the aircraft, which are considered to cause the death, Name(s) and surname(s) of the person(s) accompanying the deceased person, If there is a medical doctor in the flight, who has confirmed the death, their name and surname, diploma number and contact details are recorded, The health team and the security personnel shall meet the aircraft at the first airport landed on after the death incident. All passengers shall stay in the aircraft until the death is confirmed. After it is verified by the security personnel that there is nothing suspicious, the other passengers are permitted to disembark the aircraft; the passengers accompanying the deceased passenger shall not be left alone until the relevant authorities take care of them. It shall be ensured by the health personnel that the deceased passenger and the other passengers accompanying him/her are transferred to the closest health institution. In case of an onboard death; if no physician is available on board, and no confirmation of death can be received; subject to Commander's decision, landing in the closest appropriate airport shall be planned and the same processes shall be implemented  11.3. Cabin Crew Directorate Contact Information  Contact information of Cabin Crew Directorate departments shall be accessed through the TK Portal/Cabin Crew Directorate/Contact link. The relevant departments shall be contacted through Cabin Crew Directorate Call Center (Extension-11911) within business hours (08:00-17:00) on weekdays, or the Cabin Operations Control Supervisory (Extension-15519) within off hours and at weekends.  12. Emergency Medical Kit  In accordance with the requirements specified in   DK.33.001 EASA | Air Operations Regulationsarticles AMC1.CAT.IDE.A.220 First-aid Kit and AMC1.CAT.IDE.A.225 Emergency Medical Kit, first aid kit and emergency medical kit shall be available on board every aircraft. The materials of the first aid and emergency medical kits are available in the kits in accordance with DK.41.001 IOSA Standards Manual  (ISM) Sections CAB.2.2.11 First Aid Kit and CAB.4.2.2.   Medical Kit and as per the requirements specified in   DK.34.004 FAA Part 121 |  Operating Requirements: Domestic, Flag and Supplemental Operations APPENDIX A to PART 121-First Aid Kits and Emergency Medical Kits. The principles of the pre-flight check of the Emergency Medical Kit are available in   EK.10.71.003 Cabin Crew Aircraft Types Manual,  Chapter 6. Emergency Equipment. General  This chapter meets national and international first aid training requirements in accordance with; All requirements in   DK.21.001 First Aid Regulation,  DK.41.001 IOSA Standards Manual (ISM) CAB 2.2.11,  DK.49.010 European Resuscitation Council Guidelines For Resuscitation,  DK.33.008 EASA | Aircrew Regulations | Appendix to Annex V, Appendix 1 to Part-CC The requirements in DK.22.122 SHT-CC Cabin Crew Instruction ANNEX-2 Initial Training Program and Its Assessment. Successful participants shall be provided with the Republic of Turkey Ministry of Health First Aider ID Card and/or European Resuscitation Council Basic Life Support and Defibrillator User Certificate.  14.4. First Aid  First aid is the immediate attention given to any accident or life-threatening case on the scene by using the equipment available (without medical equipment) to save life or to be able to prevent a deterioration of health until paramedic help arrives. Throughout the flight operation, the first aid is applied by the Cabin Crew Members who have the valid first-aider certificate. The important factor in being efficient in emergencies is not panicking and thinking and acting quickly. Your greatest asset is your knowledge and training on how to deal with an emergency situation that requires first aid. In an emergency first aid administration, your first responsibility is to accurately assess the type of illness or injury and then administer the appropriate first aid. In the event that a passenger has several injuries or there is more than one injured passenger, make sure that you identify and administer first aid to the most life-threatening condition first.  14.4.1. Primary Purposes of First Aid  Eliminate the life-threatening situation, Ensure maintenance of vital signs, Prevent a deterioration of ill/injured person's health, Facilitate recovery.  14.4.2. Crew Responsibilities  Crew coordination is essential in administering first aid. First of all, the cabin crew shall check the patient's condition quickly, start the intervention, and provide the entire crew with the information flow. Inform the Commander and the Cabin Chief immediately. Within the scope of the “Smiling Doctors” application, if there is a passenger requiring emergency medical intervention on board, assistance is requested by first checking the passenger manifest. Passengers included in the Smiling Doctors passenger member program are also required to present an ID card or business card. (If there is one of the Smiling Doctors on board, assistance is first requested from that passenger. In case of a negative response or if there is no Smiling Doctor on board, a doctor's announcement shall be made immediately.) Check ID or visiting card of the person who says that s/he is a doctor to make sure s/he is a ‘medical’ doctor; if no relevant identity card can be submitted, inform the Commander of the situation. According to the requirements available in DK.21.160 Law On The Practice Of Medicine And Medical Sciences Law No.1219, no one who is not a Medical Doctor can perform medical intervention on a patient. In the absence of any physician, a Cabin Crew Member's intervention shall be limited to first aid. This first aid does not include administering medicine and injections. At the destination station, the cabin crew's responsibility remains until the arrival of health officers. When Administering First Aid;  Do not leave the ill/injured person. Call the other Cabin Crew Member to assist you. Reassure the ill/injured person and others and abstain from frantic behavior. If possible, talk to the ill/injured person and try to learn about her/his illness. Try to find the health card (Medical warning emblem) of the ill/injured person. This record can either be in her/his bag or tied to her/his wrist, ankle or neck. Give the information obtained from the ill/injured person to the cabin crew that came to assistance and ask for the necessary equipment and supplies (First Aid Kit, Emergency Medical Kit, oxygen cylinder, blanket, pillow, etc.). When the patient is found to be unconscious, a defibrillator is immediately requested and breathing is checked. As the Cabin Crew Member/chief who has obtained the information, give such information to the entire cabin and flight crews, and make the announcement for physician ASAP. Get the necessary permissions from the flight crew; take all the necessary equipment and supplies to the ill/injured person, and assist the first aid. Do not allow incompetent persons to take on the responsibility of first aid. Keep other passengers away from the scene. Inform the Commander immediately so that s/he can decide on whether to ask for a medical assistance at the arrival station or to divert. Ensure that the emergency exits are ready for an intervention until the medical assistance comes to the aircraft. Complete and report all the necessary documents after the intervention. Make sure that the documents have been completed correctly. Deliver the documents to the relevant departments or persons as specified on the documents. When the medical teams get on the aircraft, hand over the ill/injured person to them, and make sure that all the equipment and supplies remain on board the aircraft. In the event that inflight medical equipment is used, inform the Commander of the same. The Pilot in Command checks the Minimum Equipment List (MEL) of the relevant aircraft and, if necessary, creates a record in the Aircraft Maintenance Log (AML) as a defect. While closing the Emergency Medical Kit, First Aid Kit, and Universal Precaution Kit, they shall be sealed with blue seal. No catering seal shall be attached. The seal number is written on the relevant after-use label in the kit, and the label is affixed on the kit. The new kits are handed over by the ground official to the cabin chief of the departure flight if found on board the aircraft. The Emergency Medical Kit, First Aid Kit, and Universal Precaution Kit may not be opened by the cabin crew for checking purpose.  FR.35.0046 Emergency Medical Kit After Use Label for Emergency Medical Kit, FR.35.0117 First Aid Kit After Use Label for First Aid Kit, or FR.35.0053 Precaution Kit Label for Universal Precaution Kit is affixed on the external face of the used kit. In case of an inflight medical emergency, the Commander decides on the use of the Emergency Medical Kit. Cabin crew members follow the validity date of their certificates related to First Aid Applications.  14.4.3. Basic Applications of First Aid  The basic applications of first aid are stated as   Check, Call, Care   (CCC).  Check (C):   The most important thing is to check for potential dangers on the scene and establish a safe environment.  Call (C):   The Incident/Accident shall be reported to required health institutions by the first aider or other persons via telephone as soon as possible. If the situation takes place inside the aircraft, it is necessary to notify the Cabin Chief in charge and the captain pilot of the situation rapidly, and ensure that the announcement is made for a doctor.  Care (C):   Ill/injured persons shall be quickly but calmly cared for on the scene.  14.4.4. Chain of Survival  1. Medic Alert Emblem  Medic Alert Emblem is a tag worn on a bracelet or necklace by persons with chronic conditions. Reasons of Sudden Death  Heart problems, airway obstruction, suffocation, freezing, electric shock, poisoning are causes of sudden death.  14.5. Assessment of Ill/Injured Persons and the Scene 14.5.1. Vital Signs  CONSCIOUSNESS:   Patient's consciousness is perhaps the most reliable factor in evaluating the central nervous system. Under normal conditions, a person shall be responsible to aural and physical stimulants, and are aware of the time, place, their name, surroundings and their status. Changes in this state indicate illness or injury. Conscious → Responds to all stimulants. Level 1 unconsciousness → Responds to verbal and loud stimulants. Level 2 unconsciousness → Responds to painful stimulants (unresponsive to verbal stimulants). Level 3 unconsciousness → Unresponsive to all stimulants (loss of consciousness, comatose).  RESPIRATION:   The number of breaths taken per minute is that person's respiratory rate. The normal respiratory rate is 12-20 per minute for adults, 16-22 per minute for children, and 18-24 per minute for infants. Respiratory rate, intervals and depth are factors to check. Rapid and shallow respiration indicates shock. Hyperventilation, dyspnea and panting respiration indicate partial airway obstruction or lung disease. The patients, feeling suffocated, cannot cough or speak and everyone in this state will instinctively hold their throats. The pulse oximeter device allows observing the percentage of oxygen in the patient's blood. The oxygen saturation value shall remain within the range of 95-99%.  PULSE:   This is the number of pressure beats made by throbs on the artery. Pulse rate, amplitude and regularity shall be assessed. The normal pulse rate in a healthy adult is 60-100 per minute and indicates the heartbeat rate. The normal pulse rate is 100-120 per minute in a child, and 100-140 per minute in a baby. A quick and weak pulse may indicate blood loss-induced shock.  Where to Check the Pulse  Carotid Artery: Both sides of Adam's apple Brachial Artery: The inner side of the arm, the upper side of the elbow (for infants) Ulnar Artery: The inner side of the wrists, the upper part of the thumb (for adults/infants) Leg Artery: In the middle of the dorsum of the feet While checking the ill/injured person’s blood circulation, check the pulse of adults and children on the carotid artery, and the pulse of infants on the brachial artery.  BODY TEMPERATURE:   Normal body temperature is 36.5 °C (97.7 Fahrenheit). Changes in body temperature occur in illness or injuries. These are encountered when the nervous system is overworking e.g., cold and damp skin, blood loss (shock) or loss of temperature. Stimulation of the nervous system results in sweat glands working excessively and veins in the skin contracting; this causes the skin to be cold, pale, moist and sticky. These are the early symptoms of shock and shall be immediately recognized. The cause of dry and hot skin, on the other hand, may be the high temperature or exposure to extreme heat. Digital Body Thermometers are used to measure body temperature. Digital Body Thermometer measures temperature easily, quickly and safely via armpit or mouth. It E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 229 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250
=== Sayfa 232 ===
gives warning through a “beep sound” signal after end of temperature measurement when applied on the patient and accordingly does not vary depending on ambient temperature while reading. Digital Body Thermometer is not disposable, for this reason the tip of the thermometer shall be cleaned using the antiseptic cloth available inside the First Aid Kit before and after measurement. It is closed automatically. It has an LCD screen which facilitates reading the temperature via digital screen. The normal body temperature for the armpit is 36.5 °C. If it is over the normal value, it is regarded as high temperature; if it is under the normal value, it is regarded as low temperature. If it is over 41-42 °C or 34.5 °C and below, it indicates a critical condition. 31 °C and below is fatal.  BLOOD PRESSURE:   It refers to the pressure which the blood circulating inside the body applies to the artery wall. The changes in the blood pressure reflect to the changes in blood volume, the capacity of the veins or the blood pumping efficiency of the heart. Blood pressure may decrease considerably in severe bleeding, heart attack or other shock-related cases. Low blood pressure shows that the amount of blood in the arteries is not sufficient for all organs. As a result, the organs may be damaged severely. Excessive salt intake, stress and obesity are among the causes of elevated blood pressure.  Systolic pressure; indicates the maximum amount of pressure in the arteries while the heart is beating. Its normal values are between 100 - 140 mm Hg.  Diastolic pressure; indicates the minimum amount of pressure in the arteries while the heart is relaxing. Its normal values are between 50 - 100 mm Hg. In many diseases and injuries, both of them change correspondingly; that is either both of them increase or decrease.  If The Blood Pressure Increases:  If the person is conscious, keep her/him in the half-sitting position (You shall never let her/him lie down if s/he is conscious), Loosen the person's collar, tie, belt and the other tight garments, Help her/him take her/his medicine if any.  If The Blood Pressure Decreases:  Let the person lie on her/his back and elevate her/his legs above the heart level (shock position), Give sugared water, fruit juice, etc. (if s/he is conscious and not throwing up).  SKIN COLOR:   Skin color depends on the blood in the skin veins. In dark-skinned people, skin color depends mostly on the pigments in the skin. Such pigments may hide the changes caused from the disease or injury. In dark-skinned people, color changes may be clearly seen in nail folds, white part of eyes (sclera) or inside the mouth. In light-skinned people; if the skin becomes red, white or blue then such case is considered as medically important.  Red color;   may be seen in hypertension (dark red, purple), carbon monoxide poisoning (cerise) and inflammatory diseases (red).  White color;   pale, white or ash gray or gray color is the sign of poor circulation. These are encountered in persons who are in shock, extremely frightened or were exposed to extremely cold temperatures. In such cases, there is not sufficient amount of blood in the skin veins. Besides, pale skin, purple nails and lips are seen in a heart attack.  Bluish Color (cyanosis);   is seen when the blood oxygenation is in bad condition. In such cases, the blood and accordingly the above skin are dark-colored. Cyanosis is the result of airway obstruction or respiratory failure due to insufficient lung functions. Generally, it is seen on the fingertips and around the mouth firstly. It always means that there is not sufficient amount of oxygen and such disorder shall be treated. Besides, jaundice seen in liver failure may also be an example of skin color changes.  SIZE OF THE PUPIL AND LIGHT REFLEX:   Under normal conditions, the eye pupils are both in the same size and have uniform perimeters. Changes in one or both are important. Pupils unequal due to genetic reasons is a rare case. The changes in the pupil size are considered to be a symptom of brain injuries. Such changes are seen in head traumas or paralysis. The persons with central nervous system disorders or drug addicts (opium derivatives such as cannabis) have small pupils in the dim light. Enlarged pupils indicate the loss of consciousness or case of limpness; such enlargements are usually observed immediately after the heart stops (in 30 seconds). However, physical head injuries or psychological mental trauma and previous drug use causes pupils to remain small even in patients whose heart has stopped. If the patient is deceased, her/his pupils will be extremely enlarged and will be unresponsive to light. When the light is directed to the eyes, the pupils immediately become smaller. Such case is not seen in diseases, poisoning, excessive drug use (the substances dulling the central nervous system; e.g., ketamine, ecstasy) and injuries.  CAPILLARY REFILL:   Capillary refill is the term that defines capillary circulation. This is the ability of capillaries to fill with blood. Capillary beds under the nails are the most reliable parts for such test. When pressed, the pink color that is seen under the nail under normal conditions shall be seen again in 2 seconds. If the capillary refill time is more than 2 seconds or such refill does not occur, then it E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 230 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250
=== Sayfa 233 ===
may be a sign of vascular disorder. If the color seen after the capillary refill is blue, then the test is not valid; because this color shows that the capillaries is refilled with the blood from the veins not the arteries.  ABILITY TO MOVE:   If any conscious person(s) cannot move voluntarily, such cases are defined as paralysis. It may be encountered with such cases as a result of diseases or injuries. Paralysis (hemiplegia) may be seen as a result of cerebral bleeding or cerebral thrombosis. Long term use of some medicines may also lead to paralysis.  CAUTION:   If the patient cannot move her/his arms and legs after injury, spinal cord injury will be presumed until proven otherwise. If the patient cannot move her/his legs while not having any difficulty moving her/his arms, this indicates spinal cord injuries below the neck. Such cases are important and shall necessarily be recorded together with the details regarding when they have happened.  RESPONSE TO PAINFUL STIMULANTS:   It is normal that the body is able to respond to any sound(s) or any painful physical examination. However; the patient not screaming and writhing when s/he shall be in pain does not indicate lack of injury. Variant responses to painful stimulants indicate that the healthy senses have been lost due to the injuries or diseases. The Cabin Crew Member administering the first aid shall check patient's response to painful stimulants by squeezing the massage muscles to check the patient's consciousness. For the second assessment, repeat the same process from head to toe in a controlled manner to detect injuries, if any. Excessive pressure shall be avoided. Loss of volitional movements in such limbs as arms and legs caused by injuries or paralysis is accompanied by the loss of senses at such areas. However; sometimes the patients are able to move. The patient complains about numbness and tingling. This shall be considered as a symptom of spinal cord injury, and acts that can worsen the situation shall be avoided. If the loss of sense in any limb is accompanied by a severe pain, the cause of this may be that the main artery of such limb is obstructed. In such cases, pulse cannot be taken. These limbs can be moved, but the patient prefers to keep the limb still due to pain. Patients who are in severe shock, have used excessive amounts of drugs and are hysteric may not feel the pain for a long time after the accident. Such cases are do not depend on the loss of mobility.  14.5.2. Purpose of the Assessment of the Ill/Injured Person  Assessing the severity of diseases or injuries, To identify the priorities for first aid, To identify the first aid method to be applied, To assess the ill/injured person's conditions in order to make an appropriate intervention.  14.5.3. First Assessment Phases of the Ill/Injured Person  Assess the ill/injured person's consciousness by asking kindly "Are you feeling okay?" or touching their shoulder softly. Assessment of the victim's consciousness is important for the next phases. Thus, the first assessment phases of the ill/injured person are as follows: 1. Make sure that the environmental safety is ensured, 2. Check whether the injured person is conscious or not, 3. Check the victim's ABC (Airway-Breathing-Circulation).  14.5.4. Second Assessment Phases of the Ill/Injured Person  After it is realized that the ill/injured person has vital signs through the first examination, the first aider shall examine the ill/injured person thoroughly in the second assessment phase. The second assessment phases are as follows: Obtaining Information Through Conversation: - Introduce yourself, - Learn the ill/injured person's name and, call her/him by her/his name, - Inspire confidence by treating her/him kindly and indulgently, - Eliminate the ill/injured person's fears and relax her/him, - Learn the nature and circumstances of the incident, background of the person, the last food s/he had eaten, the medicines s/he take, and whether s/he has allergy or not. Thorough Examination Shall Be Performed: E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 231 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250
