- Level of consciousness, comprehension, sensation - Respiratory rate, rhythm, depth - Pulse rate, rhythm, intensity - Body or skin temperature, moisture, color  Head:   Examine to find out whether there is any injury or bruise on hair, scalp, head and face as well as whether any fluid or blood comes out of the mouth and nose; then check inside the mouth.  Neck:   Check whether there is any pain, tenderness, swelling or deformity. Take the possibility of neck injury into consideration unless proved otherwise.  Rib Cage:   Examine to find out whether there is any stabbed object, open wound, deformity or bruise; then check whether there is any pain and bleeding or not when pressed softly. Try to find out whether the rib cage expansion is normal or not. Slide your hands to the back of the ill/injured person, while examining the chest; and check the ill/injured person’s back as well.  Abdominal Cavity:   Examine to find out whether there is any stabbed object, open wound, deformity, swelling, bruise, pain and abdominal tenderness or not. Slide your hands to the waist of the ill/injured person and examine; then examine the hip bones, and check whether there is any fracture or injury.  Arms and Legs:   Check whether there is any loss of strength, sense and function, pain, swelling, deformity, fracture and whether the pulse can be measured or not.  NOTE:   After the second assessment phase is performed, choose the appropriate first aid treatment.  14.5.5. Assessment of Scene of Incident  Eliminate the risks of any accident to occur again. Examine scene of the incident to specify the number and types of the ill/injured persons. After scene of the incident is examined in a fast manner; identify the medical intervention treatment to be performed.  14.6. First Aid in case of Impaired Consciousness 14.6.1. Impaired Consciousness/Loss of Consciousness  The case of partial or complete loss of consciousness starting from somnolence (impaired consciousness) to the case of not responding to any stimulant (loss of consciousness), due to a failure in the normal activities of the brain.  Fainting (Syncope):   It refers to the short-time, shallowing and temporary loss of consciousness. It is caused by the decrease in the blood flow to the brain.  Causes of Syncope:  - Fear, extreme excitement  - Heat, fatigue  - Enclosed areas, polluted air  - Standing up suddenly  - Low blood glucose  - Severe infections  Symptoms of Syncope:  - Dizziness, fainting, falling - Numb legs - Mental confusion - Pale face E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 232 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250
=== Sayfa 235 ===
- Feeling cold, sweating - Rapid or weak pulse rate  If the Person feels dizzy:  - Lay the patient down in supine position and elevate her/his legs 30 cm above the head level (Shock Position), - Loosen her/his tight clothes and make sure that s/he rests until feeling better.  If the Person Has Fainted:  - Lay the patient down in supine position and elevate her/his legs 30 cm above the head level (Shock Position), - Check whether the airway is open or not, and ensure that it will not be obstructed, - Loosen her/his tight clothes, - If the patient vomits, keep him/her in lying (recovery) position and check breathing, - Keep onlookers away from the scene.  Coma:   It refers to the long-term loss of consciousness caused by the loss of response to external stimulants and the reflexes such as swallowing and coughing.  Causes of Coma:  - Falling down or tough impacts,  - Head traumas especially,  - Poisoning,  - Excessive alcohol and drug use, - Diabetes, - Liver diseases, - Inflammatory diseases such as convulsion.  Symptoms of Coma:  - Loss of reflexes such as swallowing and coughing, - Loss of responses to laud and painful stimulants, - Urinary and fecal incontinence.  In Case of Loss of Consciousness:  - Check the ill/injured person's vital signs (ABC), - Ask for medical help (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician). - Keep the ill/injured person in recovery position (to keep airway open), and check her/his breathing frequently, - Do not leave the ill/injured person until the medical assistance arrives.  14.6.2. Recovery Position  Check that whether the victim is conscious or not, by means of any laud stimulant(s) or by shaking her/him gently by the shoulders, Loosen her/his tight clothes, Check whether there is any foreign body inside the mouth or not, Check breathing with the look-listen-feel method, E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 233 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250

Check the pulse on the carotid artery, Kneel down on the side of the ill/injured person towards which s/he will be turned, Put the ill/injured person's opposite arm onto her/his opposite shoulder, Bend the leg which is on the opposite side of you in a manner to form a straight angle, Elevate the arm that is on your side above the head level, Turn her/him in one move by holding her/his opposite shoulder and hip, Adjust the upper leg so that both the hip and knee are bent at right angles to support the front, His/her head is brought to a position slightly bent forward (backward*) with the airway open, Bend the knee of the lower leg slightly to support the back, Place the head onto the stretched arm in a manner to bend forward slightly, Keep the person in this position, until the medical assistance (112) arrives, Check her/his breathing and pulse every 3-5 minutes. *The differences compared to the current Guideline and bulletins published by the European Resuscitation Council are indicated.  Figure-26: Recovery Position  14.6.3. Convulsion  It refers to the involuntary contraction of the muscles caused by the electrical discharges in the brain, due to any irritation in the central nervous system.  Causes of Convulsion:   Brain injuries seen as a result of head traumas, brain infections, high fever and some diseases.  Types of Convulsions as per Causes:  Convulsions caused by high fever, Epilepsy.  Convulsions Caused by High Fever It refers to the cases where the body temperature goes over 38 °C as a result of any inflammatory disease. Such cases are common especially in 6-month to 6-year-old children. In that case; First wrap the patient in a wet towel or sheet, If the fever does not decrease with such method, then place them in a bath of room-temperature water, Ask for medical help. (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician)  14.7. Diabetic Diseases 14.7.1. Hypoglycemia  Since, just like oxygen, the brain consistently requires glucose, loss of consciousness and permanent brain damage may occur rapidly when blood glucose remains low. Insulin shock occurs quicker than a diabetic coma, e.g., in a matter of minutes.  Causes of Low Blood Glucose E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 234 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250
=== Sayfa 237 ===
Due to diabetes treatment (excessive insulin intake), After prolonged exercise, Long-term fasting, After meals for persons having undergone intestinal surgery.  Symptoms of Hypoglycemia:   Fear, sweating, rapid pulse rate, trembling, sudden hunger, fatigue, nausea. Symptoms in Case of Hypoglycemia and Long-Term Occurrence: Headache, visual impairment, drowsiness, weakness, difficulty in speaking, confusion, concussion and loss of consciousness.  First Aid Treatment for Hypoglycemia  Check the patient's ABC (Airway-Breathing-Circulation), If s/he is conscious, try to find out whether s/he is diabetic or not. Ask the following questions to the patient or her/his relatives; 1. Have you eaten anything today? 2. Have you taken insulin today? If the patient is conscious and does not vomit, feed her/him with sugar or sugary drinks; even if the symptoms stated above are caused by the intake of excessive amount of sugar, feeding her/him with sugar is less harmless than low level of blood glucose. This is because low blood glucose can cause permanent damage both in the brain and other vital organs. Never use artificial sweeteners such as saccharine. The symptoms of hypoglycemia will disappear in 1-2 minutes after sugar intake. If the patient is unconscious, call for medical assistance (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician) and put them in the recovery position. Try to find the patient's health record and medical warning card.  14.7.2. Hyperglycemia  This refers to cases where the level of blood glucose is above normal levels.  Symptoms of Hyperglycemia:   Frequent thirst, dry mouth, frequent urination, general uneasiness, acetone smell inside the mouth.  First Aid Treatment for Hyperglycemia:  Assess the patient's ABC (Airway-Breathing-Circulation), Ask whether s/he has any medicine and, if any, help her/him to take her/his medicines, Let her/him drink ample water, Monitor the patient's condition frequently, If the patient becomes unconscious, put her/him in recovery position and call for medical assistance. (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician)  14.7.3. Hypoglycemic Attack  Hypoglycemic attacks occur in times of very low blood sugar levels. These attacks may contain dizziness, fainting and seizures. If their consciousness is open and they are not vomiting, give sugar or sugary drinks orally; where consciousness is closed, take them to the recovery position if they are breathing.  14.7.4. Sugar Coma  In a high sugar coma, there is a lack of insulin. It occurs when a person using insulin does not take insulin. As a result of a lack of insulin in the body, blood sugar rises rapidly and damages various organs of the body, resulting in a coma. If the patient is conscious, s/he is asked if s/he has drug or not, if s/he has, s/he is helped to take the drug and plenty of water is given. In the event of unconsciousness, the patient is placed into recovery position if breathing.  14.8. EPILEPSY (CONVULSION)  This is a chronic illness. Some situations may induce an epileptic seizure. For example; long-term fasting, sleeplessness, fatigue, discontinuation or changes of regularly used medicine without doctor approval and hormonal changes may lead to epileptic seizures. In some cases, epileptic seizures may be confused with withdrawal fits seen in drug addicts. Epilepsy patients with recurrent seizures can generally be identified by the cards they carry with them, or by questioning their family members.  Symptoms of Epileptic Seizure:  The patients have early symptoms (prodromes) such as sensing smells that are not there, cramps, etc., which emerge later and are called precursors, Sometimes, the patient shouts, collapses after losing their consciousness severely and suddenly, Intense and widespread cramps may be observed; the patient may stop breathing for 10–20 seconds, Cyanosis is observed in the tissues and on the face, Then, short and widespread cramps, breathing loudly, excreting excessive saliva, and incontinence may be observed, The patient may bite their tongue, bang his head to the ground and be injured; extremely uncontrolled behaviors are observed, At the last stage, the patient regains consciousness, does not know where s/he is, and is sleepy, In some people, epileptic seizures may be seen as the following mild symptoms (pensive look towards a point, involuntary facial expressions and movements, meaningless speech and repetitive movements, loss of memory).  First Aid Treatment for Epileptic Seizures:  Take the required security measures regarding the incident (for example; if the person suffers from an epileptic seizure on the roadway, stop the traffic flow on the road), Do not intervene in the seizure, and do not try to tie up the patient, Do not try to open the patient’s locked jaw, and make sure that she/he does not injure herself/himself, Do not use or make her/him smell something foreign and do not feed her/him with any food or drink, Put something soft under her/his head to prevent her/him from hitting her/his head, Remove everything that may injure the patient from the scene, Loosen her/his tight clothes, and do not forget that the patient may vomit, If any injury occurs by falling, administer required treatment, Ask for medical help. (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician)  CAUTION:   DO NOT MAKE THE PATIENT HAVING AN EPILEPTIC SEIZURE SMELL ONION, COLOGNE, GARLIC, etc., and DO NOT PUT YOUR FINGERS INTO HER/HIS MOUTH!  14.9 Stroke - Paralysis  Stroke is a situation that arises with instant stopping of blood flow to the brain and is characterized with the fast spread of brain function loss signs and symptoms. It is colloquially known as paralysis as well; but not every paralysis is a stroke, because not all of them are cerebrovascular (e.g., poliomyelitis, most of the facial paralysis types).  Symptoms:  Weakness in one or both sides of the body: Mostly it is seen in hands, arms, legs and face. Difficulty in speaking, Loss of feeling: Topognosis, numbness, Changes in consciousness, Sightseeing defects, Dizziness, vertigo, Instant and severe headache. First Aid:  Examine the patient's vital signs (ABC). Avoid jolting, moving and making the person talk. Ask for medical help. (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician)  14.10 Life-Threatening Medical Emergencies 14.10.1. Respiration and Heart Arrest  If a person stops breathing for more than 3-5 minutes, permanent brain damage occurs. A-B-C rule constitutes the most important part of the first aid.  14.10.2. Bleeding  1 L of blood loss constitutes a critical life hazard for adults. This value is much lower for children and the elderly. Bleeding may occur through stools due to reasons such as gastric ulcers.  14.10.3. Shock  All severe injuries, heart diseases, high fever, loss of liquids and electrolytes as well as extreme fear and excitement may induce shock. The symptoms may not be immediately visible or may prove lethal if appropriate precautions are not taken.  14.11. Heart Attack  Causes of Severe Pain in the Chest:  The most common causes of severe pain in the chest are heart spasms (angina pectoris) and heart attacks (myocardial infarction). Both of them are the result of the interruption of blood supply to a part of the cardiac muscle. Genetic factors, age, gender, smoking, stress, irregular nutrition, etc., affect cardiovascular health.  Symptoms of Heart Spasm (Angina Pectoris):  It lasts for a short period and the accompanying pain dies away within 5-10 minutes; shortness of breath or anxiety occurs, The feeling of pain usually starts out in the chest and spreads to the arms, neck, back and jaw, It usually results from physical exercise, physical straining, excitement, sorrow or overeating, Resting will stop the pain; pain continuing while resting however indicates a serious condition, The form or severity of the pain is independent of breathing.  Symptoms of Heart Attack (Myocardial Infarction):  The patients experience symptoms such as fear of death, extensive anxiety, sweating, nausea and vomiting, The pain occurs in any part of the chest or stomach cavity, especially in the neck-tie area and spreads to the shoulders, neck, jaw and left arm, even if they have many common characteristics with heart spasms (angina pectoris) in terms of duration and severity, heart attacks are more severe and last for a longer period, The most common symptoms are indigestion, flatulence pain or muscle pain; hence it may be confused with such problems (Such flatulence or muscle pains shall be presumed as symptoms of a heart attack until proved otherwise), The form or severity of the pain is independent of breathing.  First Aid Treatment for Chest Pains:  Check the vital signs of the patient (ABC), Immediately get patient to rest and calm her/him down, Ask for medical help (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician). Move the patient to a half-sitting position and help her/him to take her/his medicine, if any, E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 237 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250

Supply the patient with oxygen and monitor her/his vital signs on the way to hospital.  14.12. Basic Life Support 14.12.1. Respiration and Heart Arrest  Basic Life Support : These are drug-free treatments administered to individual who is unconscious and cannot breathe normally in order to ensure their lungs are supplied with oxygen through artificial respiration and blood is pumped from the heart through cardiac massage after ensuring airway patency. A. Checking the Airway Patency: Head-tilt-chin-lift position B. Checking Respiration: Look-Listen-Feel (maximum 10 seconds) C. Ensuring Circulation: Cardiac Massage-Rescue Breaths (Artificial Respiration) (30/2)  14.12.2. Basic Life Support for Adults  The first-aider shall make sure that s/he and the ill/injured person are safe; gloves and mask shall be used to give any kind of first aid. The differences indicated in Table-26: Table of Basic Life Support Practices are considered. Check if the ill/injured person is conscious by tapping her/his shoulders gently and asking “Are you OK?”, if they are unconscious; Call for medical assistance (get someone call 112/call for help on board/ask for defibrillator). Lay the patient down on a firm surface, kneel down next to her/him and loosen her/his neckties, belts and collars. Check inside the mouth and remove anything that may cause airway obstruction, if any. Put your one hand onto the ill/injured person’s forehead and the other hands’ fingertips under the jaw in order to open the airway. Push the head back by pressing so that the jawbone becomes perpendicular to the floor, thus putting the ill/injured person in the head back-chin up position. Check whether the ill/injured person breathes through the Look-Listen-Feel method for maximum 10 seconds. Observe heaving of the chest. Bend over and bring your face close to the patient's face and try to feel her/his breathing. If s/he is not breathing, or is not breathing normally, then communicate all details of the ill/injured person to the Commander and Cabin Chief. Announcements for any physician(s) shall be made upon acknowledgment by the flight crew. Place the heel of one hand over the center of the ill/injured person's chest (at the lower half of the rib cage after identifying the top and bottom of the rib cage). Place your other hand on top of the first hand. Lace your fingers together, with the fingers of the lower hand facing upwards. Position your shoulders directly over your hands, keeping your arms straight and your fingers off the chest. Apply rhythmical compressions on the chest in a way to lower the chest bone 5 cm* (1/3 of the chest height when viewed from the side); push at a rate of 100 compressions per minute. After 30 compressions, apply artificial respiration twice to the ill/injured person (30/2). When the ill/injured person is in the head-tilt/chin-lift position, put your mouth over her/his mouth in a way to cover it, and clog her/his nostrils. Perform artificial respiration twice, each of which lasts for 1 second, in order to help the ill/injured person's chest to rise, then open both the mouth and the nostrils for exhalation. Open the AED immediately upon receiving it (the device starts to operate immediately upon opening its cover). Unpack the pads by following the audio guidance given by the AED. (*) Place the heel of one hand over the center of the child's chest (at the lower half of the rib cage after identifying the top and bottom of the rib cage), then start the massage with one hand; if the child seems like adult, perform the massage with both hands. Basic Life Support for Infants (0-1 Years of Age)  The first-aider shall make sure that s/he and the infant are safe; gloves and mask shall be used to give any kind of first aid. AED is applied to infants between 29 days and 1 year of age. Unpack the pads by following the audio guidance given by the AED. If available, infant-child pads are used. If there is a risk of contact between the pads on the infant, or if the adult pads are to be used, place one pad on the upper back (between the shoulder blades) of the infant, and the other pad on the front side of the infant (slightly to the left if possible). If there are two first-aiders, one of them continues to give basic life support while the other is placing the pads on the chest. Make sure that nobody touches the infant while the AED makes rhythm analysis. The AED analyzes the rhythm and gives the shock command if the shock is needed. If shock is to be applied, make sure that nobody touches the infant, and press the shock button. After the shock, start 30:2 BLS without waiting. If the shock is not necessary, follow the audio guidance of the device, and start 30:2 BLS. Continue the cardiac massage/AED application until the infant’s vital signs are observed again and the medical assistance arrives. Neither turn off the device nor remove the pads. The cardiac massage on board the aircraft is never stopped even during landing, within the knowledge of the Commander. Airway Obstruction  It refers to the cases where the airway is obstructed and the air influx which is necessary for respiration is blocked. Such obstruction may be either complete or partial.  Symptoms of Airway Obstruction  Symptoms of Partial Obstruction: Coughs, Can breathe, Can speak. In such cases, do not touch the patients, but encourage them to cough. If the person cannot cough effectively and their respiration and cough become weaker, the complete obstruction procedure is applied.  Symptoms of Complete Obstruction: Cannot breathe, Suffer from pain, put their hands to their necks (as reflex), Can't speak, Cyanosis of the skin, Can't cough. Make a fist with one hand and place the thumb side of the fist against the patient's abdomen just above the navel and well below the lower tip of the breast bone, Grasp your fist with your other hand, Perform abdominal thrusts backwards and upwards, Continue to perform such thrusts for 5 times until the foreign body is removed, If the airway is not opened, then hit the patient's back gently again, Apply such practices for 5 times in regular turns; after each maneuver, before performing the next maneuver, the foreign body is checked to see if it has come out*. If the patient is unconscious, lay her/him down on a firm surface, Check the patient's pulse on their carotid artery, and also check their respiration, Ask for medical help. (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician) Start the Basic Life Support. Do not apply abdominal pressure on pregnant women or children under 1 year of age. The rate is slower during CPR than during chest compressions. First Aid Treatment for Asphyxia  Asphyxia:   It refers to the cases where the tissues are impaired due to the fact that such tissues are not supplied with sufficient amount of oxygen.  Causes of Asphyxia:  Falling back of the tongue into the throat due to fainting and loss of consciousness, Inhaling fluids into the trachea, Foreign body obstructing the trachea, Hanging, Impaired lungs, Gas poisoning, Drowning.  Common Symptoms of Asphyxia: E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 244 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250

Having difficulty in breathing, Noisy, rapid and deep breathing, Catarrh in the mouth and serous sputum, Cyanosis in face, lips and nails, Anxiety together with contradictory and irresolute replies, Fainting.  First Aid Treatment for Asphyxia: Eliminate the cause of asphyxia, Check whether the injured person is conscious or not, Check the patient's vital signs (ABC), Keep the patient in half-sitting position if s/he is conscious, Apply Basic Life Support treatment if s/he is unconscious and is not aspirating, Call for medical assistance (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician), Monitor her/his vital signs, In cold weather especially, even if 20-30 minutes have passed, the Basic Life Support shall be started in case of drowning in water. Besides, body trauma and spinal fractures shall also be considered in case of drowning in water. Therefore, it is necessary to avoid pushing the head backwards too much. In case of drowning, it is possible to apply mouth-to-mouth or mouth-to-nose artificial breathing in the water, and this application shall be started in the water. This application may be impossible in deep waters; therefore, it is necessary to draw the patient to shallow waters immediately.  14.15. Shock  The acute circulatory failure, which occurs due to the fact that the cardiovascular system cannot supply the vital organs with sufficient amount of blood, and which is accompanied by hypotension.  Psychogenic shock:   It is one of the most common types of shock seen on board. The main causes of psychogenic shock are extreme fear (for example, aviophobia), sorrow, extreme fatigue, long-term air travel and immobility, severe pain.  Cardiogenic shock : It is seen in the patients with circulatory failures, heart and respiratory diseases. Such patients' pulses cannot be measured, and their heartbeats are thready (rhythm disorder, fibrillation, severe heart failure). Such patients shall be supplied with oxygen.  Hypovolemic shock : It is caused by the loss of excessive amount of fluid, electrolyte and blood.  Septic shock : It occurs in inflammatory diseases and accompanied by high fever.  Toxic shock : It can be seen upon the poisonings (see Poisonings 14.20).  Anaphylactic Shock : It can be seen upon the allergic overreactions (see Allergic-Anaphylactic Reactions 14.24).  Common Symptoms of Shock:  Decreased body temperature, cold and moist skin. Over-sweating. Pale, whitish or bluish (cyanosis) skin: Caution! If you suspect of shock in dark-skinned patients, then check under the eye lids, nail beds and nail folds. Extreme restlessness, fatigue, thirst, nausea and vomiting. Rapid and weak pulse rate or no pulse. Pulse rate goes over 100 beats per minute. Hypotension. Increase in respiration rate, shallow breathing and shortness of breath. Loss of consciousness in sudden shock cases. Apply first aid treatment for all persons who have been severely injured regardless of the observance of such symptoms; it may be seen that the injured persons, who are not tolerant to severe pain and fear, suffer from shock.  First Aid Treatment for Shock:  First aid treatment for shock and the methods of shock protection are the same. Ensure the peripheral safety. Make sure that the patient's airway is open, and supply her/him with oxygen via medical or portable oxygen cylinder. First of all, make sure that respiration of the patient is sufficient. Stop the bleeding, if any. Put the patient in shock position. Lay the patient down; but do not forget that some patients suffering from shock as a result of severe heart attack or lung disease breathe more easily in sitting or half-sitting position. Keep the patient in the most comfortable position. Keep the patient warm, do not move them, and secure their fractures, if any, with splints. Ensure that the ill/injured person is dispatched to the healthcare organization quickly. (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician) Relieve the patient off her/his anxiety and fears, and then provide psychological support.  Shock Position:  Lay the patient down in supine position. Elevate the patient's legs approximately 30 cm above the head level and place any stable object (sheet, blanket, pillow, rolled cloth, etc.) under the ill/injured person's feet or ankles in order to maintain the elevation. Cover the patient and keep her/him warm. Do not leave the ill/injured person, and check their vital signs periodically (every 2-3 minutes) until medical assistance arrives.  14.16. Bleedings  It refers to the cases where the blood flows into either a body cavity or outside the body as a result of deformity in the veins.  Factors Identifying the Severity of Bleeding : Speed of bleeding, the area which the blood flows into, the amount of bleeding, physical conditions and age of the person.  14.16.1. Types of Bleeding  External Bleeding:   In such type, the bleeding is from the wound to outside of the body.  Internal Bleeding:   It cannot be seen clearly, due to the fact that the blood flows into a body cavity.  Bleeding through Orifices:   It refers to the cases where the bleeding is from ear, nostril, mouth, anus and reproductive organs. Such cases may be arterial, venous and capillary bleeding. Observing the symptoms of bleeding is essential in order to identify the type of bleeding.  Arterial Bleeding : It is usually expelled from the wound in spurts in synchronization with the heart beats, and it is light-colored.  Venous Bleeding : It is dark-red colored and escapes in oozing.  Capillary Bleeding : It escapes in small bubbles. 14.16.2. First Aid Treatment for External Bleeding  Examine the ill/injured person (ABC). Ask for medical help. (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician) Assess the wound or bleeding. Put pressure directly on the wound with a clean cloth. If the bleeding does not stop, put another cloth over the first one and boost the amount of pressure. Wrap the bleeding area with the bandage and tie a knot over the wound. Elevate the bleeding area above the heart level. Compress on the pressure point closest to the bleeding area. Apply tourniquet method under the circumstances where there is only one first aider in spite of the fact that there is more than one injured person, the injured person will be carried to another area under difficult conditions, it is encountered with loss of limb cases and/or it is not satisfactory to compress on the pressure points. Take the ill/injured person in shock position. Check the ill/injured person's vital signs frequently (every 2-3 minutes). Cover the ill/injured person, but do not forget that the bleeding area shall not be covered. Write all details regarding the applied treatment (like tourniquet) legibly. Dispatch the ill/injured person as soon as possible.  14.16.3. Points to Compress on the Body  In arterial bleeding, the first thing to do is to compress on the bleeding area or the area close to the bleeding area. The areas to compress are as follows:  1. Neck:   Jugular artery (carotid artery) pressure point  2. On collar bone:   Brachial artery pressure point  3. Armpit:   Brachial artery pressure point  4. Upper part of the arm:   Brachial artery pressure point  5. Groin:   Leg artery pressure point  6. Femur:   Leg artery pressure point WHILE PERFORMING FIRST AID ON ALL BLEEDING PATIENTS, GLOVES SHALL BE WORN TO BE PROTECTED AGAINST AIDS AND OTHER INFECTIOUS DISEASES.  14.16.4. Tourniquet Application  Tourniquet is mainly applied for three cases: If there are many injured persons in spite of the fact that there is only one available first aider (with the purposes of stopping bleeding, and then, taking care of the other injured persons), If the injured person will be carried to another place under difficult conditions (if there will be a long rough road), In case of loss of limb, If the pressure applied to the pressure points is not satisfactory, tourniquet can be applied.  Note:   Do not apply a tourniquet under any circumstances other than the above-mentioned. The tourniquet application is the last application to be executed in case bleeding cannot be stopped.   However, it is not applied as frequently as it used to be. Because  tissues may be damaged or limb may be completely lost in case of long-lasting tourniquet application. Tourniquet Application:  Continue to compress on the pressure point with one hand. A wide, at least 8-10 cm wide strong and inelastic material (other than cutting materials such as rope, wire) is taken. Fold the band to its half-length and wrap it around the limb. Insert one end into the collar and pull, then wrap it around both ends. Relieve the pressure on the pressure point and knot a tie tightly enough to stop the bleeding completely. Wrap the area with a wide bandage. Insert a rigid object (such as pencil) through the bandage in parallel to the limb. Twist the rigid object until the bleeding stops. Position such object in straight position to the limb and secure the object so that it will not open. Pin a card indicating the injured person’s name and the time when the tourniquet has been applied (in hour/minute form) to her/his clothes. In the event that there are many injured persons, write "Tourniquet" or "T" on the injured person's forehead either with a lipstick or a non-erasable pen. Cover the injured person with a blanket but be careful that the tourniquet area or the medical dressing is not covered. Loosen the tourniquet every 15-20 minutes (until the tourniquet-applied area turns pink), and then twist again. The tourniquet is applied on the single bone regions like arm and thigh, but not on the forearm and leg, as it may prevent feeding of the hands and feet. In case of limb loss, the tourniquet may also be applied on forearm and leg.  14.16.5. First Aid Treatment for Loss of Limb  Lay the injured person down in supine position. Elevate the injured person's legs approximately 30 cm above the head level (shock position). Compress on the bleeding area or pressure points in order to stop bleeding. If the bleeding cannot be controlled with these methods, tourniquet shall be applied from the nearest healthy area to the lost limb. Place the lost limb inside a clean, waterproof bag and then close it tightly. Put this bag inside another bag filled with 1 scale of water and 2 scales of ice (if available). Wrap the bag with a clean cloth. Write the details of the injured person who has lost her/his limb on the bag, and put this bag on the same vehicle with the injured person. Make sure that s/he is dispatched to any health institution within 6 hours at the latest. Ask for medical help. (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician)  14.16.6. Internal Bleeding  Internal bleeding may occur as a result of severe trauma, impact, fracture and gunshot wounds. Symptoms: Hypovolemic-shock related symptoms are observed, Pulse rate is weak and rapid, Skin is cold and moist (sticky), Eyes are glassy; pupils may be enlarged and light reflex is weak, In severe cases, blood pressure decreases, E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 248 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250
=== Sayfa 251 ===
The patients are generally thirsty and almost always anxious, The patients may suffer from nausea and vomit, In mild gastrointestinal bleeding cases, dark-colored vomit like coffee grounds is observed; but in severe gastrointestinal bleeding cases, bright-red blood comes out of the mouth and the stool is in dark-black colored. Apply the first aid treatment stated below for the patients suspected of suffering from internal bleeding: Check whether the ill/injured person is conscious or not as well as their ABC (Airway-Breathing-Circulation), Cover the patient and elevate her/his legs 30 cm above the head level, Ask for medical help (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician). Do not give her/him any food or drink, Do not move her/him (especially, if there is any fracture), Assess her/his vital signs, Ensure that the patient is dispatched to the health institution. Pupillary light reflex is highly important in cerebral bleeding cases and shall necessarily be checked; if the brain death occurs, pupillary reflex is not observed. When you point flashlight to pupils for 1-2 seconds, both pupils shall become smaller simultaneously; when you remove the flashlight, they shall become larger and recover their normal size again. If pupillary reflex is not observed, then it indicates brain death; if pupillary reflex is asymmetrical (that is, if both pupils do not become smaller and larger simultaneously), then it indicates paralysis (see Pupillary reflex).  14.16.7. First Aid Treatment for Bleeding from Orifices  Nose Bleeding:  Calm the ill/injured person down, relieve her/him of her/his anxieties, sit her/him down and get her/him bend her/his head forwards, Hold the nostrils for 5 minutes and ensure that the ill/injured person is sent to the medical doctor.  Ear Bleeding:  Calm the ill/injured person down and relieve her/him of her/his anxieties, If the bleeding is mild, clean the ear with a clean cloth, If the bleeding is severe, cover the ear with clean cloths but make sure that the ear is not clogged, If s/he is conscious, lay her/him down in supine position; but if s/he is unconscious, lay her/him down on her/his bleeding ear, If the ill/injured person suffers from ear bleeding, blood vomiting or bleeding from anus or reproductive organs, dispatch her/him to the medical doctor together with the blood samples.  14.17. Injuries  Wound is the disruption of the integrity of the skin or mucosa as a result of a trauma. The structures like blood vessels, muscles, and nerves may also be affected. Since the protection feature of the skin will be impaired, the infection risk increases.  Wound Types Cut Wounds:   They are caused by sharp objects like knife, jack-knife, and glass. They are generally simple wounds. Their depths are easily detected.  Crush Wounds:   The wounds caused by strong hit of the factors like stone, fist, or stick. The edges of the wound are crushed. There is not much bleeding, but there is tissue damage and sensitivity.  Puncture Wounds:   They are the wounds caused by long and sharp objects. They go deep down from the surface. They can be deceptive and include tetanus hazard.  Avulsion Wounds:   It is caused by traction effect on the tissues. The entire organ related to that tissue; scalp may also be damaged. Infected Wounds : They are the wounds likely be infected. Wounds with high risk of infection; delayed wounds (more than 6 hours), wounds with separated sutures, non-uniform wounds, very dirty and deep wounds, gunshot wounds, bite and sting wounds.  Common Symptoms of Wounds : Pain, bleeding and scabbing.  First Aid Treatment for Injuries:  Check the patient's vital signs (ABC). Assess the wound site (finding out how and when it occurred, whether there is any foreign body and bleeding or not, etc.). Stop the bleeding and wrap any clean cloth around the wound. Ensure that the patient goes to the health institution. (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician) Warn her/him against the possibility of tetanus. Do not touch any foreign body on the wound and secure it.  14.17.1. Penetrating Chest Injuries  Any object penetrating into the chest hurts pleura and lungs. As a result of such injuries, the symptoms stated below may be observed: Severe pain, respiratory distress, cyanosis, hemoptysis, open pneumothorax (breathing through the chest wound).  First Aid Treatment for Penetrating Chest Injuries  Check whether the injured person is conscious or not. Check the injured person's vital signs (ABC). Cover the wound site with a cloth wrapped in a plastic bag, nylon, etc. Keep three sides of the cloth that you’ve placed on the wound closed tightly and leave one side open so that the air does not contact with the wound in the course of inhalation and lets out in the course of exhalation. If the injured person is conscious, then keep her/him in sitting position (so that s/he breaths more easily). Do not give anything orally to the injured person. Check her/his vital signs frequently. Take all required measures for shock because shock is highly probable in open pneumothorax cases. Ask for medical help. (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician)  14.17.2. Penetrating Abdominal Injuries  Abdominal organs may be damaged. Internal and external bleeding may be observed together with hemorrhagic shock. If the abdomen is rigid like wood and aching, then it means that the health condition of the injured person is critical. Intestines of the injured person may stick out.  First Aid Treatment for Penetrating Abdominal Injuries  Check whether the injured person is conscious or not. Check the injured person's vital signs (ABC). Do not try to tuck the organs sticking out in, cover them with a wide, wet and clean cloth. If the injured person is conscious, lay her/him down in supine position and bend her/his legs; cover her/him to prevent heat loss. Do not give any food or drink orally to the injured person. Check her/his vital signs frequently. Ask for medical help. 14.17.3. Skull and Spinal Injuries  Central nervous system in the cranial cavity may be affected depending on the severity of the impact. Sudden compression or dislocation of vertebrae may be observed in spinal injuries. In consequence of this, the nervous system is affected badly and several negative effects may occur.  Types of Skull Injuries Scalp Injuries:   The scalp can change its place easily on the skull and is split easily with any impact. In that case, there is too much bleeding; therefore, it is necessary first to stop the bleeding.  Skull, Brain Injuries: Skull Fractures:   In case skull fractures, brain damage is more important than the fracture itself. Therefore, it is necessary to check if there is any brain damage symptom.  Facial Injuries:   In case of mouth and nose injuries, the respiration may be affected seriously, and the sensory organs may be damaged. As a result of a facial injury, nasal bone, jawbone injuries may be observed.  Spinal Injuries:   The waist and neck parts are the most damaged parts, and they cause very intense pain. Mostly the neck is affected in accidents.  Reasons of Skull and Spinal Injuries  Falling down from height, Head and body injuries, Automobile or motorcycle accidents, Sports and work accidents, Getting trapped under debris.  Symptoms of Skull and Spinal Injuries  Changes in the level of consciousness, memory changes or memory loss, Pain on head, neck and back, Tingling or numbness in hands and fingers, Complete or partial loss of mobility in any part of the body, Deformity in skull or spine, Coming out of cerebrospinal fluid from the nostrils and ears (CSF), External bleeding on head, neck and back, trauma, loss of balance, bruises around ears and eyes. HOWEVER; EVEN IF SUCH SYMPTOMS ARE NOT OBSERVED, facial and collar bone injuries, all fall cases, traffic accidents, and all injured persons who are unconscious shall be treated as skull and spinal injuries.  First Aid Treatment for Skull and Spinal Injuries  Check whether the patient is conscious or not. Check the patient's vital signs (ABC). Call for medical assistance immediately (112). If the injured person is conscious, immobilize her/him. If there is any risk, drag the injured person in straight position. Do not disturb head-neck-body axis. When the medical assistance arrives, place the injured person on the stretcher by preserving the head-neck-body axis. Do not jolt the injured person while carrying and dispatching. Record all details regarding the applied first aid treatment and the injured person, and inform them to the medical team. Do not leave the injured person alone until the medical assistance arrives.  14.17.4. Cerebral Hemorrhage  It is a severe intracranial hemorrhage occurring in the brain tissue. It may either cause brain trauma or concussion or occur spontaneously due to hemorrhagic stroke. Non-traumatic intracerebral hemorrhage leads to a spontaneous bleeding in the brain tissue; stress may be the cause .  Risk Factors for Cerebral Hemorrhage:  Hypertension, diabetes, menopause, smoking, excessive alcohol drinking, severe migraine.  14.17.5. Tetanus  Tetanus is an infection, which is characterized by severe permanent spasms and which affects the central nervous system. The cause of tetanus is the toxin of the soil-dwelling bacteria called Clostridium tetani. Accordingly, the wounds which occurred long time ago (more than 6 hours), highly dirty and deep wounds, shapeless wounds with open stitches, open bleeding wounds with broken bones, wounds occurring as a result of bites, stings, gunshot and microbial infections are highly potential to be infected with tetanus. Dispatch persons injured in such manner to the health institution as soon as possible and ensure that they will be vaccinated against tetanus and tetanus immunoglobulin treatment (a medical treatment used in the Diagnosis and Treatment of Tetanus available in R.O.T. Ministry of Health Travel Health Department) is applied if necessary within 24 hours. All wounds except for the surgical wounds are considered as non-sterile or dirty wounds. Simple wounds that we often encounter in daily life are washed with clean water. If the infected wounds will be treated in the health institution and the injured persons will be vaccinated against tetanus as soon as possible; control bleeding without touching the foreign body stabbed in the wound, if any, and dispatch the injured persons after covering their wounds. CAUTION: Adults shall be vaccinated against tetanus every 5-10 years in order to protect themselves from the risk of tetanus in injuries and burns.  14.18. Burn, Freezing, Hypothermia and Heat Stroke 14.18.1. First Aid Treatment for Burns  Factors Identifying the Severity of Burns: Severity, extent, area, infection risk, age, respiratory damage, preexisting diseases (such as cancer, diabetes, etc.)  Degrees of Burn  1. Degree Burns: Redness on the skin, pain and edema on the burnt skin are observed. It takes approximately 48 hours to heal. 2. Degree Burns: Blisters (bulla) on the skin are observed, and they cause pain. It heals when the skin renews itself. 3. Degree Burns: It affects entire dermis. It gives damage especially to muscles, nerves and veins. Its effects range from white and black wounds to completely black wounds. It is painless owing to the fact that the nerves are affected. The patient may suffer from shock.  Adverse Effects of Burns to the Body  It leads to operative dysfunction of organs and systems depending on the severity, extent and the affected part of the body. The patient may suffer from shock as a result of fluid loss and pain. Infections may occur as a result of microorganisms and toxins within the patient's own body.  First Aid Treatment for Heat Burns  If the person is still exposed to burning, try to prevent her/him from acting in panic and running. Cover the injured person with either a blanket or a covering and roll her/him. E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 252 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250

Check the injured person's vital signs (ABC). Check whether the injured person has any difficulty in breathing or not. Take the risk of edema into account and take her/his ring(s), bracelet(s), watch(es), etc. off accordingly. Take the injured person's clothes off without touching the burnt skin. If her/his cloth(es) sticks to the skin, leave it there and cut away the remaining fabric. Hold the burnt skin under running water for at least 20 minutes (If the burnt surface is extended, do not apply this treatment owing to the fact that doing so could cause sudden drop in body temperature). Pay attention to hygiene and sanitation; do not break blisters. Do not apply any burn ointment or cream on the burnt surface. Cover the wound area with sterile gauze or clean moist cloth in order to keep the wound area clean and prevent it from getting infected. Cover the injured person with a blanket. Cover the burnt surfaces with separate bandages. If the burnt surface is extended, the health institution is far away and the injured person is conscious and does not vomit, feed her/him orally (a mixture of 1 L water-1 teaspoonful salt- 1 teaspoonful carbonate) in order to prevent fluid loss. Ask for medical help. (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician)  First Aid Treatment for Chemical Burns  Block the contact of the chemical product with the skin as soon as possible. Rinse the burnt surface softly under plenty of non-pressurized water for at least 15-20 minutes. Take the injured person's clothes off. Cover the injured person. Ask for medical help. (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician)  IMPORTANT:   If possible, hold the burnt surface above the heart level in order to prevent edema occurrence in first and second degree burns unless the injured person has another health problem.  First Aid Treatment for Electrical Burns  Calm down and do not act in panic. Before touching the injured person, shut the electric current off; if such an action is not possible, then interrupt the injured person's contact with the electric current via any wooden stick or rope. Assess the injured person's ABC (Airway-Breathing-Circulation). Do not treat the injured person with any first aid treatment applied with water. Do not move the injured person. Cover the damaged surface with a clean cloth. Call for medical assistance (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/announcement for Physician).  14.18.2. Heat Stroke  Heat stroke occurs when the body fails to regulate its own temperature as a result of exposure to high temperature and moisture.  Symptoms of Heat Stroke  Muscle cramps, E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 253 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250

Weakness, fatigue, Dizziness, Behavior disorders, nervousness, Pale and warm skin, Over sweating (decreasing gradually), Abdominal cramps, vomiting, nausea, Loss of consciousness, hallucinations, Rapid pulse rate.  First Aid Treatment for Heat Stroke  Take the patient to any cool and well-ventilated place. Take her/his clothes off. Lay the patient down in supine position and elevate her/his arms and legs above the heart level. If the patient does not suffer from nausea, supply her/him orally with a mixture of 1 L water-1 teaspoonful salt-1 teaspoonful carbonate, or soda.  Risk Groups in Heat Stroke  Although there is no particular risk group for the heatstroke, the persons who are susceptible to other diseases and injuries are affected by the heatstroke worse than the other people. These people are heart, blood pressure, diabetes, cancer, kidney patients, those well below and above normal weight, those having psychological or psychiatric disorders, people over 65, children under 5, pregnant women, those apply continuous and unconscious diet, those who do not drink sufficient amount of water.  14.18.3. Freezing  Tissues are damaged as a result of the fact that the areas exposed to cold are not supplied with sufficient amount of blood and blood clot develops owing to the extreme cold.  First Degree:   It is the mildest form of freezing. It heals quickly if treated at its early stages. Pale and cold skin are observed together with numbness and weakness. Redness and prickling sensation are seen later on.  Second Degree:   If the time of exposure to cold is prolonged, symptoms become evident. Tension develops in the damaged part. Edema, swelling, pain and water blisters (bulla) are observed. Water blisters turn into black scabs while healing.  Third Degree:   Tissues are damaged permanently. A black part occurs on the skin which can be easily distinguished from the living and healthy skin.  First Aid Treatment for Freezing  Take the patient to a warm place and block her/his contact with the cold. Calm her/him down, make sure that s/he rests, do not move her/him, put dry clothes on her/him. Feed her/him with warm drinks, do not break blisters, cover the areas with blisters. Do not rub the frozen part, ensure that such part gets warm through the person's own heat generating ability. Keep the arms and legs in their usual position. If numbness continues after such processes, then cover the damaged part with a bandage. Elevate the arms and legs. Ask for medical help. (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician)  14.18.4. Hypothermia  Hypothermia is a dangerous condition that occurs when the body loses heat faster than it produces and that needs urgent intervention. Hypothermia can result in loss of consciousness and death if not intervened in a short time. Any further decrease in body temperature shall be avoided.  Symptoms of Hypothermia:   Shivering, slurring and slow speaking, slow breathing and falling heart rate, cold hands and feet, numbness in arms and legs, loss of skills in hands and low energy, fear and irrational behavior, memory loss, drowsiness, contraction of muscles and dilated pupils.  Causes of Hypothermia:   Hypothermia is caused by inadequate movement in cold weather, stay in water for long periods even in hot weather, falling into cold water, especially in infants and minor children: wet or damp clothing ,   large burns in the body, accident in snowy weather ,   inadequate clothing or low outdoor temperatures.  Recommendations to Prevent Hypothermia  When going to cold air;  Wrap up:   You can lose your body temperature quickly, especially from the head, face and neck parts of your body. Use beanie, scarf and face mask to prevent this. Wear gloves.  Do not use excessive effort:   Avoid activities that cause you to sweat a lot. The combination of wet clothing and cold air can cause you to lose body heat faster.  Wear in a layered manner:   Wear loose, layered, light clothing. As an outer layer, choose clothes made of tightly woven, waterproof material that can protect you from the wind. As an inner layer, wool and silk garments keep the body heat better than cotton.  Stay dry:   Try to stay as dry as possible. Get rid of your wet clothes as soon as possible. Pay particular attention to keeping your hands and feet dry. Wear water-proof and snow-proof boots.  14.19. Traumas (Dislocation and Sprain)  Fracture is loss of integrity of bone structures. Fractures may occur without any cause or as a result of any impact. The risk of fractures occurring without any cause increases parallel with age. Symptoms of Fracture: Increasing pain while moving, deformity, loss of mobility (dysfunction), edema and cyanosis as a result of bleeding. Palpation is necessary to identify the aching part. Fracture Types; Closed Fracture: Bone integrity is impaired, but the skin is intact. Open Fracture: The skin integrity has been lost. Broken bone ends may come out, includes the risk of bleeding and infection. Adverse Effects of Fractures Injuries in veins, nerves, muscles and compression (no pulse on the fractures part, paleness and coldness), Hemorrhagic shock in segmental fractures.  14.19.1. First Aid Treatment for Fractures  Treat the life-threatening cases first of all. Do not move the injured person and keep her/him warm. If the arm has been affected, take the injured person's ring(s), watch(es), etc. off (otherwise, the edema that may develop would lead to tissue damages). Do not cover the fingers completely while identifying and wrapping the damaged part with bandage. Thereby, you can check skin color, mobility and tenderness of the fingers easily. Secure the fractured, dislocated, sprained parts together with the lower and upper joints of such parts. Poisoning  Poisoning is deterioration of the normal body functions. It is caused by toxic substances that are swallowed, inhaled, or in contact with skin.  Common Symptoms of Poisoning:  Digestive System Disorders: Nausea, vomiting, stomachache, diarrhea.  Nervous System Disorders: Loss of consciousness, convulsion, discomfort, behavioral inconsistency.  Respiratory System Disorders: Shortness of breath, cyanosis, respiratory arrest.  Circulatory System Disorders: Irregular pulse rate, cardiac arrest. Types of Poisoning;  Through Digestion: The most common type of poisoning cases. The causes of such cases are chemical products used generally in the gardens, poisonous mushrooms, rotten food, medicine and excessive amount of alcohol consumption.  Through Respiration: The poisoning cases where the poisonous substances are taken through respiration. The causes of such cases are carbon monoxide (gas leak from gas cylinder, water heater and butane gas heater), carbon dioxide released from cesspools or rocks, chlorine used for ensuring pool hygiene, adhesives, paints and the substances used with the purpose of cleaning. E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 258 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250
=== Sayfa 261 ===
Through Skin: The poisoning cases where poisonous substances are taken through skin. Such cases are caused by the fact that poisonous substances like insect stings, animal bites, medicine injections, hair dyes and agricultural pesticides are absorbed in the skin.  14.20.1. Poisoning Through Digestion and First Aid Treatment  A great many parasitic microorganisms use food products in order to be transmitted to the humans. It is enough to take only a small dose of such microorganisms in order to catch the disease. Infectious jaundice, cholera, tuberculosis and brucellosis may be given as the examples of such diseases. The main cause of food poisoning cases is orally intake of the food products “contaminated” with the bacteria. If the food products which is not rotten physically and organoleptically and have not lost their food quality are contaminated with bacteria, then they lead to poisoning. There are two types of poisoning; 1. The poisoning that the bacteria itself directly causes. Typhoid and infections of Escherichia Coli may be given as the examples of such type. 2. Bacterial toxins. (e.g., Staphylococcus poisoning, “Botulism”).  14.20.1.1. Salmonella Poisoning (Typhoid and Paratyphoid (A, B, C) Infections)  Salmonella is generally found in animals. Food of animal origin are highly potential to carry such bacteria. The risk of the existence of salmonella species is high in such food as the inadequately processed fermented sausage, poultry meat, inadequately heat-processed sausages and salami, eggs and food containing egg ingredients, dairy products like ice-cream and cream, salads and sauces, aquaculture products and ready meals. Resistant bacteria can survive for a long period in frozen and dried foods of animal origin. Health problems such as headache, feeling bad, stomachache, mild fever, nausea, vomiting and diarrhea as well as characteristic stomach and intestinal problems are observed after approximately 12-36 hours.  14.20.1.2. Poisoning Caused by Round-Shaped Bacteria - Cocci (Staphylococcus)  Intake of pre-formed bacterial toxins is the main cause of food poisoning. Especially the food which is served in the meetings with broad participation,   prepared   beforehand   and   hot-preserved   is   highly   favorable   for   the   bacteria   to   develop   and   produce   toxin.   In staphylococcus-related food poisoning cases, stomach and intestinal problems occur within 1-3 hours as of intake of the contaminated food. Severe nausea, vomiting and diarrhea are observed, and such symptoms last for a period longer than 6-8 hours. Ways of Protection: 1. Serve the food, which is frozen while being loaded to the aircraft, as soon as possible after heating it in the course of flight. 2. Do not eat, serve, reheat the food which has been left in warm ovens for a long time. 3. Preserve the opened milk cans among the ice cubes (if available) and do not leave them in warm ovens under any circumstances.  14.20.1.3. Can Poisoning (Botulism)  The most typical and common type of poisoning caused by toxins of bacteria. Can poisoning is caused by intake, together with food consumed, of the toxin generated by Colostridium Botilinum, which contaminates canned goods that are produced under non-hygienic conditions or as a result of damage on the can, the spore of which reproduces under deoxygenated environment. Symptoms are observed 24 hours after intake of the toxin. The toxin affecting the central nervous system generally leads to death occurrences and if the patients do not die, the effect of the toxin may last for weeks.  Ways of Protection: 1. Do not eat the canned food, packages of which are swollen, damaged, deformed, drilled or distorted. 2. Make sure to check the expiry dates of canned food.  14.20.1.4. First Aid Treatment for Poisoning through Digestion  In the cases suspected of poisoning, the purpose of the first aid is to remove the cause of poisoning from the stomach and intestines immediately. Check whether the patient is conscious or not. If the mouth has contacted with the poisonous substance, then wash inside of the mouth with water; if the hand has contacted with the poisonous substance, then rinse the hand with soap and water. Check the patient's vital signs (ABC). Assess the symptoms such as vomiting, nausea and diarrhea. If the patient has taken caustic substance, do not try to get her/him vomit under any circumstances. If the patient is unconscious, take her/him in recovery position. Cover the patient. Ask for medical help. (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician) Gather the details regarding the incident and record them; - What type of poisonous substance is it? - Does the patient take medicine or drugs? - When was the patient found? - What kinds of medicine are there in the house?  14.20.2. Protection Methods of Food Poisoning During the Flight  a) Plan the hygiene standards in food production in a manner to prevent cross-contaminations. b) Compliance of all employees serving at production, loading, checking and service phases, with the hygiene rules, will minimize the risk of cross-contamination in relation to catering supplies at all phases both before and after the production. c) Check all food products before loading and serving stages and send the suspicious ones to confirmatory tests. d) The durability periods of catering products vary depending on the catering ingredients, flight duration, loading, and storage conditions. The requirements specified in EK.10.71.008 Cabin Product and Service Manual Table-3: Durability Period of Products are followed. e) Prevent the contact of sharp objects and others, which have been used for raw meat products and egg, with the cooked or ready-to serve food without washing them thoroughly. f) It is highly important to cook and heat the food adequately in order to prevent the infections transmitted especially via meat products. g) Check the expiry dates of food and adhere to such dates. h) In order to decrease the risk of incapacitation of flight crew, the flight crew members shall not eat the same foodstuffs, before and during the flight. i) Since the most acute forms of food poisoning often occur within 1-6 hours of eating contaminated food, flight crews shall pay attention to meals eaten within 6 hours after the flight. Flight crews shall refrain from consuming food and drinks that are served cold, as well as perishable foods. Milk and cream products, mayonnaise sauces, salads, meat pies, and other meat products pose a risk. j) In food poisoning, the character and severity of symptoms depend on the nature and dose of the toxin and the patient's resistance. The onset can be sudden. Fatigue, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal cramps, intestinal motility, diarrhea may occur.  14.20.3. First Aid Treatment in case of Poisoning through Respiration  Move the patient to the fresh air or ventilate the place by opening the window(s) and door(s). Examine to find out that whether the patients have vital signs or not (ABC: Airway-Breathing-Circulation). Keep the patient in half-sitting position. If s/he is not conscious, put her/him into the recovery position. Ask for medical help (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician). Take all required measures in order to protect you and your periphery in the course of intervention. Symptoms of Carbon-Monoxide Poisoning  Extreme fatigue, dejection, unrest, flu-like condition, nausea, dizziness, vomiting, tingling, coma, fits, respiratory arrest, chest pain, palpitation, hypotension, cardiac arrest, headache and skin and nails in cherry red for a short time. First Aid for Drug Poisoning (Overdose Medication)  Drug poisoning may arise from overdose of prescription drugs or consumption of illegal drugs. The symptoms of drug poisoning resemble   the   symptoms   of   alcohol   poisoning.   However,   the   people   under   the   influence   of   narcotics   exhibit   some   common behaviors/actions/symptoms. They include, without limitation, the following: Abnormally wide pupils Intoxicated appearance and behavior Rapid breathing and pulse Muscular contraction Numbness Sweating A person consuming drug and alcohol simultaneously may exhibit a mixture of these symptoms. Keep calm and put the person at ease. If the person loses their consciousness, keep them in the coma position as long as they keep breathing.  14.20.6. Alcohol Poisoning  The influence of alcohol may vary by the body size, metabolism, whether the stomach was empty or not before drinking. General symptoms of alcohol poisoning: Lethargy, talking incomprehensibly, red skin, blurred vision, nervousness, nausea, Mental confusion, abrupt changes in behaviors, tiredness, dizziness, Headache, constricted/dilated pupils, uncoordinated behaviors, unconsciousness. Avoid serving more alcohol, with an appropriate excuse, to someone you think has already drunk too much. Inform the other cabin crew members not to give alcoholic drinks to that passenger. Local symptoms such as pain, swelling and redness are observed. If the bee stings more than one spot on the skin, if the bee stings any spot near the trachea or if the patient is allergic to bee stings, such cases may be dangerous.  First Aid Treatment for Bee Sting  Wash the wounded site and remove the bee's sting if visible. Apply cold treatment to the wounded site. If the bee stings the patient's mouth and s/he has difficulty while breathing, ensure that s/he sucks on ice (if available). If the bee stings the patient's mouth or if the patient is allergic to bee stings, call for medical assistance. Pain, edema, inflammation, redness, cyanosis, muscle cramps, shivering together with tingling sensation, discomfort and convulsion may be observed.  First Aid Treatment for Scorpion Sting  Do not move the stung part of the body. Keep the patient in lying position and apply cold treatment to the wound. Wrap the wounded site with bandage but make sure that the circulatory system is not blocked. Do not perform any medical intervention on the wound. Check the patient's health condition frequently.  Symptoms of Snake Bite  Local and general symptoms are observed. Cyanosis on the wounded site, inflammation (lasting 1-2 weeks), digestive problems such as vomiting, stomachache and diarrhea, extreme thirst, shock, bleeding, psychological disorders, irregular heartbeat, headache and respiratory disorders may be observed.  First Aid Treatment for Snake Bite  Calm the patient down, ensure that s/he rests and wash the wound with water. First Aid Treatment for Eye, Ear and Nose Injuries 14.22.1. First Aid Treatment for Foreign Body into the Eye  If the Foreign Body is a Small Particle e.g., Dust; Turn the eye to the light and look inside the lower eyelid thoroughly. Keep the upper eyelid open if required. Try to remove the foreign body by means of any moist cloth. Tell the patient to blink her/his eye. Do not rub the eye. If the foreign body cannot be removed, send the patient to the health institution.  If Any Object is stabbed into the Eye or Any Metal Object gets into the Eye; Do not move the patient unless required. Do not touch the eye under any circumstances. If bandage will be applied, cover both eyes with the bandage. Ask for medical help. (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician) Send the patient to the health institution employing an optometrist.  Injuries Caused by Chemical Substances; Various chemical substances (cleaning materials and detergents, alcohol, laundry bleach, etc.) may lead to eye irritation. Lay the patient down on which side s/he suffers from irritation. Rinse the patient's eye with ample water and do not forget to open her/his eyelids in the course of such treatment. Remove her/his contact lens if any. Send the patient to the health institution employing an optometrist.  14.22.2. Contact Lenses and Ocular Prosthesis  Many people use contact lenses. They are generally in transparent color and accordingly it is difficult to see them. If there is any risk of eye irritation, do not remove lens owing to the fact that doing so could give more damage. If it cannot be thrown out, call for medical assistance. (112/Commander/Cabin Chief/Announcement for Physician)  14.23. Physiology of the Respiratory System  The main function of lung is to supply blood with oxygen and to release carbon dioxide from the blood while exhaling. All kinds of lung diseases causing the blood to be supplied with insufficient amount of blood are harmful to human health. Excessive amount of carbon dioxide creates adverse effects, as well. Blood carbon dioxide level in arteries is the main warning about the person's respiration. If blood carbon dioxide level is too low, the patient begins to take shallow and slow breaths automatically. Such condition reducing the amount of released carbon dioxide helps the carbon dioxide in blood return to its normal level. If carbon dioxide level in arteries exceeds the normal level, the patient begins to take rapid and deep breaths and thereby releases carbon dioxide and her/his blood level decreases.  14.23.1. Anoxia-Hypoxia  Anoxia   is a condition in which all tissues of the organism are deprived of oxygen.  Hypoxia   is a condition where the tissues are not supplied with sufficient amount of oxygen. It is highly dangerous and may lead to death if sustained for an extended period of time.  Causes of Hypoxia  Medical Issues: Heart attack, pulmonary edema, acute drug use, pneumonia, paralysis, chest injuries, asthma and allergic reactions, shock, prolonged pulmonary diseases. Atmospheric Events: Insufficient oxygenation caused by the sudden atmospheric pressure discharge and the drop of partial pressure of atmospheric oxygen at high altitude. People's resistance to atmospheric hypoxia varies from person to person.  Symptoms of Hypoxia (Depletion of Oxygen)  Early symptoms are tachycardia (abnormally fast heartbeat rate), nervousness and irritability. It comprises the period experienced before the vital organs are damaged. Afterwards, symptoms showing that the mental functions of the brain have slowed down (slowdown in thinking, deciding, self-control and reflexes) are observed. It is observed that the patient needs to take deep breaths. Together with such symptoms, the conditions stated below are seen: Fatigue, drowsiness and frequently yawning, Headache, blackout, visual impairment, Pale skin, cyanosis (blue color) in progressive cases, Tingling sensation in hands and feet, tinnitus, Movement irregularities, repeating most-recent moves, (Gradually) Loss of consciousness, fluttering and coma.  First Aid Principles E K . 1 0 . 7 1 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 3 C a b i n C r e w M a n u a l QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 264 | Total Page: 298  05045415456216863576102259255250

Supply the patient with additional oxygen. In atmospheric cases, supply the patient with oxygen from either medical or portable oxygen cylinder for 10-15 minutes, in medical cases supply the patient with high-flow rate oxygen (4 L/min.) until the medical assistance arrives. If the patient is not given additional oxygen, her/his recovery process will be slow and difficult.  CAUTION:   Oxygen is an inflammable and combustible gas. Remove all sources of flame away. Be careful while supplying patients of chronic pulmonary diseases (such as emphysema) with oxygen over 25-30% and be always ready to perform artificial respiration treatment.  14.23.2. Hyperventilation  It is observed in patients who do not have any pulmonary disease. It is directly associated with the psychological state of patients. The main cause is decrease of blood carbon dioxide level of arteries below normal level and hyper-respiration the depth of which has increased. Causes of Hyperventilation: It may be a side effect of hypoxia Anxiety or emotional stress Pain Motion sickness Heat Turbulence Symptoms; Sudden depression developed with panic attack, Rapid (30-40/minute) and deep breathing, Shortness of breath in spite of rapid breathing, Numbness and tingling sensation in hands and feet, Flexor spasms of hands and feet. While treating hyperventilation, having a psychological approach is highly important. Ease the patient's anxiety by expressing the condition to her/him, assure her/him that s/he will get better following the treatment you will apply. Bring the O 2   source near the patient, and supply her/him with oxygen at the lowest level for a short time.  14.24. Allergic-Anaphylactic Reactions  Allergy may be defined as the overreaction of the protective mechanism of the human body against allergenic substances.  14.24.1. Substances Causing Allergic Reactions  Medicine allergies; Penicillin and derivative antibiotics, iodine solution and pomades, Food allergies; Nuts, shellfish (mussel, oyster, shrimp, lobster), eggs, various vegetable and fruit (tomato, strawberry, chocolate, aubergine, etc.), Pollens of various plants and flowers, Feather and hair of animals, Insect allergies; Bees, ants and some other insects, Various cosmetic products, Sun allergy.  Symptoms:  Allergic reactions are characterized by local and general symptoms such as redness on the skin, skin eruption, urticaria, itching, swelling on the skin and mucosa, eye irritation, sneezing, nasal congestion, shortness of breath, asthma attack, allergic-anaphylactic shock. If any of such symptoms are observed, ask the patient if s/he has been exposed to any allergenic substance recently. Generally, the patient or her/his relatives knows/know and indicates/indicate the allergenic substances. They usually state that such symptoms are observed after the patient has contacted with the allergenic substances or taken them as food. If the patient and her/his relatives does not/do not know the cause of allergy, then begin to search the potential allergenic substances around the patient and in the catering supplies in line with the symptoms.  14.24.2. Food Allergy  The food allergy is an unexpected response of the immune system. The symptoms and findings may be mild or severe. The symptoms may be itch, swollen tongue, vomiting, diarrhea, problematic breathing, or low blood pressure. Food allergy generally emerges within a few minutes to a few hours after the exposure. The symptoms may emerge within a few minutes or a few hours. When the symptoms are severe, it may appear as anaphylactic shock; food intolerance and food poisoning are different conditions. Cow milk, peanut, egg, shellfish, fish, pistachio, soy, wheat, rice, and fruits are some of the foods that cause food allergy. The cure of food allergy is to avoid the foods defined as allergens. The allergens may be taken into body by eating foods that include these allergens, or by handling any surface that might have been in contact with the allergens and then touching the eyes or nose with that hand. For overly sensitive people, avoidance is not to touch or smell the problematic foodstuff.  14.24.3. Allergic Rhinitis (Hay Fever)  An allergic origin condition observed with frequent nasal congestion, sneezing, nasal discharge, eye irritation and pain in forehead. It is generally associated with seasonal allergies. It is frequently encountered with such allergy when pollens of trees, flowers and various plants begin to float in the air. Moreover, it may be encountered with such allergy in over polluted air and when there is any dust, wool, and animal feather or hair around.  14.24.4. Exanthematous Diseases  The most common cause of exanthematous diseases is viral infections that cause skin changes either directly or through the reaction of the immune system. They are the skin redness and symptomatic skin rashes that spread uniformly throughout the body or part of the superficial part of the body, spontaneously occurring immediately and disappearing again without significant skin changes. They are sudden allergic reactions caused by infectious, toxic or food related causes. Diseases that cause skin rashes such as measles, scarlet fever, chicken pox are exanthematous diseases.  14.24.5. First Aid Treatment for Allergy  First aid treatment to be applied to the patient shall be in line with the symptoms and based upon removing allergenic substances away. Main purpose of the first aid treatment shall be especially checking the patient's respiration and keeping the airway open. Ask the patient if s/he has any antiallergic (antihistaminic) medicine(s) with her/him and help her/him while taking her/his medicine(s) if any. Loss of consciousness is observed in patients suffering from anaphylactic shock and they need supportive oxygen together with accessory respiration. Emergency landing is required in such cases and the patient shall be immediately dispatched to emergency department.  14.25. Asthma  Asthma is defined as the sudden spasms developed together with hypersecretion of the bronchioles. Sometimes, the patients have great difficulty while exhaling and accordingly cyanosis may be observed. The patients exert excessive power especially while exhaling due to the obstruction. Such reaction, which allergenic substances cause in airways, is an over-response of normal protective mechanism. Such allergic response may lead to anaphylactic shock characterized by respiratory distress that may lead to coma and death.  First Aid Treatment for Asthma  Put the patient in sitting/half sitting position in order to help her/him to breath more easily. Supply her/him with oxygen. Help her/him to take her/his medicine(s), if any. Remove secretions from the oral cavity if s/he has not developed coma and supply her/him with oxygen. If the patient is in a coma, ensure airway patency. Emergency landing is required if the patient's health condition is getting worse and if there is a risk of coma.
